docs.title: Where the bound is large
docs.text:
The bound is not small for every figure. It holds tightly for time per output token (at most 1.09 against any alternative in any workload swept) and, away from the extremes of concurrency, for throughput. It does not hold for:

  • Median time to first token at 64 to 256 clients, against a policy that reads load. Round-robin is up to 1.55 times least-active-requests for balanced, 1.41 for decode-bound, and 1.47 times default at 64 clients. This is where the pools approach saturation: a router that reads its own counts keeps a short queue where a policy that ignores load does not. A ranking by TTFT p50 in that regime should not rest on the substitution.
  • p99 time to first token for the prefill-bound workload, up to 1.65 against least-active-requests at 64 clients, 1.34 against queue-scorer and default.
  • Throughput of the prefill-bound workload at 16 clients (1.16 against least-active-requests; the load-blind policies and default share the gap, so it is arrival imbalance across four prefill endpoints and 16 clients), and at 1,024 clients for balanced (1.12 against default).

The earlier scoping run's summary (time per output token at most 1.08, throughput at most 1.07, p99 time to first token at most 1.13) holds for balanced to within 0.05 and not for the other two kinds. The table of ratios is the whole statement; a single "at most" would hide the cells above.

docs.title: The prefill-pool check
docs.text:
llm-d's max-score picker draws one counter at every pick of every profile, so a request that picks a prefill endpoint and then a decode endpoint draws two successive values. Read literally, with the candidates in a fixed order, that would give a prefill pool of even size only every other endpoint. The first version of the table mapped no policy for that reason.

The check uses a workload that saturates the prefill pool (prefill-bound), where a pool served through one endpoint would give the one-endpoint rate. In requests per second, round-robin:

Prefill endpoints 16 clients 64 256 1,024 least-active-requests 1 (1P3D) 13.6 13.6 13.6 13.6 13.6 2 (2P3D) 27.0 25.3 26.7 26.8 27.1 to 27.3 4 (4P1D) 46.3 50.2 51.6 53.3 53.6 to 54.4

Two endpoints serve about twice the rate of one; a pool that used one would give 13.6. The prediction was not reproduced. At 1 to 8 clients (alternation.csv, 2P3D) round-robin served 4.66, 9.30, 16.84 and 24.35 requests per second at 1, 2, 4 and 8 clients. TestTheEvidenceDoesNotShowAStarvedPrefillPool pins the comparison.

Why it does not show: in the router tree the entry cites (inference-sim/llm-d-router at 03246be994224ef031dfdafb966c54f60d01e933, and no other release) the hosted scheduler puts the candidates in a seeded random order before each pick (pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler_profile.go 363-370), so the choice among the tied endpoints is random and not a cycle (picker/maxscore/picker.go 108-117), and a pool of even size is used in full. BLIS's Result lists decode endpoints in TargetDistribution and not prefill endpoints, so a prefill pick cannot be read back; recording both pools is a change to the simulator. So this table shows the pool used, and not which endpoint served a request.

One result of the same check is unexplained and not about round-robin. With least-active-requests, two prefill endpoints and 4 clients, two of 500 requests did not complete in seeds 42 and 43 (timed_out, requests 55 and 56 of session users 3 and 2, round 14) and the rate was 12.7 requests per second against 16.8 for round-robin. It is in alternation.csv; runs.csv has no run with a request that did not complete. To reproduce: blis run --scenarios <work>/scn --scenario s_2P3D_least-active-requests.yaml --num-instances 5 --prefill-instances 2 --decode-instances 3 --concurrency 4 --num-requests 500 --seed 42 --prompt-tokens 8192 --prompt-tokens-min 8192 --prompt-tokens-max 8192 --prompt-tokens-stdev 0 --output-tokens 16 --output-tokens-min 16 --output-tokens-max 16 --output-tokens-stdev 0.

docs.title: How a point uses the bound
docs.text:
There is no numeric cutoff. A point whose router resolves to an entry with outcome mapped and that has a bound row whose regime matches the point's (the metric; the workload kind from the run's prompt and output lengths; a concurrency the row lists; the same model, hardware, engine release, fabric and instance layouts; a pool shape the row lists) is G2 router_differs, whatever the ratio. A point whose regime matches no row of the entry's bound stays G5 router_unsupported, with the reason "no bound for this regime" (routertable.Entry.BoundFor applies the rule, outcome regime_not_covered, and a point record that carries a bound whose regime omits the point's client count is refused). The ratios are the sensitivity of BLIS's own figures to the choice of policy, not the error of standing a policy in for the router. The dashboard prints the ratio with the figure and flags bound_wide when any relevant ratio exceeds 1.25. The table and the point record carry the numbers; the rule is applied by the scoring harness, not by this repository.

Which policy each Dynamo mode maps to: round-robin to round-robin (Dynamo rotates strictly per request; llm-d's policy picks at random among tied endpoints, and the random picker is equally close), random to random-picker (llm-d's uniform draw with no counter, picker/random/picker.go, a policy BLIS hosts and the sweep ran), kv to none. For the random entry the first group of ratios is the sensitivity between the random picker and round-robin; for the round-robin entry it is the same pair seen from the other side, so the two are equal, and each entry's second group is against the policies that read load.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: The 720 runs took about 39 minutes of wall-clock time at 4 concurrent processes on a 10-core arm64 Mac that other jobs were also using (load average above 100), one run finished every 3.3 seconds on average (each took about 13 seconds of one process); a 60-run trial of one shape took 191 seconds. Peak memory was not measured. Each run writes a Result of 0.6 to 2 MB that the script deletes after reading six figures from it, so the scratch directory stays small. The committed evidence is runs.csv (98 KB) and alternation.csv (6 KB). Run it with --jobs 3 or fewer on a shared machine.

docs.title: What it does not show
docs.text:
• One model, one part, one engine. MiniMax-M2.5 on GB200 with vLLM 0.32.0 over NIXL. Another model or part moves where the pools saturate, and with it where the large ratios sit.
  • Closed-loop clients, fixed lengths, no shared prefix. Nothing here has sessions of several turns, a spread of lengths, an open-loop arrival rate, or requests that share a prefix. The kv mode of Dynamo exists for shared prefixes, which is why its entry maps no policy.
  • Four concurrencies and four pool shapes. Larger pools and other parallelism, and the points between 16, 64, 256 and 1,024, were not run.
  • A sensitivity, not an error. No run behind Dynamo was compared with BLIS. The ratios say how far BLIS moves when its policy changes.
  • Three seeds. A ratio between two load-blind policies below about 1.10 is inside seed noise.
  • In-sample. The entries' bounds are read from the same runs that motivated the mapping. No held-out set exists for them.

docs.title: Where the data came from
docs.text: Every figure is produced by the simulator named above from the scenario and routers in this directory. No third-party data is used or committed. The Dynamo code the entries cite is read at the commits the entries name, from ai-dynamo/dynamo (Apache-2.0); llm-d's router code is read from inference-sim/llm-d-router at b1ab0ff7c0b84090e40b874f8873e78f2ae6897c (Apache-2.0). Which recipes run which Dynamo mode comes from the dashboard's own reading of the InferenceX recipes, not from this sweep.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
One page per document kind, plus the kernel interface, the engine interface, the router contract, the closed vocabularies, the engine rules interface and the validator commands. Each document page opens with an example, then lists every key the document may contain, then every check its validator makes.

The key tables are tested against the Go types: a key the type declares and the table omits, or a key the table lists and the type does not declare, fails the build. The vocabularies are generated from the code. For anything finer than these pages, read the source; each page links to it.

Page Documents Package Scenario Scenario spec/scenario Deployment Deployment spec/deployment Workload a scenario's workload, a catalog workload shape spec/workload Model graph ModelGraph, a model's identity manifest spec/model Hardware chip, fabric, storage classes spec/hardware Coefficient set CoefficientSet spec/coefficient Acceptance profiles AcceptanceProfileSet, inline acceptance values, a scenario's pin spec/acceptance Routing profiles RoutingProfileSet, a scenario's pin spec/routing Connector registry ConnectorRegistry spec/connector Evaluation run EvaluationRun spec/evaluation Measured run MeasuredRun, the licence registry spec/measurement Result Result spec/result Field list FieldList, an engine release's fields.json spec/fields Kernel interface the Kernel a cost model implements kernel Engine interface the Engine an inference-engine model implements, its Spec envelope and its contract checks engine Router contract the Runtime a simulator implements, and the Router a hosted router implements embed Vocabularies units, methods, scope keys, dtypes, and the rest vocab and spec/ Engine rules the interface an engine release's rules implement rules Command line validate-catalog, validate-registry, validate-measurements validate/cmd

In the key tables, Type is the YAML type. Required means that if the key is absent, the validator reports an error or the loader fails. A key marked no may be omitted, and the table says what omitting it means.

docs.title: Acceptance profiles
docs.text: How far speculative decoding advances a request per verification step. The registry holds measured acceptance lengths with their provenance; a workload, a scenario or the command line may state their own; and a run resolves exactly one of them and records where it came from.

docs.title: The quantity
docs.text:
The canonical value is the mean acceptance length (AL): the tokens a request gains per verification step, counting the target's bonus token. For K speculative tokens it lies in [1, K + 1]. It is what InferenceX's golden curves publish and what the engines take (vLLM synthetic_acceptance_length, SGLang SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN).

Two other quantities are derived from it, and each has one name here:

  • The acceptance rate is the accepted fraction of drafts, (AL − 1) / K. It is vLLM's logged "Avg Draft acceptance rate" and inference-sim's --speculative-acceptance-rate. The two agree only when every step drafts all K: with a drafter that verifies fewer on some steps, such as DSpark under enable_adaptive_verification, vLLM's logged rate (accepted over drafted tokens, vllm/v1/spec_decode/metrics.py:107-110) divides by the drafts actually proposed and diverges from (AL − 1) / K. The per-token probability p of the speculative-decoding papers is a different quantity and is never called a rate in this schema.
  • Per-position rates p1..pK follow vLLM's synthetic_acceptance_rates: pi is the unconditional probability that the first i drafts are all accepted. They are non-increasing, each lies in [0, 1], and they sum to AL − 1.

No source in scope publishes per-position rates, so they are optional everywhere. A consumer that needs a distribution derives one with MinimumVarianceRates, which is vLLM v0.31.0's _acceptance_length_to_rates (vllm/config/speculative.py:557-564):

rates = [1.0] * floor(AL - 1) + [frac(AL - 1)] + [0.0] * rest, truncated to K

This is how vLLM, and the InferenceX runs that force a published AL, realise one, so a simulator using it reproduces those runs. Natural acceptance spreads more than this schedule does, so per-request tails derived from it are optimistic.

Acceptance is not the kernel's input. K and the method stay in the deployment's speculative block, because they change what a step costs; acceptance changes only how far requests advance.

docs.title: Profile set
docs.text:
A registry file under acceptance/, named by its file. This one carries real values from InferenceX's golden SPEED-Bench curves:

kind: AcceptanceProfileSet
name: inferencex-golden-al
caveats:
  - Coding only. Every curve is SPEED-Bench Qualitative coding; other categories have none.
  - Measured on B300. Reuse on another part is recorded by the resolver.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark at K 6-8 was refused by the image, so it has no value.
profiles:
  - model: deepseek-v4.1-flash
    speculative_method: dspark
    num_spec_tokens: 5
    thinking: "off"
    category: coding
    acceptance_length: 4.07
    method: measured
    provenance: &dsv41
      source: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/dsv41flash_dspark.yaml
      run: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34493175056
      benchmark: SPEED-Bench Qualitative
      prompts: 80
      hardware: b300
      engine_image: vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909
      tp: 4
      sampling: {temperature: 1.0, max_tokens: 4096}
      settings:
        draft_sample_method: probabilistic
        rejection_sample_method: block
  - model: deepseek-v4.1-flash
    speculative_method: dspark
    num_spec_tokens: 5
    thinking: "on"
    category: coding
    acceptance_length: 3.51
    method: measured
    provenance: *dsv41
  - model: glm-5.3
    speculative_method: mtp
    num_spec_tokens: 3
    thinking: "on"
    category: coding
    acceptance_length: 2.99
    method: transferred
    transferred_from: glm-5.2-fp8/mtp/k3/thinking-on/coding
    transfer_rule: the value measured on GLM-5.2 is carried unchanged, because GLM-5.3 shares its base and layer topology
    rationale: >
      Provisional. GLM-5.3 shares GLM-5.2's base and layer topology, so GLM-5.2's curve is
      the closest measured reference; replace it with a run on GLM-5.3.
    provenance:
      source: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/glm5.3_mtp.yaml
      run: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/28058352479
      hardware: b300
      sampling: {temperature: 1.0, top_p: 0.95, max_tokens: 4096}
Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always AcceptanceProfileSet. name string yes The set's identity. By convention it equals the file name, which is what a scenario's acceptance.profiles uses. caveats list of strings no What the set does not cover and how far its values travel. No entry may be empty. profiles list yes At least one profile, below.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
A profile is keyed by model, drafter, speculative method, K, thinking mode and workload category. Two profiles with one key are an error. The drafter is the model's own in-graph speculator when it is left out, or the catalog name of a separate drafter checkpoint; the same target with two drafters has two profiles.

Key Type Required Meaning model string yes The catalog model name, not the source's spelling of it. drafter string no The catalog name of the separate drafter checkpoint the value was measured with. Left out for the model's own speculator, such as its MTP layers. No +, / or space, and not the target's own name. architecture string no The target's architecture as its graph records it (global.architecture). A lookup that borrows from another target reads it; a profile that states none is never borrowed across targets. It must equal the graph's. speculative_method string yes The engine's method name, as a deployment's engine.speculative.method states it. num_spec_tokens integer yes K. At least 1. thinking string yes on or off. One of the thinking modes. category string yes The workload category, such as coding. Lower-case letters, digits, _ and -. acceptance_length number yes AL, in [1, K + 1]. per_position_rates list of numbers no K rates, each in [0, 1], non-increasing, summing to AL − 1 within 0.01. method string yes How the value was obtained. One of the methods except not_charged. provenance mapping unless method is assumed Where it was measured, below. rationale string unless method is measured The reasoning behind a value that was not measured. transferred_from string with method transferred The profile it was measured as, as model/method/k<K>/thinking-<mode>/category. transfer_rule string with method transferred The stated rule that moved the value to this profile's model.

docs.title: provenance
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning source string yes The document the value was read from. run string no The job that measured it, such as a GitHub Actions run. benchmark string no The prompt set, such as SPEED-Bench Qualitative. prompts integer no How many prompts it covered. Not negative. hardware string with method measured The catalog chip it was measured on. A resolution on other hardware records this. date string no The day the source was published or measured, YYYY-MM-DD. A lookup that borrows breaks a tie by the newest source; a profile with no date is older than any dated one. engine_image string with method measured The engine image or release that ran. tp integer no The tensor-parallel width it ran at. Not negative. sampling mapping with method measured The decoding configuration, below. settings mapping no Other engine settings that bear on acceptance, by name, such as rejection_sample_method.

docs.title: provenance.sampling
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning temperature number yes Not negative. 0 is greedy decoding. top_p number no In (0, 1]. top_k integer no At least −1; −1 and 0 disable it. max_tokens integer no Output cap. Not negative.

docs.title: Inline values
docs.text:
A workload's acceptance, a scenario's acceptance.value, and the value a command line supplies all take this form. A value names the K it was stated for; at a deployment that speculates another K it is refused rather than rescaled.

Key Type Required Meaning num_spec_tokens integer yes The K the value was stated for. At least 1. acceptance_length number one of three AL, in [1, K + 1]. acceptance_rate number one of three (AL − 1) / K, in [0, 1]. Not with acceptance_length. per_position_rates list of numbers one of three K rates, as for a profile. Alone, they state AL as 1 + their sum; with either of the others, they must agree with it. source string no Where the value came from, recorded with the resolution.

docs.title: Scenario pin
docs.text:
The value of a scenario's acceptance key.

acceptance:
  value:
    num_spec_tokens: 3
    acceptance_length: 2.8
    source: synthetic_acceptance_length in the scored run's server log

To use another profile set for the run, and to accept coding's curve for traffic that has none of its own:

acceptance:
  profiles: inferencex-golden-al
  fallback_category: coding
Key Type Required Meaning profiles string no An acceptance-profile set under acceptance/ in the registry, consulted in place of the default. Not with value. value mapping no An inline value, above. fallback_category string no The category to use when the workload's has no curve. The substitution is recorded. A fallback given on the command line outranks this one. Not with value. exact_only boolean no Limits the profile lookup to a measured profile with the run's exact key; it never borrows. Not with value.

A pin must set at least one key.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
acceptance.Resolve takes the run's model, method and K, the registry sets, the workload's terms, the scenario's pin and the command line's value, and returns the acceptance length, the per-position rates, and which layer supplied them. The highest layer that states acceptance wins; layers are not merged.

Layer Supplies acceptance by registry the profile matching (model, drafter, method, K, the workload's thinking mode and category) in the registry sets, the default; the closest one when none matches exactly (below) workload the workload's own acceptance value scenario the pin's value, or the matching profile in the set its profiles names cli the command line's value, such as --speculative-acceptance-rate at the deployment's K

registry · workload · scenario · cli

docs.title: Borrowing
docs.text:
A value stated on the command line, in the scenario or by the workload is used as stated. A profile lookup that finds no measured profile with the run's exact key borrows the closest one, in this order (design D8), and records that it did:

  1. The same target and drafter at another K. Between two measured values of K it interpolates linearly. Above the largest it takes the largest's value. Below the smallest it takes that profile's stated per-position rates for the first K positions; a profile that states none gives 1 + K(AL − 1)/K₀, where K₀ is its K. That figure cannot exceed what the profile's own rates would give, so it does not overstate drafting's gain. The lookup never extrapolates.
  2. Another drafter of the same target, preferring the same method and then the lowest value at the run's K, found by the first step's rules, so that drafting's gain is not overstated. The drafter must differ from the run's: the same drafter under another method is not another drafter, no step takes it, and the lookup refuses it.
  3. The same method on another target whose graph records the same architecture. The profile must state its architecture, and the run's must be known.

Every step keeps the category and the thinking mode, apart from a fallback category the user requested. The fallback category stands in only when the workload's own category supplies nothing: the lookup tries the exact key and all three steps in the workload's category first, and only then repeats them in the fallback category. Any remaining tie breaks in this order: the profile measured on the run's hardware, then the newest source (provenance.date), then the set name, then the key, so the choice is deterministic whatever order the sets are listed in. Two profiles that share a key but record different sampling or settings are not interchangeable, and an exact key found in two sets is ambiguous; the lookup refuses both. A scenario's exact_only, or the request's, limits the lookup to exact matches.

The resolution records step (exact, same_drafter_other_k, other_drafter or other_target), the key fields that differed, how K was brought to the run's (k_rule), and every profile read. The Result carries the same record on its speculative_acceptance property.

Nothing else falls back silently. A lookup is refused when

  • the workload states no thinking mode, or no category and no fallback was requested;
  • no profile matches on any step, and no fallback_category was requested, or the fallback has no profile either;
  • two registry sets both match an exact key, or share a key measured under different sampling or settings;
  • the scenario names a set that was not supplied. The registry is not consulted in its place.

A value stated for a K other than the deployment's is refused at every layer. The resolution also records the profile set and entry, the cited source, the category a fallback replaced, the hardware a profile was measured on when it differs from the run's, and whether the rates were derived.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A profile set is invalid if

  • kind is not AcceptanceProfileSet, name is empty, there are no profiles, or a caveat is empty;
  • two profiles share a key;
  • a profile has no model or speculative_method, thinking is not on or off, or category is malformed;
  • a drafter is the target's own name or contains +, / or a space, or an architecture contains a space or /;
  • num_spec_tokens is less than 1, or acceptance_length is not finite or lies outside [1, K + 1];
  • per_position_rates has other than K entries, an entry outside [0, 1], rises, or sums more than 0.01 from AL − 1;
  • method is not recognized or is not_charged, or a field the method requires, per the table above, is missing;
  • a provenance has no source, a negative count, an empty setting, or sampling with no temperature, a negative one, a top_p outside (0, 1] or a top_k below −1.

An inline value is invalid if num_spec_tokens is less than 1, it states no acceptance, it states both acceptance_length and acceptance_rate, either lies outside its range, or its rates are invalid or disagree with it. A pin is invalid if it sets nothing, sets both profiles and value, sets fallback_category or exact_only with value, or its value is invalid.

With a deployment in the bundle, every inline value (the scenario's pin, its trace's, its replay's, merged with its catalog entry when the bundle carries one, a catalog replay's, and the workload shape's) must name the K of each pool that speculates. When no pool speculates, a stated value draws a warning.

Source: spec/acceptance.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
One command for the catalog, one for the registry, and one for measured runs before they are committed. Each validates every document under the path it is given and exits with a code a CI step can read.

From the root of a blis-substrate checkout:

go run ./validate/cmd/validate-catalog      <catalog dir>
go run ./validate/cmd/validate-registry     <registry dir>
go run ./validate/cmd/validate-measurements [-local] <measurements dir>

The repository's own data is catalog, registry and catalog/measurements. Any directory with the same layout may be given instead.

Both write every problem to standard error. validate-catalog writes to standard output a heading for each kind of file and one line for each artifact that validates: each file, or each storage class in devices/storage.yaml. validate-registry writes one line per set to standard output, FAILED for a set that does not validate. Each ends with a summary line: all N ... validate on standard output, or N of M ... failed on standard error. Warnings are printed and do not fail the run. Both run the field layer only: these documents name no engine version, so no rules pack applies.

docs.title: validate-catalog
docs.text:
Path Validated as models/*/graph.yaml a model graph, whose name must equal the directory. A model directory without one is skipped. models/*/config.json required in every model directory; must be a non-empty JSON object. models/*/model.yaml required in every model directory; a model identity, whose name must equal the directory. hardware/*.yaml a chip networks/*.yaml a fabric devices/storage.yaml storage classes. Optional. workloads/*.yaml a workload shape, or a replay workload when its top-level key is replay: measurements/ as validate-measurements does, without -local. Optional.

Only files ending in .yaml are read in the flat directories. A path is treated as a catalog if it contains at least one of models/, hardware/, networks/, workloads/, devices/ and measurements/.

docs.title: validate-registry
docs.text:
Every file under coefficients/ whose extension is .yaml or .yml, in any letter case and at any depth, is validated as a coefficient set. Symbolic links to directories are not followed. A scenario can refer only to a set at the top level of coefficients/ with a .yaml extension, by its file name; a set elsewhere validates but cannot be named.

Files under acceptance/, found the same way, are validated as acceptance-profile sets, each reported as acceptance/<file>. Files under routing/ are validated as routing-profile sets, each reported as routing/<file>. Both directories are optional.

docs.title: validate-measurements
docs.text:
sources.yaml is validated as the licence registry, and every <license_ref>/*.yaml as a measured run against it. A run's name must equal its file name, its license_ref its directory, and its stated verdict the computed one. duplicate_of and supersedes must name another run in the directory. A YAML file at the top level other than sources.yaml fails. Without -local, every run's licence must permit redistribute; with it, scoring alone suffices, for output that stays out of the repository.

It writes one line per file to standard output, the verdict for a run, and exits 0 when every file validates, 1 when any fails, and 2 on wrong arguments or a path that is not a directory.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code validate-catalog validate-registry 0 every artifact validated every set validated 1 an artifact failed to load or validate a coefficient or acceptance set failed to load or validate 2 wrong arguments; the root does not exist; none of the six directories is present; or nothing was found to validate wrong arguments; the root does not exist; coefficients/ could not be read; or it holds no coefficient sets

Source: validate/cmd/validate-catalog, validate/cmd/validate-registry, validate/cmd/validate-measurements.

docs.title: Coefficient set
docs.text:
A set of coefficients for a cost model. Each entry records its value and unit, how it was obtained, the evidence for it, and the hardware and layouts over which it holds. The registry owns the sets; every consumer loads them through this schema.

The set below is illustrative; its values are not real coefficients. The registry's sets are in coefficients/.

kind: CoefficientSet
name: example-set
coefficients:
  - gemm_eps_max_bf16:
      value: 0.78
      units: dimensionless
      method: measured
      fitted: true
      ci95: [0.74, 0.81]
      scope: {hardware: [h100]}
  - gemm_eps_max_bf16:
      value: 0.81
      units: dimensionless
      method: measured
      fitted: true
      scope: {hardware: [h200]}
  - mfu_prefill:
      value: 0.32
      units: dimensionless
      method: literature
      fitted: false
      sources:
        - {kind: discussion, cite: "inference-sim#589", role: primary}
      rationale: >
        L40S prefill MFU discount; see the cited discussion.
      scope: {hardware: [l40s]}
  - pd_transfer_base_latency:
      value: 50
      units: us_per_transfer
      method: assumed
      fitted: false
      rationale: >
        A placeholder until a measurement exists.
      scope: {hardware: [h100, h200]}

Each entry in coefficients is a map with a single key, the entry's name. A name key inside an entry is accepted and replaced by that map key. A set is complete in itself: it does not inherit from another set. A scenario may still name several sets, and how a cost model combines them is described under Selecting an entry.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always CoefficientSet. name string yes The set's identity. By convention, not checked, it equals the file name, which is what a scenario's coefficients uses. coefficients list yes At least one entry, each - <entry name>: {...}.

docs.title: Entries
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning value number unless method is not_charged The coefficient. Zero exactly when method is not_charged. units string yes One of the units. method string yes How the value was obtained. One of the methods. fitted boolean yes Whether the value comes from fitting a curve. Must be present even when false. scope mapping yes Where the value holds, below. At least one dimension. rate_basis string no What a bytes_per_us rate measures: memory (the default) or work. A memory rate cannot exceed the chip's datasheet memory bandwidth (SUB-5). A work rate counts bytes of work, such as a record counted once per query and key pair, and may exceed it; it requires a rationale. One of the rate bases. kernel_impls list no The kernel implementations the value is valid for (below): the lookup key. A lookup matches the entry only when one of them is what runs. Allowed on measured, calibrated, transferred and literature; not on vendor_spec, roofline, assumed or not_charged. measured_on list on transferred that states kernel_impls The kernel implementations a transferred value was measured on, same form as kernel_impls. Evidence only; a lookup never matches it. Only on transferred. measures mapping no What the number includes (below). Only on measured and calibrated. fit_range list no The range of inputs the fit's data covered (below). Only on measured, calibrated and transferred (the rows a transferred value came from). A price that reads the entry outside it is extrapolated and ranks with transferred. ci95 [low, high] no 95% confidence interval. Must contain value. sources list depends on method Citations, below. If present, not empty. rationale string depends on method The reasoning behind a value that was not measured. transferred_from string with method transferred The scope the value was measured in, as the scope renders, such as hardware=h200,model=deepseek-v4.1-flash. transfer_rule string with method transferred The stated rule that moved the value to this scope. supersedes string no An entry this one replaces. validated string or list no Names of metrics the value has been checked against, such as itl. Free text. unsupported string or list no Names of metrics it has been found not to hold for. Free text.

docs.title: scope
docs.text:
Each dimension lists the values the coefficient holds for. An empty scope is not "everywhere"; it means the range is unknown, and it is rejected.

Key Type Required Meaning hardware list of strings no Chips. model list of strings no Models. tp list of integers no Tensor-parallel widths. ep list of integers no Expert-parallel widths. nodes_spanned list of integers no How many nodes a collective crosses. fabric list of strings no Inter-node interconnect classes, by catalog identity: the stem of a fabric under networks/, such as roce-200g or ib-400g. nodes_spanned says whether a collective leaves a node; fabric says over which link. A link inside one chip's NVLink domain, a whole NVL72 rack included, belongs to the chip and is scoped by hardware. Each name must be a bare identity, not empty, not a path, and listed once.

Dtype and backend are not scope dimensions. Both are part of the entry's name, as in gemm_eps_max_bf16.

docs.title: sources
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes One of the source kinds. cite string yes The reference: an issue, a paper, a datasheet URL. role string yes One of the source roles.

docs.title: kernel_impls
docs.text:
An implementation is one exact kernel: a library, the library's own name for the kernel, and the hash of its source. The lookup (design D5, VAL-8) matches an entry that lists implementations only for the primitive its name prices (the GEMMs, the decode attention, a collective; host overheads and other terms that price no lowered kernel cannot be keyed), and only when every implementation the pool runs for that primitive is one the entry lists, with library, variant and code hash all equal. A different hash of the same kernel does not match, and neither does the same hash of another kernel: there is no fallback to a sibling. What the lookup does then is the next entry by method rank (design 9.2), at worst the family's roofline or assumed entry, which state no implementation; the price reports that method.

  • An entry that lists none is unkeyed: it applies to whatever runs, and nothing shows it was measured on the kernel that runs. It prices as it always did, and a reader deciding whether a price rests on the running kernel (the G1 hash condition, design 11.3) does not count it.
  • With no implementation stated for the primitive, only unkeyed entries match.
  • The two lists of an entry say different things. kernel_impls is where the value is valid and is the key. measured_on is where its data came from. For measured and calibrated they are the same by D5, so only kernel_impls is stated. A transferred value is measured on one kernel and used for another: it states the target in kernel_impls, the source in measured_on, and the rule in transfer_rule. The same kernel on both is a transfer between chips.
  • Two entries of one name, scope and method that differ only in kernel_impls are two coefficients: a kernel whose source changed has its own value.
Key Type Required Meaning library string yes The library that runs the kernel. variant string yes The library's own exported kernel name. code_hash string yes The hash of the kernel's source and target GPU architecture, or of a binary library: lower-case hexadecimal, at least 12 digits.

docs.title: measures
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning time string yes One of the measurement times: device, or device_and_host. execution string yes One of the measurement executions: captured or eager. harness string yes The harness that collected the data, with its pin.

docs.title: fit_range
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning dim string yes The input dimension, such as tokens or ranks. Listed once. low number yes The smallest value the fit's data took. high number yes The largest value the fit's data took. Not below low.

An interval ci95 that is unbounded, or wider than half the value, marks the entry unidentified: its data do not determine it, and a price that used it ranks with assumed.

docs.title: Identity is name and scope
docs.text: Two entries may share a name if their scopes differ. The set above has two gemm_eps_max_bf16 entries, one for H100 and one for H200. Two entries with the same name and the same scope are an error, because a cost model would use whichever came last. Scopes are compared without regard to order: [h100, h200] and [h200, h100] are the same scope.

docs.title: Selecting an entry
docs.text: The schema defines what an entry says. Choosing among entries is the cost model's job, and the cost model in kernel/ does it as follows. An entry applies to a deployment if, for every dimension its scope states, the list includes the deployment's value; hardware, model and fabric names are compared without regard to case, and a dimension the scope omits does not constrain it. The kernel reads the scenario's sets in order and, within each set, its entries in order, and the last applicable entry for each name is the one it uses. A later set can therefore override part of an earlier one. Entries that do not apply are skipped. Construction fails if no entry applies at all, or if the cost model needs a coefficient no applicable entry supplies.

docs.title: What a method requires
docs.text: Method rationale sources Other measured — — Allows fitted: true. A source is expected but not required. calibrated required at least one of kind measured_case Allows fitted: true. validated must name the held-out metrics. literature required at least one vendor_spec required at least one transferred required — transferred_from and transfer_rule required. roofline required at least one, naming the catalog facts it was computed from assumed required — not_charged required — value must be 0.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A set fails to load if an entry is not a single-key map, an entry has no fitted key, sources is present but empty, ci95 is not a two-element list, validated or unsupported is neither a string nor a list of strings, or any mapping has a key its type does not declare.

A loaded set is invalid if

  • kind is not CoefficientSet, name is empty, or there are no entries;
  • an entry has no name, or repeats another entry's name and scope;
  • value is not finite, units or method is not recognized, or scope is empty;
  • value is 0 with a method other than not_charged, or nonzero with not_charged;
  • fitted is true with a method other than measured or calibrated;
  • a companion field the method requires, per the table above, is missing;
  • a source has an unrecognized kind or role, or an empty cite;
  • ci95 has a non-finite end, has low above high, or does not contain value.

Source: spec/coefficient.

docs.title: Connector registry
docs.text:
Which KV-connector names a deployment may use, which engine interface each implements, and which engine model reproduces its behaviour. A deployment's `offload.connector` and `pd_transfer.connector` are looked up here rather than in a list compiled into a simulator, so a connector that behaves like an existing one is data, not code.

# A KV-connector registry. The built-in entries for vLLM live in blis-vllm; this example
# shows the shape with two of them.
kind: ConnectorRegistry
name: example
connectors:
  OffloadingConnector:
    upstream: KVConnectorBase_V1
    behaves_like: offloading
    roles: [offload]
    evidence: diff-test @ vLLM v0.32.0
  NixlConnector:
    upstream: KVConnectorBase_V1
    behaves_like: nixl-pull
    roles: [pd_transfer]
    evidence: diff-test @ vLLM v0.32.0

An entry earns behaves_like only by evidence. Implementing an engine's connector interface is not the same as behaving like one of its connectors, so a vendor connector is registered only once it passes the differential tests the engine module runs against the engine release; until then it is unsupported. This page describes the shape. The entries for vLLM live with the engine model, in blis-vllm.

Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always ConnectorRegistry. name string yes The registry's identity. connectors mapping yes At least one entry, by connector name exactly as the engine registers it (vLLM's KVConnectorFactory.register_connector). Key Type Required Meaning upstream string yes The engine interface the connector implements, as the engine names it. Which interfaces exist is the engine module's to check. behaves_like string yes The engine model that reproduces the connector's behaviour, in the engine module that owns the registry. roles list yes What a deployment may use it for: offload, pd_transfer, composite. Each at most once. evidence string yes How the entry earned behaves_like, such as diff-test @ vLLM v0.32.0.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A registry is invalid if kind is not ConnectorRegistry, name is empty, it has no connectors, a connector name is blank or has surrounding spaces (names match the engine's exactly), or an entry omits upstream, behaves_like or evidence, has no roles, or lists an unknown or repeated role.

Source: spec/connector.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The choices made against a scenario: how its cluster is divided into pools, each pool's parallel layout and engine settings, the KV offload tiers, and how KV moves from prefill to decode. A deployment is validated with its scenario, because most of what makes a layout feasible depends on the cluster.

kind: Deployment
name: 1p3d-ep8
pools:
  - role: prefill
    nodes: 1
    parallel:
      tp: 1
      pp: 1
      dp: 8
      dp_local: 8
      enable_expert_parallel: true
    engine:
      all2all_backend: deepep_high_throughput
      max_num_batched_tokens: 16384
  - role: decode
    nodes: 3
    parallel:
      tp: 1
      pp: 1
      dp: 8
      dp_local: 8
      enable_expert_parallel: true
    engine:
      all2all_backend: deepep_low_latency
      max_num_seqs: 512
offload:
  tiers:
    - tier: cpu_dram
      bytes: 549755813888
pd_transfer:
  connector: NixlConnector

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always Deployment. name string yes The deployment's identity. pools list yes At least one pool, below. offload mapping no KV offload tiers below HBM. pd_transfer mapping if any pool is prefill How KV moves from prefill to decode. router mapping no The inputs of the llm-d router that routes the deployment's requests. Absent: the router's built-in configuration over every pod.

docs.title: Pools
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning role string yes colocated, prefill or decode. nodes integer yes Nodes in the pool, at least 1. parallel mapping yes The parallel layout of each engine in the pool. engine mapping no The engine's settings for the pool, held unopened; the engine model opens and checks it. See below. labels mapping no Kubernetes labels on the pool's model-server pods, as its pod template sets them. The router selects and filters endpoints by them. llm-d.ai/role is derived from role (colocated -> prefill-decode, prefill -> prefill, decode -> decode); given here, it must have that value.

A pool may run several engines with the same layout and settings. Its nodes is the pool's whole extent; one engine may occupy only part of it.

Pools of role prefill and decode come together or not at all, and neither may appear beside a colocated pool.

docs.title: parallel
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning tp integer yes Tensor-parallel width, at least 1. pp integer yes Pipeline-parallel width, at least 1. dp integer yes Data-parallel width, at least 1. dp_local integer no Data-parallel replicas resident on one node. Must divide gpus_per_node and not exceed dp. Zero means the launch decides. data_parallel_load_balancing string no How the data-parallel ranks are exposed, which decides what a router chooses between. One of the load-balancing modes. Omitted, internal. hybrid and external need dp > 1. The rules pack refuses external on a model without experts and hybrid without dp_local, and names the mode that runs when the engine resolves hybrid to another. --api-server-count is not part of it: it sets how many frontend processes share an endpoint, not which ranks a router can reach. pcp integer no Prefill-context-parallel width. Zero or 1 means off. dcp integer no Decode-context-parallel width. Reuses the tensor-parallel ranks; see below. Zero or 1 means off. enable_expert_parallel boolean no Shard MoE experts across ranks. Default false.

There is no key for the expert-parallel width. It is derived: tp × pcp × dp when expert parallelism is enabled, and 1 otherwise. A key for it would let a document state a width no engine would build. Parallel layouts explains this and the checks below in more depth.

docs.title: engine
docs.text: A pool's engine block is the engine's own settings, and this schema holds it unopened: it loads the block as written and passes it through unchanged. The engine model that a scenario's engine_version selects opens it, and its rules check it. A validator passes those rules in (Bundle.Rules), and they report a problem in the block at its path below deployment.pools[i].engine. For vLLM the keys, their defaults and their checks are blis-vllm's (rules/engineconfig, documented in blis-vllm's engine-configuration reference).

docs.title: Offload
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning tiers list yes At least one tier, below. eviction_policy string no KV offload cache policy. Omitted means lru. prefetch_depth integer no How many steps ahead a fetch is issued. connector string no The KV connector that implements offload. spec string no The offloading spec, such as CPUOffloadingSpec. connector_options mapping no The connector's own options, held unopened for the engine model; see below.

docs.title: offload.connector_options
docs.text: The offload connector's own options. This schema holds them unopened, as it does a pool's engine block, and the engine model's rules check them (Bundle.Rules). A problem in them is reported at its path below deployment.offload.connector_options.

docs.title: offload.tiers
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning tier string yes The storage class this tier uses. If the scenario's cluster lists storage, it must be one of those. bytes integer yes Capacity of the tier in bytes, at least 1.

docs.title: PD transfer
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning connector string no The KV connector that moves KV from prefill to decode.

There is no bandwidth key. Transfer bandwidth comes from the scenario's fabric and a registry coefficient, so it cannot be set here.

docs.title: router
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning epp_flags list no The router's (EPP's) command-line flags, verbatim, one list entry per flag (--name=value). They select the pool with --pool-name or --endpoint-selector. A Helm chart's epp.flags map is rendered to this list (name: value becomes --name=value). endpoint_picker_config string no The EndpointPickerConfig file, as the router reads it with --config-file; a blank path is an error. Naming the configuration here and in epp_flags is an error. manifests list no Kubernetes manifest files. The router reads their InferencePool, InferenceObjective and InferenceModelRewrite objects; other kinds are ignored. Objectives and rewrites take effect only for an InferencePool (--pool-name); with a standalone pool (--endpoint-selector) the router does not reconcile them, so a consumer may refuse them there.

Paths are relative to the directory of the file that holds the deployment. The block names the router's own inputs and nothing else: scorers, weights, admission and flow control are configured in those files, exactly as for a real deployment, so the same files configure the real router and a simulated one. There is no deployment key for a routing decision. The router here is the Endpoint Picker. The multimodal Coordinator pipeline is a separate llm-d component and is not named by this block; a simulator that cannot host it refuses it at startup.

These checks are syntactic. A deployment that passes them is well formed, not necessarily routable by a given consumer: a simulator refuses, at its startup and with the reason, router flags, plugins or manifests it cannot run faithfully.

pools[].labels are a different kind of input from the three above. In a real deployment the labels live in each pool's pod template; a deployment here has no pod spec, so the labels restate them, so that an InferencePool selector or a label filter has the pods' labels to match.

docs.title: On its own
docs.text:
A deployment is invalid if

  • kind is not Deployment, name is empty, or pools is empty;
  • a pool's role is not recognized, or its nodes is less than 1;
  • tp, pp or dp is less than 1, pcp or dcp is negative, dp_local is negative, or dp_local exceeds dp;
  • dcp does not partition the group it reuses. With pcp at most 1, tp must be divisible by dcp. With pcp above 1, dcp must be 1, pcp or tp × pcp;
  • a prefill pool has no decode pool, a decode pool has no prefill pool, or a colocated pool appears beside either;
  • a prefill pool is present and pd_transfer is absent;
  • offload is present with no tiers, a tier is unnamed or named twice, a tier's bytes is below 1, or prefetch_depth is negative;

It draws a warning if expert parallelism is enabled but the derived width is 1. The checks of a pool's engine block are its engine model's.

docs.title: Against its scenario's cluster
docs.text:
These run when the bundle holds both documents. A deployment without its scenario is itself reported, because these checks would otherwise be skipped.

  • The pools' nodes must sum to the cluster's nodes. A deployment lays out the whole cluster.
  • A pool's dp_local, when set, must divide gpus_per_node.
  • An engine needs one GPU per rank, pp × tp × pcp × dp in all, and they must fit in the pool's nodes. Decode-context and expert parallelism add no ranks.
  • With dp_local set, the local replicas must fit on one node in the way the engine places them. The check refuses only layouts that no launch could place. In the rare case that its bounded search cannot decide, it reports a warning that the layout's fit is unverified.
  • Each offload tier must be one of the cluster's storage classes, if the cluster lists any.

Engine-release checks, such as whether a backend name exists or whether prefill-context parallelism may be combined with data parallelism, are in the rules pack.

Source: spec/deployment.

docs.title: Router contract
docs.text:
Package embed is the interface between a simulator that hosts a request router and the router it hosts. The simulator implements Runtime; the router implements Constructor, Router and Flight. The llm-d router fork is the implementation in use, and inference-sim hosts it.

The boundary is ownership. The host owns simulated time, background work and randomness, the endpoints' lifecycle, and what each engine publishes. The router owns every routing decision and the meaning of its configuration. Router configuration (scorers, weights, profiles) never appears in the contract: it travels as the deployment's own bytes in Config, and what the host needs to know about it comes back as facts in Requirements.

A router is a deterministic function of its Config, the Runtime it runs on and the sequence of calls the host makes. It reads time, starts concurrent work, blocks, draws randomness and reaches the network only through the Runtime.

The package uses the standard library only. A test enforces that rule.

docs.title: Host side
docs.text:
Method Does Now() time.Time The current time. NewTimer(d) Timer, NewTicker(d) Ticker Timers and tickers on the runtime clock. Go(fn) Runs fn concurrently. The runtime may run it until it finishes or parks before returning. Every(ctx, name, interval, fn) Calls fn every interval until ctx is done. WithTimeout, WithDeadlineCause The context functions on the runtime clock. Park(ready) Called by a router goroutine before it blocks; it blocks only while ready() is false. Rand(stream) Rand A named random stream. Local(key, init) any State the router would otherwise keep process-wide.

RoundTripper is an optional capability, found by type assertion, for a runtime that serves the router's outbound HTTP (engine metrics, prompt rendering).

docs.title: Router side
docs.text:
Method Does Constructor(ctx, rt, cfg) (Router, error) Builds a router with no endpoints. Neither it nor work it starts calls Rand before it returns, because the host derives the stream scope from the constructed router. If it fails, it has already stopped what it started. A refused plugin type wraps a *RefusalError. Config.Allow(pluginType) (bool, string) The host's plugin policy. A type the router cannot host for a stated reason is refused with that reason; otherwise Allow decides; a type the router has not audited is refused even when Allow permits it. Config.Logger *slog.Logger Receives the router's logs; nil discards them. Config.Check(Requirements, Pool) error The host's own check, which the router calls after parsing the configuration and before it builds any plugin. A failure is returned unwrapped. Requirements() Facts about the configuration, known from the parsed configuration before any plugin exists: metric flags, inert flags, metrics extractors and sources, KV-event indexes, topology labels, whether it disaggregates. Pool() The pool served. Pool.ID() renders it as Kind.group namespace/name. FlowControl() Whether flow control is on, the longest bounded queue-wait budget and the expiry sweep. IdleSkippable() Whether the host may skip background ticks over an idle period. SetEndpoint, RemoveEndpoint The endpoints and their readiness. Route(ctx, req, done) One routing decision. done receives a Flight and a Decision, or a Rejection, exactly once. WantsKVEvents, IngestKVEvents, ClearKVEvents Engines' KV events, in vLLM's vocabulary (BlockStored, BlockRemoved, AllBlocksCleared). A batch names the engine that published it in KVBatch.Engine, vllm or sglang; unset means vllm, and a router refuses any other value instead of decoding it as vLLM's. Stop() Ends every loop and goroutine the router started.

KVIndexInspector is an optional capability, found by type assertion, for a router that can report its KV-event index per endpoint and tier (KVBlocks). It serves conformance and fidelity tests; a host does not depend on it in production.

BlockStored also carries, all optional and absent at their zero value, the adapter (LoRAID, LoRAName), what else entered each block's hash (ExtraKeys, CacheSalt) and the KV-cache group (GroupIdx, SpecKind, SlidingWindow); BlockRemoved carries GroupIdx. Each field's comment names the engine that emits it. AllBlocksCleared{Tier} drops one tier's blocks, or every tier's when Tier is empty.

A Flight is a dispatched request. The host hands it the response headers (ResponseHeaders, which returns the headers after the router's handling) and the body (ResponseBody), then ends it once: with the last body chunk, or with Terminate (client-disconnect, evicted, error). EvictionSignal is closed when the router revokes the request. It is nil when the router never evicts.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text:
A Request is what a client sends; the router renders its request headers from it, in sorted key order. :method is POST, :path is Path, content-type is application/json, and x-request-id is ID, always. The others are sent only when the field is set:

Field Header Rendering Objective x-llm-d-inference-objective verbatim FairnessID x-llm-d-inference-fairness-id verbatim TTFTSLO x-llm-d-slo-ttft-ms whole milliseconds, rounded up, when positive TTL x-llm-d-inference-ttl time.Duration.String, when positive; a flow-controlled request's queue-wait budget is the shorter of it and the configured one

docs.title: Rejections
docs.text: RejectKind Meaning no-endpoints No endpoint could serve the request. ttl-expired It waited in flow control past its queue-wait budget. saturated Flow control's queues were at capacity. context-cancelled The client gave up while the router held it. admission An admission check refused it. unavailable The router could not serve it and gave no more specific reason. unclassified Any other outcome. A host treats it as a defect, not as load shedding.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text: embed/embedtest checks a Constructor against the contract, as testing/fstest checks an fs.FS. It drives the router through a fixed scenario on a deterministic Runtime that it provides, and it plays the engines. A Suite supplies one router configuration per behaviour: plain routing, flow control that holds requests, KV-event routing, and optionally eviction and an always-unavailable configuration. It also names a plugin type to refuse. A router passes embedtest.Run(t, suite) when every part behaves as this page describes.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Runtime, Router and Flight are implemented in other repositories, so none of them gains a method within a major version. A new capability is a separate interface. Struct types may gain fields in a minor version; their zero value keeps the earlier meaning. A new RejectKind or Termination value is a minor change, and a host maps a kind it does not know as it maps unclassified.

docs.title: Engine interface
docs.text:
engine.Engine is the interface an inference-engine model implements and a discrete-event simulator calls: the counterpart of the kernel interface for scheduling rather than pricing. One value is one engine instance, the state machine behind one server process.

The boundary follows from who owns time. The simulator owns the clock, the event queue and the decision of when to step. The engine owns every scheduling, KV-cache and connector decision, and the metrics those decisions produce. An engine reads no clock and schedules no event: every call carries the simulated instant as a value (engine.Time, microseconds), and where an engine rule makes work wait until a later instant, the engine reports that instant through NextWake.

Nothing in the package names an engine. Configuration reaches an engine as an opaque engine.Spec that the simulator hands over unread, so a second engine implements the interface in its own repository with no change here or in the simulator.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Does Add(r Request, now Time) error Hands over a request that arrived at now. Schedules nothing. Schedule(now Time) (Batch, error) Decides one batch: which requests run, how many tokens each, which are preempted, which KV transfers start. ErrNoCapacity when InFlightLimit batches are in flight. StepTime(b Batch) Duration Prices the forward pass of a batch that runs requests; at least one microsecond. An Empty batch is not priced. Complete(id BatchID, outcome Outcome, end Time) (Result, error) Applies a batch's outcome (tokens sampled, drafts accepted) and returns what became visible: tokens emitted, first tokens, finishes, KV events. TransferDone(id TransferID, ok bool, now Time) error Reports that an asynchronous KV load or store finished, successfully or not. Finish(id string, why FinishReason, now Time) error Ends a request for a reason the engine did not decide (client abort, timeout). A no-op for an unknown or finished request. NextWake(now Time) (Time, bool) The earliest instant after now at which state may change with no new input; false if none. InFlightLimit() int How many batches may be in flight at once (for vLLM, max_concurrent_batches); at least one. Metrics(now Time) Metrics The engine's exported metrics. Snapshot() State Current state (waiting, running, in-flight, KV capacity), a copy the caller may keep. Plan() plan.PoolPlan (engine.Planned, optional) The pool plan the engine's transfers are priced against; required of an engine that starts a transfer. Fields() fields.FieldList The field list of the engine release this engine models: every configuration field and environment variable it reads, with its status and estimation rule (design VLM-3, SGL-3). The substrate defines the method and the shape of a list (the field list) and holds no engine's fields. The same list on every call, valid under FieldList.Validate, naming the engine kind and upstream release. inference-sim fields prints what the registered engine returns, without reading it.

docs.title: Requests: engine.Request
docs.text:
A request carries its identity, prompt, assigned output and scheduling facts. The LoRA fields follow vLLM's LoRARequest: Adapter is its lora_name and AdapterPath its lora_path. vLLM puts both, as ("lora", lora_name, lora_path), into the hash of every prefix-cache block of a LoRA request (_gen_lora_extra_hash_keys in vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py, v0.32.0), so an engine that models that hash needs the path as well as the name; the integer adapter ID does not enter it. Both are empty for the base model. Request.Validate refuses a path with no adapter name, and Add of the reference FIFO engine calls it.

A request that is a disaggregated decode (RemotePrefill) also states Peer, the node and rack of the engine holding its KV. A P/D proxy hands a vLLM decode engine the prefill's address in kv_transfer_params; a decode engine cannot learn where it pulls from any other way, and the links of the pull depend on it. Request.Validate refuses a remote prefill with no peer and a peer on any other request.

Calls are sequential: a simulator never calls an engine from two goroutines, and an engine starts none.

docs.title: Pipeline stages
docs.text:
An engine whose batches run through more than one pipeline stage, each on its own devices, also implements engine.Pipelined:

Method Does StageTimes(b Batch) []Duration StepTime(b) split by stage, in pipeline order: one entry per stage, each at least one microsecond, summing exactly to StepTime(b).

A simulator that honours it starts stage s of a batch once stage s-1 of that batch has ended and stage s has finished the batch ahead of it, and completes the batch when its last stage ends. The interface is optional: a simulator that does not look for it times each batch as one StepTime on one device, which serializes the stages. enginetest.Drive honours it and checks its law, including that every batch has the same number of stages.

docs.title: Batches
docs.text: A batch that runs requests gets a BatchID greater than every earlier one of the same engine and stays in flight until Complete names it. Any number of batches may be in flight, up to InFlightLimit. They complete in the order they were scheduled (ErrOutOfOrder otherwise), which is how vLLM's engine core consumes its batch queue: it appends each scheduled batch at one end and takes results from the other. A batch that runs nothing (Empty) is not in flight, but may still start transfers.

docs.title: Transfers
docs.text:
An engine reports each asynchronous KV move once, as an engine.Transfer among a batch's TransfersStarted. The simulator asks the Environment what the move demands of the fabric (Environment.TransferDemand, design section 6.2); it does not derive that from the report.

Field Meaning ID, Request The transfer's life: the simulator reports its end with TransferDone(ID, ...), and Request is the request it serves. Kind, Tokens, Blocks, Tier The engine's own report: load or store, size, and the offload tier as the engine's configuration names it. Empty Tier is a move between pools. Move The same move as the cost model prices it (plan.Transfer): the catalog device the tier name stands for, the node and rack that send and receive, and which way the bytes go.

Only the engine knows what a tier name means or where its ranks sit, so the engine states Move and the simulator fills nothing in. Transfer.Validate refuses a report that disagrees with its Move (tokens, direction, a tier name on a move between pools or none on a move to a tier). An engine that starts a transfer also implements engine.Planned, whose Plan returns the plan.PoolPlan the transfer is priced against, and PoolPlan.CheckTransfer refuses a move to a device the plan does not list or to a node the pool does not have. env.DemandFor is the simulator's side: it runs both checks and then calls TransferDemand with the engine's Move.

Admission has the same split. plan.HostPlan.Admission is the shape of the queue a request waits in before the engine admits it: Servers independent first-in first-out queues of WorkersPerServer servers each, stated by the engine from its own settings. Environment.HostDemand is what a request of a given prompt length asks of it: Service, the time it holds one server, and Delay, the time it only waits, which sum to the kernel's AdmissionOverhead. The simulator schedules a request as done = Admit(arrival, Service) + Delay on a queue of that shape, and knows nothing of the engine's own names for the servers. Delay is the part of the overhead that is not known to be work a server does (the registry gives the per-request term as a latency intercept of unknown origin), so charging it as Delay is an assumption with a bound on each side: all of it as Service is the serial model, none of it the concurrent one.

enginetest.Drive runs those checks on every started transfer, and Options.Boundary takes each one on across the simulator's side (envtest.Boundary does it with an Environment). An engine whose transfers cannot be demanded fails there, not as a zero price in a run.

docs.title: A pull that moves nothing
docs.text: A remote prefill can find all of its KV already here. Its pull then has Tokens 0 and Blocks 0, and Transfer.Validate, plan.Transfer.Validate and env.DemandFor accept it, for a move between pools only. The demand is zero bytes with no link and no floor: no division happens, and no handshake is charged, because the design prices none. A load or store to a tier of nothing is an engine bug and is refused. A negative size is refused everywhere.

docs.title: Limits, deferred to M3
docs.text:
• A pool that spans nodes (inference-sim/blis-substrate#48). plan.Transfer has one From and one To, but a vLLM offload job runs on every worker, each moving its own shard on its own node. Today an engine states the node that holds the tier (the first node of the pool when each node holds one), and the cost model prices that node's link. The demand is right for a one-node pool and does not fan out across nodes. The choice between one transfer per node and a lead rank with fan-out is open.
  • A hybrid model's KV groups (inference-sim/blis-substrate#49). vLLM's offload worker copies each KV cache group's blocks over that group's layers only, so a hybrid model moves fewer bytes than its blocks times the pool's stride. plan.Transfer has one Tokens, so the per-group sizes are lost at the boundary and the demand is sized from Tokens. Until a field carries them, the engine's own TransferTime and the TransferPricer and GroupTransferPricer interfaces stay, and are retired when it does.

docs.title: The wake protocol
docs.text:
• The simulator calls NextWake after every state-changing call (Add, Schedule, Complete, TransferDone, Finish, and a wake firing). An engine never cancels a wake: it reports a different instant, or false, the next time it is asked.
  • An earlier instant than the pending wake supersedes it; a later one, or false, replaces it.
  • The instant is always after now. A wake at or before now breaks the contract.
  • An engine with unfinished work, nothing in flight, no transfer outstanding and an empty Schedule must report a wake, or nothing would step it again.
  • At one instant a simulator processes, in this order: arrivals; transfer completions; batch completions; wakes and steps; timeouts last, so a request that completes at the instant its deadline passes has completed. An engine may rely on that order.

docs.title: Configuration: engine.Spec
docs.text:
Field Meaning Kind The engine model, such as vllm; the simulator looks it up in the factory registry. UpstreamVersion The real engine's release the configuration was written for. An engine refuses a release it does not model. Config The engine's configuration block, as YAML only the engine decodes. A factory decodes the node itself, so an error names its line in the document. Roots Directories the engine may read further inputs from, by role (catalog, registry, the configuration's own directory). Pool Which pool of a multi-pool document this engine is. Seed The run's seed.

engine.Register(f Factory) makes a factory available under its kind (it panics on an empty or a duplicate kind), engine.New(spec) builds an engine through it, and engine.Kinds() lists the registered kinds.

docs.title: Checking an implementation: engine/enginetest
docs.text: enginetest.Drive is a minimal discrete-event driver that follows the contract exactly. Driving an engine through it checks the laws every engine keeps, and reports the first one broken: no request is lost or finished twice, and none is finished that was never added; a batch runs only requests the engine holds, each once, and preempts only requests it holds and does not run, each once; batch IDs never repeat; batches complete in order; no more batches are in flight than the limit; a wake is always after the instant it was asked at; a step always takes time; a batch emits output only for its own requests, at most one sampled token plus its accepted drafts each; a finish reports the output tokens its batches emitted; an engine with work left always has a way to be stepped again; and the same inputs give the same run. enginetest.TestEngine runs those checks as a Go test, and enginetest.CheckProtocolErrors checks the error values. enginetest.FIFO is a deliberately simple engine built only through Spec and the registry: the proof that a second engine plugs in without changing this module.

docs.title: Rules: rules.EngineRules
docs.text: What one engine release accepts and refuses reaches a consumer, such as a cost model, through the rules.EngineRules interface rather than a concrete pack type, so the packs can live with the engine model that owns them. Rules packs lists the rules the registered packs check.

docs.title: Evaluation run
docs.text:
What a benchmark measured, one row per concurrency level, so that a prediction for the same scenario can be compared with it. The fields follow what benchmark harnesses already report.

For a validation case, use a measured run, which also records provenance, licence terms and metric definitions.

kind: EvaluationRun
name: llama-3.1-8b-on-h100-tp2-dp4
scenario: llama-3.1-8b-on-h100
harness: aiperf
engine_version: "0.29.0"
date: "2026-09-20"
points:
  - concurrency: 1
    completed_requests: 96
    output_tokens_per_sec: 157.3
    input_tokens_per_sec: 2543.0
    ttft_ms: 168.6
    itl_ms: 6.0
    mean_isl: 8015
    mean_osl: 496
    kv_utilization: 0.10
  - concurrency: 8
    completed_requests: 640
    output_tokens_per_sec: 1084.2
    ttft_ms: 212.4
    itl_ms: 7.1
    kv_utilization: 0.62
    prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.54

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always EvaluationRun. name string yes The run's identity. scenario string yes The scenario that was measured. harness string yes The benchmark harness that produced the numbers. Harnesses compute percentiles differently, so a comparison needs to know which. harness_version string no Its version. engine_version string yes The engine release the run exercised. It may differ from the scenario's. date string no When the measurement was taken, as an ISO 8601 date. points list yes At least one point, each at a different concurrency.

docs.title: points
docs.text:
Every field is as measured. Nothing is derived, so a reader can recompute any derived quantity and check it.

Key Type Required Meaning concurrency integer yes Simultaneous requests the harness kept in flight, at least 1. completed_requests integer no Requests finished at this level. output_tokens_per_sec number no Output throughput, tokens per second. input_tokens_per_sec number no Input throughput, tokens per second. ttft_ms number no Time to first token, ms. itl_ms number no Inter-token latency, ms. e2e_ms number no End-to-end latency, ms. mean_isl integer no Mean input length actually served. mean_osl integer no Mean output length actually served. kv_utilization number no Fraction of the KV pool in use, in [0, 1]. prefix_cache_hit_rate number no Fraction of prompt tokens served from cache, in [0, 1]. preemptions integer no Requests evicted and later recomputed. Nonzero means the engine ran out of KV cache space at this load.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A run is invalid if

  • kind is not EvaluationRun, or name, scenario, harness or engine_version is empty;
  • there are no points, a concurrency is below 1, or two points share a concurrency;
  • any number is not finite;
  • output_tokens_per_sec, ttft_ms or itl_ms is negative;
  • kv_utilization or prefix_cache_hit_rate lies outside [0, 1];
  • preemptions is negative.

A point with output throughput but neither ttft_ms nor itl_ms draws a warning: no prediction can be compared with it.

Source: spec/evaluation.

docs.title: Field list
docs.text:
An engine repository's classification of every configuration field and environment variable one release of its engine reads: whether the port models it, has proven it inert, or does not model it, with the evidence for each, and the rule a scoring harness applies when a run did not record the field (design VLM-3, §11.2).

Each engine repository publishes its list as fields.json at its root. The simulator prints it with blis fields --engine <kind>, and the accuracy dashboard and the configuration search read it there, so neither keeps a table of its own (COV-3, CFG-3). The list is JSON. fields.Parse (and fields.Load) reads it strictly: a key the schema does not declare, a key that appears twice in one object, anything after the document, or a number that does not convert exactly is an error naming where it is. fields.Marshal writes the canonical bytes, and a repository checks its committed file by comparing the two.

{
  "kind": "FieldList",
  "engine": {
    "kind": "vllm",
    "version": "0.32.0"
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND",
      "source": "env",

      },
      "estimation": {

        "preserves": "the backend vLLM picks for the tensor-parallel group and whether it may fall back to trtllm",
        "valid_when": [
          {
            "value_in": [
              "auto"
            ]
          },
          {
            "value_in": [
              "mnnvl"
            ],
            "tp_group_nodes": {
              "gt": 1
            },
            "compute_capability": {
              "gte": "10.0"
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL",
      "source": "env",

      "evidence": {

      },

      }
    },
    {
      "name": "kv_cache_dtype",

      },

            "value": 0,
