}

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always FieldList. engine mapping yes The engine and release the list classifies, below. fields list yes One entry per field, sorted by name and then source, in byte order; a field appears once.

docs.title: engine
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes The engine kind, for example vllm. version string yes The upstream release, for example 0.32.0.

docs.title: fields
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning name string yes The upstream's own name for the field or the variable. source string yes config for a configuration field, env for an environment variable. status string yes One of the statuses below. evidence mapping yes The one key the status requires, below. value_classes mapping for modelled and proven_inert The classes of values the evidence covers, below. Not allowed for the other statuses. estimation mapping yes The estimation rule, below.

Statuses:

modelled · proven_inert · not_modelled · inert_unproven

modelled The port reads the field and it changes a decision. proven_inert The field changes no decision, by a passing test or a reviewed argument. not_modelled The port refuses the field when it is set away from its default. inert_unproven Believed inert without a proof. Allowed only until M2 (release plan §3.3); a point that sets such a field is graded G2.

docs.title: evidence
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning traces list for modelled Paths, from the engine repository's root, of recorded traces whose scenarios set the field. At least one, none empty, none twice. proof string for proven_inert The test, or the argument, that shows the field inert. issue string for not_modelled The issue tracking the field, as <owner>/<repo>#<n>. note string for inert_unproven Why the field is believed inert.

Exactly the key its status requires is set; any other is an error.

docs.title: value_classes
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning type string yes One of the value types below. values list of strings for a proven-inert enumerated field Every value an enumerated field accepts. Optional for a modelled one. covered list of strings for boolean and enumerated The values the evidence sets: "true" and "false" for a boolean. At least one, none twice. thresholds list for numeric The values the upstream compares the field with, in increasing order of cut; two may share a value, below. covered_classes list of integers for numeric The numbered classes the evidence sets a value in, increasing. At least one.

A modelled field records the classes of values its evidence covers (design VLM-3), because evidence at one value says nothing about a value the upstream treats differently. A scoring harness grades a run G1 only when each modelled field it sets has a value in a covered class, and G2 when it sets one outside every covered class (design §11.3). ValueClasses.Covers answers that for one value.

Value types:

boolean · enumerated · numeric

boolean Two classes, true and false. enumerated One class per value. numeric An ordered number. n thresholds make n+1 classes, numbered from 0 for the values below the first threshold. A value is in class k when it is above k thresholds.

A proven-inert field records the classes its probes cover, and they must be all of them: a probe in one class shows nothing about another. A proven-inert enumerated field lists every value in values, so the check can tell that none was left out. A list the engine cannot write in full (a free-text field) is not provably inert by this record.

docs.title: thresholds
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning value number yes The number the upstream compares the field with. Finite. closed string yes Which class a value equal to value falls in.

Sides:

below · above

above A value equal to the threshold is in the class above it: the upstream compares with x >= value. below A value equal to the threshold is in the class below it: the upstream compares with x > value.

The thresholds are generated from the upstream's comparisons of the field, so a comparison the engine adds is a class the list must record. closed says which class takes the value equal to the threshold; it is not interval notation for the class itself. Thresholds increase by the place each cuts the line. Two comparisons at one value, x >= 8 in one place and x > 8 in another, send 7.999, 8 and 8.001 to three different sets of decisions, so the list states both, [8 above, 8 below] in that order (the cut of x >= 8 is just below 8 and that of x > 8 just above it), and they make three classes: below 8, 8 itself, above 8. Two thresholds at one value with the same side cut the line once and make an empty class, and [8 below, 8 above] is refused as out of order; each is written one way only.

ValueClasses.Covers takes any integer or float width, a json.Number or a numeric string, and refuses NaN and the infinities. A consumer in another language restates the rule, so these vectors, which a test here checks, fix it at a threshold. With thresholds [8 above]: 7.999 is class 0, 8 is class 1, 8.001 is class 1. With [8 below]: 7.999 and 8 are class 0, 8.001 is class 1. With [1 above, 256 below]: 0 is class 0, 1 and 256 are class 1, 257 is class 2. With [8 above, 8 below]: 7.999 is class 0, 8 is class 1, 8.001 is class 2.

docs.title: estimation
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning rule string yes One of the rules below. setting mapping for substitute Configuration field names and the values that stand in for this field. Not empty. reason string for substitute Why the setting is a fair stand-in. preserves string with valid_when A sentence naming what the upstream resolves identically when the field is left unset or stated as setting. valid_when list no Clauses saying when the stand-in is exact, below. Absent, the rule applies to every value.

Rules:

leave_unset · substitute · none

leave_unset Leave the field unset, so the engine resolves the upstream's default (X19). substitute State setting in place of the field; the point names the estimate and is graded G2. none No estimate exists; a point that needs one is not scored (G5).

setting and reason are allowed only with substitute. preserves and valid_when are allowed only with leave_unset or substitute.

docs.title: When the stand-in is exact
docs.text:
A stand-in is exact for a recorded value when the upstream resolves the field, left unset or stated as setting, as it resolves that value (design §11.2). Whether that is so can depend on the value and on the run. valid_when lists clauses: the stand-in is exact for a recorded value when at least one clause holds, and a clause holds when every key in it holds. A value for which no clause holds is not stood in for, and the point is G5 with the reason field_not_modelled. No new status, grade or reason code is involved. A clause sets at least one key.

Key Type Required Meaning value_in list of strings no The recorded value equals one of them. value_list_has_any list of strings no The recorded value, split on commas, has at least one of them as an item. value_list_has_none list of strings no The recorded value, split on commas, has none of them as an item. value_not_prefixed list of strings no The recorded value starts with none of them. tp_group_nodes mapping no The nodes the pool's tensor-parallel group spans satisfy the comparison, below. compute_capability mapping no The part's compute capability satisfies the comparison, below.

Strings are compared after trimming and folding to lower case, on both sides. A list is not empty.

A comparison sets at least one operator and holds when every operator it sets holds.

Key Type Required Meaning eq integer no The count equals it. gt integer no The count is greater than it. gte integer no The count is at least it. lt integer no The count is less than it. lte integer no The count is at most it. Key Type Required Meaning eq string no The capability equals it. gt string no The capability is greater than it. gte string no The capability is at least it. lt string no The capability is less than it. lte string no The capability is at most it.

A capability is "<major>.<minor>", such as "10.0", and orders by major, then minor, so 9.10 is below 10.0. The loader refuses any other spelling.

A consumer asks fields.Exact(estimation, facts) and does not restate these rules. The facts are Value, the recorded value; TPGroupNodes, the nodes the pool's tensor-parallel group spans, from the pool's tensor-parallel size and its GPUs per node; and ComputeCapability, the part's, from the catalog. A fact the consumer cannot supply is left unset, and a clause that needs it does not hold. Exact is false for rule none, and true for any value when valid_when is absent.

In the example above, VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND reads: auto is always exact; a stated mnnvl is exact only on several nodes from compute capability 10.0 up. The upstream resolves two things, the backend and whether a failed mnnvl workspace may fall back to trtllm. Left unset on one node it picks mnnvl and allows the fallback; a stated mnnvl never allows it. The two differ on a node without multicast, which no clause can state, so a stated mnnvl on one node is outside the rule and the point is G5 field_not_modelled. A rule must preserve everything the upstream resolves, not only the name.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Three schemas describe physical resources: a chip, an inter-node fabric, and the storage classes KV cache can be offloaded to. Every figure in them is a datasheet figure, or one computed from datasheet figures; Provenance says which. A measured correction to any of them is a coefficient and belongs in the registry.

The chip and fabric keys are in PascalCase, as the catalog's files write them. Each key carries its unit. All three schemas accept the catalog's _comment and _comment_* keys inside each chip, fabric and storage class, and discard them on load. Any other undeclared key, including any other key that begins with an underscore, is an error.

docs.title: Chip
docs.text:
A file under hardware/, named by its file.

hardware/h100.yaml
Provenance: vendor_spec
FieldProvenance:
  MemoryGiB: "measured:H100 SXM5 80GB HBM3"
TFlopsPeak: 989.5
TFlopsFP8: 1979.0
BwPeakTBs: 3.35
_comment_memory: "MemoryGiB is the device total the CUDA driver reports (torch.cuda total_memory), which is what vLLM v0.31.0 multiplies by gpu_memory_utilization (requested = ceil(total_memory x gmu), vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:539-558), not the datasheet's 80 GB: 85,029,158,912 B = 79.1896 GiB on H100 SXM5 80GB HBM3 (vLLM usage stats 'gpu_memory_per_device': 85029158912, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26836; vLLM start-up logs 'Free memory on device (76.0/79.19 GiB)', InferenceX DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash H100 runs, https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35314892357). Measured, not vendor_spec; the rest of this file is vendor_spec."
MemoryGiB: 79.1895752
_comment_interconnect: "IntraNodeBwGBps is the on-package NVLink 4 link as a per-GPU NOMINAL unidirectional bandwidth in GB/s: 900 GB/s bidirectional datasheet spec => 450 unidirectional per GPU. vendor_spec (bidirectional / 2), NOT measured effective throughput; any measured correction is a per-cluster blis-registry number. The inter-node fabric figure and the intra:inter ratio it feeds (#1530) live with the reusable Network fabric class (networks/ib-400g.yaml), paired with this chip per deployment (a cluster/pool concept, #1662)."
IntraNodeBwGBps: 450
_comment_sm: "SMCount is the count of enabled Streaming Multiprocessors on the GH100 die as shipped in this part, from the NVIDIA datasheet (https://resources.nvidia.com/en-us-tensor-core/nvidia-tensor-core-gpu-datasheet). H100 SXM5 enables 132 of the GH100 die's 144 SMs. The cost model uses SMCount for two things: the per-SM share of peak FLOPs, and the 12-SM derate a Triton-path KV fetch withholds while it overlaps a forward pass (cost model §8.3), which is 9.09% at 132 SMs and 11.11% at 108."
SMCount: 132
_comment_cc: "ComputeCapability is the CUDA compute capability NVIDIA lists for this part (https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus). A model graph that differs by GPU generation resolves its architecture overlay by the major version, so a chip that states none cannot run such a graph."
ComputeCapability: "9.0"
Key Type Required Meaning Provenance string yes Where the figures come from. One of the provenances. FieldProvenance map no The source of a field when it is not the file's Provenance, by field name: datasheet, published, or measured:<device>. A field it does not name has the file's. TFlopsPeak number yes Dense BF16 peak, TFLOP/s. TFlopsFP8 number no Dense FP8 peak, TFLOP/s. Omit on parts without native FP8. If set, it must exceed TFlopsPeak. TFlopsNVFP4 number no Dense NVFP4 (NVIDIA's 4-bit float) peak, TFLOP/s. Omit where the format is emulated rather than native. BwPeakTBs number yes HBM (on-package memory) bandwidth, TB/s. MemoryGiB number yes HBM capacity, GiB. IntraNodeBwGBps number yes On-node bandwidth per GPU, one direction, GB/s. NVLink where present. SMCount integer yes Streaming multiprocessors, positive. ComputeCapability string no CUDA compute capability, major.minor, such as 9.0 (H100, H200) or 10.0 (B200, GB200). A model graph that distinguishes architectures is resolved by the major version; one cannot be resolved for a chip that states none. GPUsPerNode integer no GPUs in one node. GPUsPerRack integer no GPUs in one rack, where a rack is a distinct link tier. A multiple of GPUsPerNode. IntraRackBwGBps number no Bandwidth between nodes inside a rack, GB/s. Needs GPUsPerRack.

docs.title: Fabric
docs.text:
A file under networks/, named by its file.

networks/ib-400g.yaml, comments omitted
Provenance: vendor_spec
InterNodeBwGBps: 50
Key Type Required Meaning Provenance string yes One of the provenances. FieldProvenance map no The source of a field when it is not the file's Provenance, as on a chip. InterNodeBwGBps number yes Bandwidth per GPU, one direction, GB/s: the NIC's line rate in Gb/s divided by eight. Nominal, not measured. RDMA boolean no Whether transfers bypass the CPU.

docs.title: Storage classes
docs.text:
One file, devices/storage.yaml, names each storage class. The key is the class's name, which scenarios and deployments use. A name key inside a class is accepted and replaced by that key. Comment keys are allowed inside a class but not at the top level of the file, where every key is a class.

A class is a name and a description, and states no number. What a transfer to or from it costs is a fitted or assumed value, so it is a coefficient and not a catalog fact (design SUB-18): the registry holds offload_tier_<class>_read_rate, offload_tier_<class>_write_rate (bytes per microsecond, equal to MB/s) and offload_tier_<class>_base_latency (microseconds per transfer) for every class on every chip, with the method and the evidence of each, and the kernel's TierTime reads them from the scenario's coefficient sets. A file that still states read_bandwidth_mb_s, write_bandwidth_mb_s or base_latency_us is refused.

devices/storage.yaml
# Storage tiers for KV-cache offload: the classes a deployment's offload block may name.
#
# A tier is an identity and a description here, and states no number. What a transfer to or
# from a tier costs (the read rate, the write rate and the fixed cost of one transfer) is not a
# declared fact of a device, so it is not in this file (SUB-18, SUB-3). Every figure this file
# held was one of two things: a fit to one host's measurements (cpu_dram), or a value the
# simulator's authors chose for a class (the rest), with no datasheet, benchmark or other
# source cited for it. A fitted or assumed value is a coefficient, and the coefficient registry
# holds each one scoped to the hardware it describes, with its method and its evidence:
#
#   offload_tier_<tier>_read_rate     bytes per microsecond (equal to MB/s), tier to GPU
#   offload_tier_<tier>_write_rate    bytes per microsecond, GPU to tier
#   offload_tier_<tier>_base_latency  microseconds per transfer
#
# in the registry set cost-model-offload-tiers, written by
# registry/scripts/emit_offload_tiers.py. The kernel's TierTime reads them from the scenario's
# coefficient sets. A tier added here needs those three entries for every catalog chip, and a
# test fails until it has them. A file that states read_bandwidth_mb_s, write_bandwidth_mb_s or
# base_latency_us for a tier is refused.
#
# The tiers were split verbatim from the kv_offload_devices: section of inference-sim's
# defaults.yaml (blis-catalog b20b7f1), added by inference-sim PR #1594 (commit 3673d3655e),
# whose own comment describes them as "representative device classes seeded for the multi-tier
# offload holes (#1588/#1589); operators override per run for their hardware". The tiers are
# classes (an NVMe Gen4 drive, object storage), not specific products, so no single datasheet
# could state them.
nvme_gen4:
  _comment: "A PCIe Gen4 NVMe drive, as a class and not a product. Its terms are the registry's offload_tier_nvme_gen4_* entries, assumed."
nvme_gen3:
  _comment: "A PCIe Gen3 NVMe drive, as a class and not a product. Its terms are the registry's offload_tier_nvme_gen3_* entries, assumed."
sata_ssd:
  _comment: "A SATA SSD, as a class and not a product. Its terms are the registry's offload_tier_sata_ssd_* entries, assumed."
cpu_dram:
  _comment: >-
    Pinned host DRAM, reached across the host link. Its terms are the registry's offload_tier_cpu_dram_* entries:
    the rates were fitted to InferenceX CollectiveX swap_blocks rows on one H100 host (sku h100-dgxc) and are
    scoped to that host as transferred rates, with the floor assumed; every other chip carries the same figures
    as transferred and assumed entries until its own host is timed. The host link's own ceiling is the registry's
    host_link_bandwidth, per chip.
s3:
  _comment: "An object store reached over the network, as a class and not a product. Its terms are the registry's offload_tier_s3_* entries, assumed."
nvme_gen4_raid0_8x:
  _comment: >-
    A DGX/HGX H100 node's local NVMe data volume. NVIDIA's DGX H100 user guide and datasheet state 8 x 3.84 TB
    NVMe U.2 drives in RAID 0 at /raid (PCIe Gen4); the drive model is not public. Its terms are the registry's
    offload_tier_nvme_gen4_raid0_8x_* entries: assumed, scoped to the DGX H100 node, and carried unchanged,
    as assumed, to the other chips.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Every number must be finite. Beyond that, a chip is invalid if

  • Provenance is not recognized;
  • TFlopsPeak, BwPeakTBs, MemoryGiB or IntraNodeBwGBps is not positive;
  • SMCount is missing or not positive;
  • TFlopsFP8 or TFlopsNVFP4 is negative;
  • TFlopsFP8 is positive but not above TFlopsPeak; no shipped part has an FP8 peak at or below its BF16 peak, so this is almost always a transcription slip;
  • a peak is a sparse figure entered as dense: TFlopsFP8 is more than 3.5 times TFlopsPeak, TFlopsNVFP4 is more than 3.5 times TFlopsFP8, or TFlopsNVFP4 does not exceed TFlopsFP8 (design SUB-16: catalog peaks are dense figures, and their ratios between data types are the datasheet's; the shipped parts run 2.0 to 3.11);
  • GPUsPerRack is not a multiple of GPUsPerNode, when both are set;
  • IntraRackBwGBps is set without GPUsPerRack;
  • ComputeCapability is set but is not major.minor;
  • FieldProvenance names a field the type does not have, or a source that is not datasheet, published or measured:<device>. A fitted or assumed value is not a catalog fact: it is a coefficient and belongs in the coefficient registry (design SUB-18);
  • a fact the file states has no source: the source of a fact FieldProvenance does not name is the file's Provenance, which must itself be a source, so a file whose Provenance is derived states a source for each fact it records; or FieldProvenance names a fact the file does not state.

A fabric is invalid if Provenance is not recognized, FieldProvenance is invalid as above, or InterNodeBwGBps is not positive. A storage class is invalid if its name is not lower-case letters, digits and underscores, because the name is the middle of three coefficient names. devices/storage.yaml fails to load if it declares no class, a class with no value, or a class that states a rate or a latency.

The catalog's convention that each SMCount cites a source in its _comment_sm prose is not checked, here or anywhere else, because comments are discarded before validation. blis-schemas#32 records why it was left out of the schema.

docs.title: Why three schemas
docs.text:
A chip's peak rates belong to the die. A fabric belongs to the cluster: the same chip sits behind InfiniBand in one cluster and RoCE in another. Storage belongs to whoever provisioned the node. The cost of a collective that crosses nodes depends on the ratio of on-node to off-node bandwidth, which is a property of a chip paired with a fabric, not of either one. The ratio is therefore a function of both, hardware.IntraToInterRatio(chip, fabric), and not a key in either file.

Source: spec/hardware.

docs.title: Kernel interface
docs.text:
kernel.Kernel is the interface a cost model implements and a simulator calls. One value prices one pool of one deployment: how much memory a rank holds, how long a forward pass over a batch takes, and what transfers and host work cost. The cost model in kernel/ is the implementation in use.

Every method is a pure function of its arguments and the configuration the kernel was constructed from: the same inputs give the same outputs, nothing is mutated, and calls are safe from several goroutines at once. There is no Init method; a kernel comes from its implementation's constructor, already resolved. Why the interface is drawn this way is the subject of Where the kernel stops.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Memory FixedBytes() MemoryBreakdown Per-rank memory that does not depend on the requests: weights, activation peak, captured CUDA graphs, redundant experts, communication buffers. SequenceFixedBytes() int64 Per-sequence memory that does not grow with length, such as recurrent state. Zero for a model with attention only. SequenceVariableBytes(tokens int) int64 Per-sequence memory for a given token count, quantized to the engine's page size. Step time StepTime(Batch) StepEstimate The time of one forward pass over a batch. Transfers TierTime(tier, dir, bytes, queueDepth) time.Duration One transfer to or from an offload tier. PDTransferTime(tokens, from, to Placement) time.Duration Moving one request's KV between pools. PDTransferDemand(tokens, from, to Placement) TransferDemand The same handoff as payload, floor and links, for a caller arbitrating concurrent transfers. Host work AdmissionOverhead(promptTokens int) time.Duration CPU work before a request can be scheduled, such as tokenization. Excludes queueing. AdmissionDemand(promptTokens int) HostDemand AdmissionOverhead split into Service, the time a request holds one server of the admission queue (plan.HostPlan.Admission), and Delay, the time it only waits. They sum to AdmissionOverhead. OutputTokenOverhead() time.Duration Host work per emitted token, such as detokenization and streaming. CompletionOverhead() time.Duration Fixed work when a request finishes. Counts toward end-to-end latency, not time to first token. Provenance Provenance() []CoefficientOrigin Every coefficient the kernel used, with its set, method and scope. Resolved() Resolution What the kernel resolved, including requests it overrode. Deployment() deployment.Pool The pool it prices, as the document stated it.

Deployment() returns the request and Resolved() the resolution. For the parallel widths or the all-reduce backend, read Resolved(). For settings that resolution does not change, such as max_num_seqs and block_size, read the pool. The returned pool is a shallow copy; treat it as read-only.

docs.title: Step estimates
docs.text:
A step is priced as a sequence of stages, one per layer, since each layer needs the previous layer's output. Within a stage, work on different resources can overlap.

StepEstimate reports two bounds and a diagnosis:

Overlap Perfect overlap within each stage: the slowest resource in each stage, summed over the stages. NoOverlap No overlap anywhere: every resource's work, summed. Bottleneck The resource that did the most work over the step, which answers "what should be relieved". It is not the resource that set Overlap; since Overlap sums per-stage maxima, no single resource need account for it. PerResource Each resource's total, for a caller that needs to see why. Stages For a pipeline-parallel deployment (pp > 1), the step split by stage in pipeline order, each bracketed the same way and including the send of its activations to the next stage. The stages' Overlap figures sum exactly to Overlap, and their NoOverlap figures to NoOverlap; a single-stage step reports none. A simulator needs the split because two batches in flight occupy two stages at once: a new batch can enter every slowest-stage time, while each batch's output takes the whole sum. kerneltest.CheckStages checks the law. Trust How much the price rests on measurement (design VAL-3): the least trusted effective rank among the coefficients the price used, with the method and the entry that set it. The rank is a method's place in the order measured (1), calibrated, transferred, literature, vendor_spec, roofline, assumed (7). A price that reads an entry outside the range its fit covered ranks no better than transferred (3) and carries the flag extrapolated. An entry whose 95% interval is unbounded or wider than half its value ranks as assumed (7) and carries the flag unidentified; it keeps its method and its citations. The zero value means the implementation does not report trust. Ties go to the entry whose name sorts first, so the answer does not depend on the order of lookups.

docs.title: Unusual model shapes
docs.text:
conformance/shapetest holds six model graphs that each differ from the catalog's models in one structural way: every layer windowed, every layer recurrent, MLA only, a draft layer declared last, a single layer, and no attention at all (design SUB-10). Every shape is a valid graph. An implementation either prices a shape or refuses it with its own reason, and never both or neither. A priced shape holds to the size law of its cache kind, read from the graph: a shape with no cache holds nothing per sequence; a state-only shape holds its state; a windowed shape holds some and stops growing at the window; a growing cache grows with context. No size or price is negative, and every step is positive and under an hour, with Overlap not above NoOverlap. shapetest.Run(t, build) runs the suite, and the cost model, blis-vllm and blis-sglang each run it.

A configuration whose conclusion changes between the two bounds needs a measurement rather than a prediction.

The resources are:

sm · hbm · nvlink · nic · pcie · copy_engine · host

A collective appears under sm when the resolved backend is an SM-consuming kernel and under a link otherwise. The resolved backend decides this, not the requested one.

docs.title: Batches
docs.text:
A Batch is what the simulator supplies for one step.

Field Meaning Reqs []ReqShape One entry per request in the batch. DecodeThreshold int Engine configuration that selects the attention kernel for each request. An engine that states a step as a plan.StepShape carries the same figure as StepShape.DecodeQueryLen (a request scheduling at most that many tokens is a decode; unstated reads as 1), and latencykernel.BatchOf turns a step shape into a Batch with it. The cost model supplies no threshold of its own. SMBudget int SMs available this step: the chip's count less any held by a concurrent offload fetch. PadTokens int Tokens this data-parallel rank pads its step with under vLLM's DP lockstep: every rank runs the group's largest token count, and a rank with nothing scheduled runs a dummy batch of pad alone. Pad tokens run the GEMMs, the MoE dispatch and combine and the expert paths, but never the logits, the LM head, the vocabulary all-gather or sampling. They are not requests. 0 means none; never negative. DraftPaddedTokens int Tokens this rank's drafter launches, after its own graph bucket and the width its data-parallel group agreed; the drafter coordinates its padding apart from the target's. The rows beyond the rank's own draft rows run the GEMMs and the MoE paths and no attention. An engine that states a step as a plan.StepShape carries it as DraftShape.Passes[rank].Padded. 0 means the drafter launches only its own rows; never negative. TailFrom int The index, in the model graph's expanded layer stack, of the first layer that runs over fewer rows than the requests scheduled: layers TailFrom to the end run each request's TailRows rows. The engine states it, for the steps in which its forward pass does that (an engine can run the layers past the last one that produces KV on each request's trailing window only). The embedding, the layers before it, the head, the drafter and the host and launch terms keep the whole batch. An engine that states a step as a plan.StepShape carries it as StepShape.TailFrom. 0 means no tail: every layer runs every scheduled token. A value at or past the stack's length leaves no layer in the tail; never negative. TailPadTokens int Rows the tail's batch is launched with beyond its own, when the engine pads it to a size of its own; as PadTokens does for the whole batch they run the GEMMs, the collectives and the experts, and no attention. As a step shape it is PaddedShape.TailTokens less the tail's rows. Read only with TailFrom; never negative.

Each ReqShape carries the counts an engine's own scheduler reads:

Field Meaning Scheduled Tokens scheduled this step. Under speculative decoding a decoding request schedules the draft length plus one, so a count above 1 does not imply prefill. Computed Tokens already computed, as of batch formation. PromptLen The prompt length. With Computed, it tells the last chunk of a prefill split across steps apart from a decode. CachedTokens The prefix-cache hit, already subtracted from Scheduled. A count, not a rate. TailRows How many of Scheduled the layers from Batch.TailFrom run: the request's last TailRows tokens, at their own positions (a step shape's RequestStep.TailRows). 0 means all of them, as for a decode row. Never more than Scheduled, and refused (Validate) without a TailFrom.

Batch.Tokens() sums Scheduled, and Batch.PaddedTokens() adds PadTokens: the count the layers run. Batch.Validate() refuses a negative count, more tail rows than scheduled tokens, and tail rows with no TailFrom. Batch.UniformDecode(width) reports whether every request schedules exactly width tokens. Some engine behavior, such as when dual-batch overlap engages, uses one threshold for such a batch and another for any other.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
A deployment states requests. The kernel's constructor decides what runs, and Resolution reports it.

Field Meaning TensorParallelWidth, DataParallelWidth, ExpertParallelWidth The resolved layout. The expert width is tp × pcp × dp with expert parallelism on, and 1 with it off. AllReduceBackend The all-reduce that will run, which may differ from the request. AsyncScheduling The resolved value of the tri-state request. CascadeAttention Whether cascade attention is available after every condition is applied. SequenceParallelMoE Whether the MoE input is made sequence-parallel, replacing an all-reduce with a reduce-scatter and all-gather. Overrides []Override Each request the layout could not honor: the field, what was requested, what was resolved, and why.

A width of zero means unset, not "no parallelism". TensorParallel(), DataParallel() and ExpertParallel() return the widths with a floor of one, for a reader that may see a zero value.

docs.title: Transfer demand
docs.text:
PDTransferTime prices a handoff as if it ran alone. A simulator running several at once needs to know which links they share, and which part of each price sharing stretches. PDTransferDemand answers both:

Field Meaning Bytes int64 The payload. Floor time.Duration Time the transfer takes however much bandwidth it gets. Sharing a link does not lengthen it. Links []LinkUse Every link the payload crosses, each named once: a LinkID and the rate the link offers to a transfer alone on it.

A LinkID is opaque. Two demands naming the same ID share that link while both are in flight, and IDs are comparable across the kernels of one deployment.

The law is part of the contract: alone, a demand costs exactly what PDTransferTime charges, max(Floor, Bytes / slowest link rate), or Floor with no links. TransferDemand.AloneTime() is that definition, including its conversion to a duration, so an implementation that computes PDTransferTime from its own demand satisfies the law by construction.

The kernel states the links; it never sees other transfers. How a shared link's bandwidth is divided is the simulator's to decide, and the schema does not prescribe it.

Package contracts/conformance/kerneltest checks the law against any implementation, the way testing/fstest checks a file system:

func TestPDTransferLaw(t *testing.T) {
    k := newKernel(t) // the implementation under test
    kerneltest.TestPDTransfer(t, k, kerneltest.PDCases())
}

Where the scenario states switch groups, a handoff between groups names two more links, uplink/egress/group/<g> and uplink/ingress/group/<h>; see Switch groups.

PDCases covers a same-node, a same-rack and a cross-rack handoff at token counts from 0 to 131,072. CheckPDTransfer checks one case and returns an error, for a caller with cases of its own; TestPDTransfer fails when given no cases, since it would then check nothing. CheckLinksAgree checks that two kernels of one deployment name the same links at the same rates for one handoff, and that both demands are well formed. CheckPDTransfer requires a well-formed demand (TransferDemand.Check, which also refuses a payload that crosses no link, since an arbiter would then have nothing to share), the same demand from two calls, and an exact match with PDTransferTime. TestPDTransfer also requires that more tokens never move fewer bytes between one pair of placements; it does not require the floor to stay fixed, since per-transfer overhead can grow with the pages a transfer moves.

Adding a method to Kernel breaks every other implementation, fakes included, until it adds the method.

docs.title: Other types
docs.text:
Type Meaning MemoryBreakdown Weights, ActivationPeak, CUDAGraph, EPLBRedundant, CommBuffers, in bytes; Total() sums them. Direction to_tier (eviction) or from_tier (fetch). Priced separately because flash reads and writes differ. Placement A rank's Node, Rack and Pool (the pool's role). Comparing two placements chooses the link a transfer uses. CoefficientOrigin One row of the provenance trail: entry Name, Set, Method, Scope, and KernelMatch: exact when the entry lists a kernel implementation that runs, unkeyed when it lists none, empty for a value the kernel supplied itself.

Source: kernel.

docs.title: Measured run
docs.text:
A measured sweep recorded as a validation case: where every number came from, under what terms, how each metric was defined, and how far the configuration BLIS would simulate is from the one that ran. The verdict is computed from those facts, never read from the file.

A measured run supersedes the evaluation run for scoring. Runs live in the catalog under catalog/measurements/<license_ref>/<name>.yaml, beside the licence registry catalog/measurements/sources.yaml.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always MeasuredRun. name string yes The run's identity, a lowercase slug. In the catalog, also its file name. schema_version integer yes Always 1. source mapping yes Where the numbers came from, below. model string no The catalog model that was served. engine_version string no The engine release that ran. cluster mapping no The cluster it ran on. Coefficients are not part of a measurement, so this is the cluster alone. deployment mapping no The deployment that ran, checked against cluster when both are present. router mapping no The router in front of the deployment, below. workload mapping no The workload binding that reproduces the request stream. client mapping yes The load generator, below. metric_defs mapping yes Each metric's definition, keyed by metric name. points list yes One entry per load level, strictly increasing. The first is the anchor shape error is measured from. provenance list no One row per setting, comparing the sources that state it. diff list no Each difference between the measured configuration and BLIS's. verdict string no EXACT, PARTIAL or NOT_REPRODUCIBLE. If present, must equal the computed verdict. resolution string with EXACT STRICT or RESOLVED. If present, must equal the computed resolution. duplicate_of string no Another run with the same model, hardware, loads and values. supersedes string no A run this one replaces.

docs.title: source
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes The publisher. One of the source kinds. adapter mapping yes The extracting code: name, version and the sha256 of its source. inputs list yes Every file read, each with its digest. At least one has role report. extraction mapping yes How values were read, below. retrieved_utc string no When the inputs were fetched, RFC 3339 in UTC. license_ref string yes The entry in measurements/sources.yaml whose terms govern the run. docs.title: metric_defs
docs.text:
Each definition is keyed by the metric name the points use. A field left out is unstated, and any unstated formula, population, clock, or statistic (denominator for a throughput) keeps the run from EXACT: a scorer cannot tell whether a BLIS metric is the same quantity.

Not for a throughput. population string no What the statistic is over: per_request, pooled_chunks or pooled_tokens. denominator string no What a throughput divides by. Only for a throughput. clock string no client or server timestamps; simulated only in a Result. start_event string no When a latency starts. stop_event string no When a latency stops. output_len_source string no Where output token counts come from. reasoning_counted_as_content boolean no Whether reasoning tokens count as output. percentile_method string with a percentile How a percentile interpolates; numpy_linear. unit string yes ms, tokens_per_s or requests_per_s; must be the formula's. cite string yes Where the definition is read from: a harness file and line, or the report's text.

An unbounded rate under a cap is the cap alone. docs.text:
One row per setting, comparing the report, the script that produced it, the run's own artifact, and the value BLIS would use.

docs.title: router
docs.text:
The router is described by kind; an endpoint picker is pinned by the digest of its config, whose bytes the simulator reads.

Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes direct or epp. epp mapping with epp The picker. Not allowed with direct. Key Type Required Meaning version string yes The picker's version. image string no Its image. config mapping yes Its plugin config: path and sha256. flow_control string no A summary of the flow-control settings. docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
The verdict is computed; a stated one must match.

NOT_REPRODUCIBLE BLIS cannot build the run: model, engine_version, cluster, deployment or workload is missing, or a diff entry is not_expressible. EXACT Otherwise, when the diff is empty, no provenance row is MISMATCH or UNVERIFIABLE, every UNSTATED row has resolved_by, every metric definition is complete, the client harness is recorded, and the licence permits scoring. Resolution is RESOLVED when a row was resolved by a rule and STRICT otherwise. Only an EXACT run may anchor calibration. PARTIAL Any other run. It is scored and reported apart from EXACT runs.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A run is invalid if

  • kind is not MeasuredRun, name is not a lowercase slug, or schema_version is not 1;
  • a vocabulary value is not recognized, or a digest is not 64 lowercase hex characters;
  • the source has no adapter name, version or digest, no inputs, no report input, or an input without a url or path;
  • a timestamp is not RFC 3339 UTC, or the client image is not pinned by digest;
  • the cluster, deployment, router or workload is invalid, or the deployment does not fit the cluster;
  • a metric definition has no unit or cite, a unit that is not its formula's, a statistic on a throughput, a denominator on a latency, or a percentile without a method;
  • there are no points, two share an id, a point states no load, points mix load modes or are not strictly increasing, or a metric has no definition or a negative or non-finite value;
  • a provenance row's sources do not support its verdict, resolved_by is on a row that is not UNSTATED, or bound is missing for bounded or present otherwise;
  • a removable difference names no owner_repo;
  • a string carries a credential: a token, a private key, a Kubernetes Secret reference, or a kubeconfig path;
  • a stated verdict or resolution is not the computed one.

docs.title: Licence registry
docs.text:
measurements/sources.yaml lists every source a run may cite. Only a verified entry permits anything.

    license: Apache-2.0
    status: verified

Key Type Required Meaning id string yes The key a run's license_ref names, a lowercase slug. title string yes What the source is. license string when verified The SPDX identifier the evidence states. status string yes verified, unverified, or refused. permits list when verified Uses the terms permit: score, derive_coefficients, redistribute. Empty unless verified. evidence list when verified Quoted statements of the terms. attribution string no What a use must carry. note string unless verified Why a source is unverified or refused. A catalog run must cite a licence that permits redistribute, since a committed file is redistributed; validate-measurements -local admits one that permits only scoring, for output kept out of the repository.

Source: spec/measurement, spec/router.

docs.title: Metric registry
docs.text:
One definition, with an identifier, for every metric BLIS reports, compares, ranks or uses in a service-level check (design §8.7, DEV-8). A Result names each figure by its identifier; the definition lives here, once.

A definition states the metric's formula (the per-sample quantity), its statistic, its population (what the statistic is taken over), its window, its unit, and how it treats requests unfinished at the horizon. Time to first token, time per output token and inter-token latency follow the benchmark clients BLIS is compared with:

  • tpot_* is per request: each completed request with at least two output tokens gives one sample, (E2E - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1), as vllm bench serve computes it.
  • itl_* is pooled over tokens: every gap between consecutive output tokens of those same requests is one sample (inference-sim #1894).
  • step_interval_* is the engine's step interval. Under speculative decoding one step emits several tokens, so it is not a per-token figure, and it is never compared with itl_* or tpot_*.

docs.title: Scope and aggregate
docs.text:
A figure is a metric at a scope (design §8.7): the whole cluster, one pool, or one instance. The scope selects which requests, tokens or steps form the population; the formula, statistic, window and unit do not change. A definition states the scopes it is defined at (Scopes), in no particular order, and the aggregates its figures may take (Aggregates). Every metric is defined at the cluster, a pool and an instance except the router's queue delay, which exists only at the cluster and so has no aggregate: an aggregate ranges from a narrower scope to a wider one, and a metric defined at one scope has nothing to range over.

A figure that picks one of the figures of a narrower scope names the scope it ranges over and the aggregate: the largest p99 time to first token over instances is a figure at the cluster scope, aggregate max, over instance. It is one instance's figure, not the cluster's own p99, and the two are never compared.

The aggregates are max and min. Design §8.7 gives one example, the largest p99 time to first token over instances, and the plan speaks of ranking on "the worst" instance. The worst instance depends on which way the metric improves: the largest figure for a latency, the smallest for a throughput, a hit rate or an attainment. Each definition therefore states its direction (Better: lower_is_better or higher_is_better), and Definition.Worst returns the aggregate that picks the worst instance for it. The design names no mean or sum of figures, and an unweighted mean of per-instance percentiles or fractions is neither the cluster's figure nor a weighted one, so neither is admitted. Adding one would be a design change.

Definition.Validate refuses a definition with no scope, a scope or aggregate outside the lists, a repeated one, no direction, and aggregates with fewer than two scopes to range between. Figure.Validate first validates the figure's definition, then refuses a figure with no scope, at a scope its metric is not defined at, with an aggregate its metric does not admit, or ranging over a scope that is not narrower than its own.

docs.title: Throughput per GPU and interactivity
docs.text:
Two quantities have more than one common form, and the registry keeps each form as its own metric because a figure of one is not a figure of another. The forms below follow the result processor of InferenceX, read at the commits cited in each definition's Follows.

Throughput per GPU:

  • output_tok_s_per_gpu: output tokens over the window, over all the GPUs of the scope.
  • total_tokens_per_second_per_gpu: prompt plus output tokens over the window, over all the GPUs of the scope, prefill GPUs included. It is InferenceX's tput_per_gpu, the throughput axis of its frontier.
  • output_tokens_per_second_per_decode_gpu: output tokens over the window, over the decode GPUs of the deployment only (all its GPUs when it has no separate decode pool). It is InferenceX's output_tput_per_gpu for a disaggregated deployment, and is defined at the cluster only, where the decode GPUs are counted.

A worked example: a run with 4 prefill and 4 decode GPUs that completes 3000 prompt tokens and 1000 output tokens a second reads 125 on the first, 500 on the second and 250 on the third.

Interactivity:

  • interactivity_mean: the mean over requests of each request's own rate, (output tokens - 1) / (E2E - TTFT), after the first token. It follows aiperf.
  • interactivity_of_mean_tpot: 1000 over the mean of tpot in milliseconds. It is InferenceX's mean_intvty, which divides the mean time per output token into one.

Two requests that take 10 ms and 40 ms per output token give 62.5 tokens per second on the first (the mean of 100 and 25) and 40 on the second (1000 over the mean 25 ms). The first is never smaller than the second, and the two differ by more as the requests differ more. interactivity_p50 and interactivity_p90 are 1000 over the percentile of tpot, as InferenceX publishes its median and p90.

Compare refuses any pair across forms and names the field that tells them apart: formula for total against output tokens and for the two interactivity means, denominator for all GPUs against decode GPUs.

docs.title: Comparing figures
docs.text:
metrics.Compare returns the difference between two figures only when ComparableFigures accepts them: their definitions are identical, field for field, and their scope, member, aggregate and the scope they range over are the same. Otherwise it returns an error naming the first field that differs (scope, member, aggregate or over for the figure; the definition's field for the definition). A figure at the pool or instance scope names its member, the pool or instance it is of by the name the deployment gives it, and a figure at the cluster scope has none; design §8.7 makes the scope "the whole cluster, one pool, or one instance", so instance 3's figure and instance 7's are not comparable, and the same instance's in two runs is. For an aggregate, the member is that of the figure's own scope: the largest p99 over the instances of the pool decode is at the pool scope, member decode. Identifiers decide nothing: the same definition under two names compares, and two definitions under one name do not. A figure with no scope is refused.

The simulator reads the registry directly. The dashboard and config search read it through inference-sim metrics.
