docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always Result. schema_version integer yes Always 3. Version 3 requires each figure to state its scope; a version 2 Result is refused. name string yes The run's identity, a lowercase slug. engine mapping yes The engine the run used, below. data mapping yes The catalog and registry the run read, below. selected_entries mapping yes The registry entries lookups returned, and the files no lookup read, below. input mapping yes Everything the run was given, resolved, below. frame mapping yes The experimental frame, below. revisions mapping yes The BLIS module versions the simulator was built from. rerun_of mapping no The Result whose input this run was produced from. revision_changes list no Each component whose revision differs from rerun_of's. Only with rerun_of. window mapping yes The measured window as it fell in this run. metrics mapping no Figures keyed by metric identifier, each one of frame.metrics. Absent when the run failed an acceptance condition. requests mapping yes The count of each fate. request_rows list no One row per generated request, below. goodput mapping no SLO targets and each class's outcome, when the input states targets. breakdowns mapping no The metrics split along the axes the run exercised. reports mapping no Each component's own report, carried as reported. overrides list no Every setting simulated differently from input, and what chose it. resolutions list no The engine's own resolution of the settings it resolves, beside overrides. artifacts mapping no Bulk outputs by reference, keyed by role, a lowercase slug. runtime mapping no The only part that depends on the host or the wall clock.

docs.title: engine
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes The engine, for example vllm; equal to input.scenario.engine.kind when the scenario states it. version string yes The upstream release it models; equal to the release the scenario names.

docs.title: data
docs.text:
How the catalog and the registry reached the run (design §3.3). A content hash lists every data file as <sha256 of its bytes> <path relative to the directory>, sorts the lines by path, ends each with a line feed, and takes the SHA-256 of the result.

Key Type Required Meaning catalog mapping yes The catalog, below. registry mapping yes The registry, below. released_data boolean yes True only for a tagged simulator release, run on its substrate release's embedded data, with no overlay. Only such a run's figures are published. build string yes The simulator build: a release tag vX.Y.Z, or unreleased. Key Type Required Meaning source string yes embedded (compiled into the substrate) or path (a directory named on the command line or in the environment). hash string yes Content hash of the base data, 64 lowercase hex characters. overlays list no Each overlay applied, in order. combined_hash string yes Content hash after every overlay; equal to hash with none. Key Type Required Meaning hash string yes The overlay directory's content hash.

docs.title: selected_entries
docs.text:
The selected-entry report (VAL-6). It covers every reader behind the engine's environment, the acceptance and routing profile readers included. A candidate registry whose new entries no lookup selects shows them here as unread.

Key Type Required Meaning closeness_version integer no 2 when the recorder passed on everything each coefficient's entry states: its kernel_impls, measured_on, fit_range and ci95, the implementation it priced (priced, kernel_match) and the flags found from them. Version 2 added priced, kernel_match, measured_on and implementations; layer 10 is unreleased, so there was no version 1 in a release. It does not say the conditions were decided. Under 2, extrapolated is evaluated only for a coefficient that has a fit_range, unidentified only for one that has a ci95, and the kernel hash only for one that is exact; where that data is absent the entry did not state it, and an omitted flag is "not evaluated", not false. Absent when the recorder held only identities, when no coefficient was recorded, or in a report written before the data existed; then no coefficient carries the data, and nothing is said. A coefficient carrying the data under an absent version is refused. A reader of the older strict layout fails on the new keys. implementations mapping with closeness_version The kernel implementations the run's cost models ran, by the lowered primitive each executes (a word such as attention.prefill), each list once and sorted by library, variant and code hash: the pool's lowered implementations (VAL-8). An implementation the engine could not identify has no code_hash. Each coefficient's priced is the list of its primitive. coefficients list no Coefficients a lookup returned, once each, sorted by set, name, method, scope and kernel implementations. Two entries that differ only in the implementations they are valid for are two rows. acceptance_profiles list no Acceptance profiles a lookup returned, sorted by set and key. routing_profiles list no Routing profiles a lookup returned, sorted by set and key. unread_files list of strings no Registry files, relative and with forward slashes, from which no lookup returned an entry. Sorted; none of them is a selected entry's file. Key Type Required Meaning set string yes The coefficient set. name string yes The coefficient's name. method string yes One of the registry's methods. scope mapping yes The entry's scope, as written. file string yes The registry file it was read from. kernel_impls list no The kernel implementations the entry states it is valid for, copied from the entry: library, variant and code_hash, as in the coefficient entry. A reader maps each library version a benchmark run recorded to a kernel hash and compares it with these (design §11.3). Absent when the entry states none, and the hash of such an entry cannot be compared: a primitive priced from a vendor_spec, roofline, assumed or not_charged entry, which states none, has no hash to compare. This is the entry's validity list, which can name builds the run did not run; the build it priced is priced. primitive string no The lowered primitive the coefficient's name prices (coefficient.PrimitiveOf); absent for a name that prices no lowered kernel. Required for an exact coefficient. priced list with kernel_impls The implementations of the operations that read the coefficient, with library, variant and code_hash: what the engine lowered those operations to, matched whole by all three (VAL-8). The operations that read an entry are those of the primitive its name prices, narrowed to its kind where the name states one (attention_decode_rate_swa is read only by the sliding-window layers). An exact entry is used only when it lists every implementation among them, so priced is a subset of implementations[primitive] and of kernel_impls. A sibling build the entry is also valid for, an implementation of another primitive, and a kernel that runs only operations the entry is not read by, are not here. A reader compares the hash of each library version a benchmark run recorded with these (design §11.3, G1). Two pools that ran different builds of an entry valid for both list both. kernel_match string with closeness_version exact when the entry lists an implementation that ran, unkeyed when it lists none and so applies to every build without having been shown to match the one that ran. The kernel hash is decided only for an exact coefficient; an unkeyed one leaves it unevaluated. The kernel's own assumptions (for example trtllm_gen_prefill_lane) are not coefficients, are not in this list, and carry an empty match in the cost model's provenance. measured_on list no The implementations a transferred value was measured on, copied from the entry. Evidence about where the value came from, never a match. Only for transferred. fit_range list no The range of inputs the entry's fit covered (design VAL-10), copied from the entry: a dim, low and high per dimension. Absent when the entry records none, and the extrapolation condition cannot then be evaluated for it. extrapolated boolean no True when a step the run priced read the entry outside fit_range. The cost model sets it from the trust verdict of each priced step, and the report reads it when the Result is written, so it covers the steps priced up to then; nothing in the Result says the run had finished. Requires fit_range. ci95 list no The entry's 95% interval [low, high], copied from the entry. Absent when the entry states none, and the identifiability condition cannot then be evaluated for it. unidentified boolean no True when the entry's data do not determine it: its 95% interval is unbounded or wider than half its value (design VAL-10). Known when the cost model is built. Requires ci95.

Where an entry does not record a kernel implementation, a fit range or an interval, the Result says so by leaving the key out, and a grader treats the condition it would decide as not evaluated rather than as met (design §11.3). In the committed registry most measured entries state none of the three, so most coefficients are not evaluated until the registry records them.

Key Type Required Meaning set string yes The profile set. key string yes The profile's key, as Key.String renders it. file string yes The registry file it was read from.

docs.title: input
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning scenario mapping yes The scenario, resolved. deployment mapping yes The deployment, resolved, checked against the scenario's cluster. packaging mapping unless the scenario states gpus_per_node The cluster's packaging as the run resolved it, with the source of each value (SIM-10). policy mapping no The simulator's policy bundle, verbatim, when one was given. options list no Every option that changes a byte of the Result (SIM-10), sorted by name. workload_properties list no Each workload property and what supplied it (D8), sorted by name. Key Type Required Meaning gpus_per_node integer yes GPUs per node the run simulated, at least 1. Equal to the scenario's gpus_per_node when it states one. gpus_per_node_source string yes stated (the scenario, for a chip whose entry leaves it open) or catalog (the chip's entry). gpus_per_rack integer no GPUs per rack, a multiple of gpus_per_node. Omitted when the chip has no rack tier. gpus_per_rack_source string with gpus_per_rack catalog: only a chip's entry states a rack. Key Type Required Meaning name string yes The flag without its dashes, or the environment variable. value string yes The value the run used, as text. source string yes command_line, environment, or default.

A workload property is a quantity that depends on the request stream but that BLIS does not simulate, such as speculative acceptance or expert routing imbalance (D8).

Key Type Required Meaning name string yes The property, a lowercase slug. values mapping unless default The property's figures, by name. Finite. source string yes What supplied the values, highest precedence first: command_line, scenario, workload (stated by or derived from it), profile (the substrate's profile for the workload), default (none stated). profile string with profile The profile, as set and key. step string for a profile lookup that can borrow How the lookup found its value (D8): exact, same_drafter_other_k, other_drafter or other_target. differed list of strings with a borrowing step Each key field in which a borrowed profile differs from the run's: model, drafter, speculative_method or num_spec_tokens. None for exact. k_rule string with same_drafter_other_k How the borrowed value was brought to the run's K: interpolated, above_largest, below_smallest_rates or below_smallest_proportional. profiles list of strings with step Every profile the value was read from, as set and key, the one that sets it first; an interpolation lists both it lies between.

docs.title: frame
docs.text:
The experimental frame (design §8.6, DEV-7): what the run feeds in, when it measures, and what it measures.

Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes terminating (a fixed amount of work) or steady_state. generator mapping yes The input, below. initial_state mapping yes The engines' caches at the start, below. phases mapping yes Warm-up, measured window and drain, each by a rule. stop mapping yes The stop rule: a request count, a horizon, or both. acceptance list no The conditions under which the run counts for this frame. metrics list of strings yes The metric identifiers the frame measures, sorted. Key Type Required Meaning workload mapping one of these The workload binding the run used. load mapping one of these The offered load: a concurrency or a request rate, not both. seed integer yes The scenario seed every random substream derives from. rng string yes The random generator and its version, for example pcg64-sha256/1. Key Type Required Meaning caches string yes empty or warmed. rule string with warmed How the caches were warmed. Key Type Required Meaning warmup mapping yes The leading part excluded from measurement. measured mapping yes What opens and closes the measured window. drain mapping yes What the run does after the window closes. Key Type Required Meaning rule string yes none, requests, duration, marked (the workload marks warm-up requests) or mser5. requests integer with requests Leading requests excluded. Positive. duration_s number with duration Leading simulated seconds excluded. Positive. Key Type Required Meaning start string yes first_arrival_after_warmup, profiling_start or simulation_start. stop string yes last_completion, profiling_end or simulation_end. Key Type Required Meaning rule string yes none, until_complete or grace. duration_s number with grace The grace period in simulated seconds. Positive. Key Type Required Meaning requests integer one of these The most requests the generator emits. horizon_s number one of these The simulated time, in seconds, at which the run stops. Positive. Key Type Required Meaning condition string yes achieved_concurrency_within (a fraction of the target) or unfinished_fraction_at_most. threshold number yes The bound. Not negative. observed number yes What the run achieved. Not negative. met boolean yes Whether observed is at most threshold. A run with any condition unmet reports no metrics.

docs.title: revisions
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning simulator string yes The inference-sim build: a tag, a pseudo-version or a commit. substrate string yes The blis-substrate version the build selected. router string no The llm-d router fork's version. engine_module string no The engine repository's module version.

docs.title: rerun_of and revision_changes
docs.text:
A Result produced from another Result's input names it, and lists every component whose revision differs. Both are absent on a fresh run.

Key Type Required Meaning name string yes The other Result's name. sha256 string yes The other Result document's digest. Key Type Required Meaning component string yes A key of revisions, or catalog or registry for the data's combined hash; listed once. from string yes The other Result's value. to string yes This run's value; differs from from.

docs.title: window
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning start_us integer yes The window's start on the simulated clock, microseconds. end_us integer yes Its end; not before start_us. duration_s number yes end_us - start_us in seconds; positive when a rate is reported. requests integer yes Requests completed inside it; at most requests.completed.

docs.title: metrics
docs.text:
Each key is an identifier from the metric registry. The registry gives its formula, statistic, population, window and unit; the Result gives the value and states the figure's scope (design §8.7, DEV-8). A Result holds one figure of a metric, so a Result states no two scopes of one metric.

A figure with no scope is refused, not read as the whole cluster: a definition is never inferred (DEV-8), so a figure that does not say what it is a figure of cannot be compared. A figure is compared with another only when the metric, scope, member, aggregate and scope ranged over are all the same (metrics.ComparableFigures, or Basis.ComparableTo for the document form).

Key Type Required Meaning value number yes Finite and not negative; at most 1 for a fraction. samples integer yes The size of the population the statistic is over. Positive for a latency. scope string yes The scope the figure is at: cluster, pool or instance, one the metric is defined at. member string at the pool and instance scopes The pool or instance the figure is of, by the name the deployment gives it. A figure at the cluster scope has none. For an aggregate, the member of scope, not of over. aggregate string with over max or min, one the metric admits: the figure combines the figures of a narrower scope. Absent for a figure computed from the scope's own population. over string with aggregate The narrower scope the aggregate ranges over, one the metric is defined at.

docs.title: requests
docs.text:
Every request the generator created has exactly one fate (design §8.7, DEV-9). generated is the generator's own count, and equals the sum of the fates.

Key Type Required Meaning generated integer yes Requests the workload created, every planned session round included. completed integer yes Finished. dropped mapping no Dropped, by reason: admission_rejected, routing_rejected, encode_routing_rejected, gateway_queue_rejected, gateway_evicted, gateway_expired, unservable, context_overflow, decode_kv_unavailable. Each count positive. timed_out integer yes Cancelled by the client's timeout. in_flight_at_horizon integer yes Running when the run stopped. queued_at_horizon integer yes Waiting when the run stopped. not_started integer yes Planned, such as a later session round, but never issued. length_capped integer yes Completed requests that stopped at a length limit. Not a fate.

docs.title: request_rows
docs.text:
One row per generated request, replacing the --metrics-path and --results-path files. Times are on the simulated clock in microseconds. A latency is present only where the request produced the sample: a request that emitted no token has no ttft_us; only a completed request with at least two output tokens has tpot_us; only a completed request has e2e_us. The rows' fates agree with requests.

Key Type Required Meaning id string yes The request's identifier, never reused in a run. fate string yes completed, dropped, timed_out, in_flight_at_horizon, queued_at_horizon or not_started. drop_reason string with dropped A reason from requests.dropped. arrival_us integer yes Arrival at the client. ttft_us integer when sampled Time to first token. tpot_us number when sampled (E2E - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1). e2e_us integer when sampled Request latency; at least ttft_us. scheduling_delay_us integer no Arrival at an engine to the first scheduled step. gateway_queue_delay_us integer no Time in the router's flow-control queue. completion_index integer completed The 1-based position in the run's order of completion. prompt_tokens integer yes Prompt tokens. cached_local_tokens integer no Prompt tokens served from the engine's own cache. cached_external_tokens integer no Prompt tokens served from an external cache tier. computed_tokens integer no Prompt tokens the engine computed. output_tokens integer yes Tokens emitted. length_capped boolean no Completed at a length limit. phase string no warmup, profile or grace, when the workload marks phases. instance string no The engine instance that served it. model string no The model tag. adapter string no The LoRA adapter. slo_class string no The SLO class. tenant_id string no The tenant. session_id string no The session. round_index integer no The round within the session. agentic mapping no The request's place in an agentic replay, below. Key Type Required Meaning lane integer yes The concurrency lane. tree integer yes The tree instance. trace_id string yes The corpus trace the tree replays. stream string yes The conversation. kind string yes root, subagent or flat. stream_instance integer yes The stream's instance within the run. turn integer yes The turn within the stream. outcome string no How the load generator would record it.

docs.title: goodput
docs.text:
The figures goodput_rps and slo_attainment are metrics; this block holds the targets and each class's counts.

Key Type Required Meaning targets mapping yes SLO targets by class, as in a trace header. per_class mapping no The outcome per class; every key is a class of targets. Key Type Required Meaning completed integer yes Completed requests of the class. met integer yes Those that met the class's targets; at most completed.

docs.title: breakdowns
docs.text:
per_model, per_tenant and per_adapter restate reported metrics over each key's requests, so each of their names is a key of metrics. pd and sessions name quantities of their own.

Key Type Required Meaning pd mapping no The prefill/decode split of a disaggregated run. per_model mapping no By model. per_tenant mapping no By tenant. per_adapter mapping no By LoRA adapter. sessions mapping no Over multi-turn sessions.

docs.title: reports
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning engine mapping no Reported by the engine, keyed by pool role. router mapping no Reported by the embedded router. kernel mapping no Reported by the cost model, keyed by pool role. saturation mapping no The post-hoc saturation report, when detectors ran.

A report's numbers are not figures under the registry. A consumer that ranks or compares a number reads it from metrics.

docs.title: overrides
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning setting string yes The setting simulated differently. input string no The value input states. run string no The value the run simulated. source string yes What chose it, for example a command-line flag.

docs.title: resolutions
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning setting string yes The setting. The name an overrides entry uses for the same setting. pool string no The pool that resolved it, below. Absent for the whole deployment, or a deployment with one pool. host string no The value the host gave the engine: the host's value when overrides names this setting, else the input's. Absent when the host gave none and the engine chose one. engine string yes The value the engine resolved to, and the run simulated. reason string when it differs Why engine differs from host. Only where they differ.

Resolutions are listed once each, sorted by setting and then pool. A pool is named by its role (colocated, prefill or decode), and, when several pools share a role, by the role and the pool's position among those of that role, counted from zero (decode-0, decode-1); result.PoolLabels gives the names. A scenario names no pool, so the position in pools is the only identity a pool has. A prefill and a decode pool resolve the same setting differently, and each states its own.

An override is what the host changed; a resolution is what the engine then did with the value it was given. Design §11.2 grades a benchmark point G2 when a resolved value the run logged differs from the engine's resolution of the value passed, and this list is where the engine's resolution is read, beside the host's value. result.ResolutionsOf writes it from the cost model's own kernel.Resolution, and result.ResolutionsOfPool for one pool of several: the layout widths and modes, and each request the cost model declined.

The settings the cost model resolves, and what vLLM calls the request each answers:

setting engine value The vLLM setting it answers tensor_parallel_width the width, an integer tensor_parallel_size data_parallel_width the width, an integer data_parallel_size expert_parallel_width the width, an integer None: it is derived. With enable_expert_parallel on it is tensor, prefill-context and data-parallel width multiplied; with it off it is 1. all_reduce_backend custom or nccl disable_custom_all_reduce. The custom reduction runs unless disabled, and is declined where the group spans nodes without multi-node NVLink or has a rank count the kernel does not support. async_scheduling true or false async_scheduling, a tri-state request that the engine resolves. cascade_attention true or false The inverse of disable_cascade_attn: cascade attention is on when the request does not disable it and every gate allows it. sequence_parallel_moe true or false None: whether the MoE input is sequence-parallel, from the engine's rule or the model's own, so a request to change it is not a single setting.

A declined request is recorded under the setting it answers: the cost model's allreduce_backend request lands on all_reduce_backend, and its cache_dtype request on kv_cache_dtype, the engine's name. A request for another field is recorded under the name the cost model gives it, which is the engine's own setting name (for example quantization). The host column is empty for async_scheduling and cascade_attention unless the cost model declines a request for them, which the kernel does not do today.

docs.title: artifacts
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning ref string yes Path, relative to the Result document. sha256 string yes The file's digest. rows integer no Row count, for a table.

docs.title: runtime
docs.text:
Determinism and round-trip comparisons skip this block, and nothing else.

Key Type Required Meaning wall_clock_s number no Wall-clock seconds the run took. started_utc string no When it started, RFC 3339 in UTC, ending Z. host mapping no Host facts, for example os and arch.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Validate(Bundle{Result: r}) checks the Result field by field, the input it embeds included. Engine rules do not run on that embedded input: pass &r.Input.Scenario and &r.Input.Deployment as the bundle's Scenario and Deployment to rule-check it. With Rules set, a Result and no Scenario, the rule layer warns (result-input-rules).

Source: spec/result.

docs.title: Router table
docs.text:
An entry of the router table maps one router BLIS does not host, in one mode, to the policy of llm-d's router that stands closest to it, with the evidence for the match (design §11.3 and §11.4).

The entries are in the catalog, as routers/<name>.yaml, and the catalog reference shows them. LoadRouterEntry reads one strictly, and Entry.Validate checks it. The name is the file's stem and is not a key of the file.

routers/dynamo-round-robin.yaml
# Dynamo's frontend in its round-robin mode, which it runs when its configuration sets none.
# The entry maps the mode to llm-d's round-robin policy and says exactly how the two differ and
# how far the choice of policy moves BLIS's figures. Every citation is a line of a router's own
# code at the commit named, or of llm-d's router at the commit the module tag v1.0.0-blis.3 of
# inference-sim/llm-d-router points to. The bound is measured on BLIS only (see the guide
# contracts/guides/router-sensitivity.md); it is a sensitivity, not an error against Dynamo.
kind: RouterMapping
router: dynamo
mode: round-robin
revisions:
  - 1682167d3c97f0fc8cd405dee51f17288eeaeb55
policy: round-robin
reason: >-
  Dynamo's round-robin mode rotates strictly per request: it takes the next value of a counter
  and indexes the list of available workers by it, so successive requests go to successive
  workers and every worker gets the same number to within one. llm-d's round-robin policy does
  not rotate: it is the max-score picker with no scorer, every endpoint is tied, and the picker
  chooses among the tied endpoints at random (the hosted scheduler shuffles the candidates before
  each pick), as the random picker does. Neither reads load, so neither reacts to a worker that
  falls behind, and over a run both spread requests over every endpoint. They differ in the
  order: Dynamo's is a cycle and llm-d's is a random draw. The nearest llm-d policy picks at
  random among tied endpoints, and the random picker is equally close, so the first group of the
  bound is against it. How far the choice of policy moves BLIS's figures is the bound: small for
  time per output token and for throughput in most of the regime, large for time to first token
  at 64 to 256 clients when the alternative reads load. An earlier version of this entry held
  that no policy was close enough because llm-d's counter, drawn at every pick of every profile,
  would give a prefill pool of even size every other endpoint. The router's own tests and BLIS
  runs do not show it (the pool-balance difference), and the argument is not made here.
difference:
  - aspect: strict-rotation
    text: >-
      Dynamo rotates strictly per request (push_router.rs 357-372): the n-th request goes to the
      instance at n modulo the number of available instances. The nearest llm-d policy picks at
      random among tied endpoints: the max-score picker rotates the tied candidates by a counter,
      but they reach it in a seeded random order in a hosted runtime, so the choice is uniformly
      random, and tests of pools of two, three and four reach every endpoint in near equal counts
      and not in a cycle. The router has no policy that rotates strictly. The random picker is
      equally close, and the first group of the bound is against it. These statements are about
      inference-sim/llm-d-router at commit 03246be994224ef031dfdafb966c54f60d01e933 and no other
      release; the policy list states none of them.
    evidence: [1, 8, 9, 10]
  - aspect: frontends
    text: >-
      A Dynamo deployment can run several frontend processes, each with router objects and
      counters of its own that start at zero, so the sequence of requests a worker sees
      interleaves independent rotations; the recipes the dashboard read run several
      (enable_multiple_frontends). BLIS hosts one router and picks at random among tied endpoints. Which frontend a request reaches is the load
      balancer's choice and is not modelled.
    evidence: [2]
  - aspect: pool-balance
    text: >-
      Under llm-d's policy a prefill pool is used in full, as the random choice among tied
      endpoints gives. With a workload that saturates
      the prefill pool (8,192 prompt tokens, 16 output tokens), round-robin served 25.3 to 27.0
      requests per second at 16 to 1,024 clients with two prefill endpoints, against 27.1 to 27.3
      under least-active-requests and 13.6 with one prefill endpoint; with four it served 46.3 to
      53.3 against 53.6 to 54.4. A pool used through one endpoint would give about half. The
      14 percent gap at four endpoints and 16 clients is also seen under the random picker and
      the default policy, so it is the arrival imbalance of a policy that ignores load.
      BLIS does not record which prefill endpoint served a request, so the
      mechanism is not confirmed. The tables are in the guide.
    evidence: [5, 6, 7, 8]
  - aspect: load-blind
    text: >-
      Neither mode reads load, so neither reacts to a worker that falls behind. A policy that
      does (least-active-requests, default, queue-scorer) is not this mode; the second group of
      ratios in the bound is what a wrong guess of the mode would cost.
    evidence: [1, 7]
bound:
  evidence:
    file: registry/docs/router-sensitivity/runs.csv
    sha256: f54dad99e89c657fb03e9484c2699303754bb2e2750dbffcaf9c670ae8cd1ec2
    producer: inference-sim/inference-sim
    commit: 780f661ef9c18a2a9928acf8a63a67667cd597c0
    command: python3 -I registry/docs/router-sensitivity/sweep.py --blis <blis built from the commit> --work <scratch directory> --out runs.csv
  ratios:
    - metric: ttft_p50_ms
      against: [random-picker]
      regime:
        workload: balanced
        concurrencies: [16, 64, 256, 1024]
        model: minimax-m2.5
        hardware: gb200-nvl72
        engine_version: "0.32.0"
        fabric: ib-400g
        prefill: {tp: 1, pp: 1, dp: 1, expert_parallel: false}
        decode: {tp: 4, pp: 1, dp: 1, expert_parallel: true}

    - metric: tpot_p50_ms

        model: minimax-m2.5

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always RouterMapping. router string yes The router the run was measured behind, in lower case, for example dynamo. Never llm-d, which BLIS hosts. mode string yes The router's mode or algorithm as the run's configuration names it. When the configuration sets none, the mode the router's code defaults to, and a citation says so. session_affinity_ttl_s integer no The router's session-affinity idle timeout in seconds, when the configuration sets one. At least 1. Two runs that differ in it are different keys. revisions list of strings yes The builds of the router the run used for which the entry is established, each a full 40-character commit, sorted, each once. A mapping is a claim about the behaviour of a build, so an entry shown for one build is not inherited by another with the same mode: a run on a build not listed has no mapping and stays router_unsupported (design §11.4). Every router-side citation is at one of them, and each has a citation for the mode and one for the policy. policy string yes A policy llm-d's router offers, or none. reason string yes What the router's mode and the policy do alike and differently; for none, why no policy is close enough. difference list for a policy other than none; else no Each way the mode and the policy differ, one statement per aspect, each citing the code that shows it, below. bound mapping for a policy other than none; else no How far the choice of policy moves each figure on BLIS, measured, with its regime and evidence, below. evidence list yes Citations of both routers' code or documentation, below.

The key of an entry is the router, the mode and the session-affinity setting. The entry's file is named <router>-<mode>, with -affinity-<seconds> when the setting is set, and the validator refuses another name, so one key cannot be stated by two files, in a catalog or in an overlay.

docs.title: Lookup by revision
docs.text:
routertable.Resolve (and Data.LookupRouter) takes the router, the mode, the session-affinity setting and the router build the run used, and returns the entry with one of four outcomes. mapped: the entry covers the build and names a policy; only this scores the point, at G2 (router_differs). no_policy: it covers the build and says no policy is close enough. revision_not_covered: an entry has the key and does not list the build, so what it shows is not shown for this one. no_entry: no entry has the key. The last three are G5 router_unsupported. A point that relies on an entry carries the build it used in the revision of its router_differs, and Data.CheckRouterSubstitutions refuses one whose entry is missing, is another router's, does not cover the build, or maps to another policy.

The committed dynamo-round-robin entry covers one build of Dynamo, commit 1682167d3c97f0fc8cd405dee51f17288eeaeb55 (26 April 2026), the build the April 2026 recipes pin. A run on a later Dynamo build stays router_unsupported until an entry cites it.

Policies:

round-robin · random-picker · least-active-requests · default · none

docs.title: evidence
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning side string yes Whose code it is, below. field string yes The field of the entry it supports, below. repository string yes <owner>/<name> on GitHub. On the llm-d side, llm-d/llm-d-router or inference-sim/llm-d-router; on the router side, not those. commit string yes The full 40-character commit the passage is read at. A branch or a tag is not a pinned revision. path string yes The file, from the repository's root. For a policy other than none, one llm-d citation shows the behaviour the policy is matched to, at the commit it names; the contract keeps no list of files. lines string yes A line number, or a range <first>-<last>, at commit. claim string yes What the passage shows.

Sides:

router · llm-d

router The router the run used. llm-d llm-d's router. It supports the policy only.

Fields:

mode · session_affinity_ttl_s · policy

Each field the entry states has a citation (SUB-18): the router's own code for its mode and, when set, its session_affinity_ttl_s; and, for the policy, a passage of the router that shows the behaviour it is matched to and a passage of llm-d's router that shows the policy does it.

docs.title: difference
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning aspect string yes What differs, as a lower-case slug, for example counter, tie-break or scale. Each aspect once. text string yes How the router's mode and the policy differ in that aspect, and what BLIS does instead. It states a fact of the code, or says that an effect is not measured. evidence list of integers yes The positions (from 0) in the entry's evidence list of the citations the statement rests on. At least one, each once.

A point record carries the same statements without evidence, because a position means nothing outside the entry:

Key Type Required Meaning aspect string yes What differs, as above. text string yes How the router's mode and the policy differ in that aspect.

A mapping is a claim of nearness, so the entry says how near: every way the two differ that the code shows, and for each the passages that show it. A point scored with the entry copies the statements (without the positions, which mean nothing outside the entry) into its router_differs substitution.

docs.title: bound
docs.text:
A bound is a sensitivity, not an error. It says how far BLIS's own prediction of a figure moves when the policy changes, so it says what a wrong guess of the router's mode could cost. It does not say how far BLIS is from the router's real behaviour, which no run measured.

A bound is measured on BLIS, so it is a fact about the two policies and the workload, not about a build of the router. The entry states it once for every build in its revisions, as it states the differences, which are facts of the code at those builds. A difference or a bound that holds at one build only would need an entry of its own, which the key (router, mode, affinity) does not allow yet.

Key Type Required Meaning evidence mapping yes The measurement the ratios come from, below. ratios list yes The limits: at least one, each for one figure, one set of alternatives and one regime. not_measured list of strings yes What the bound does not cover, one sentence each. At least one: a bound that claims to cover everything is not a measured bound. Key Type Required Meaning file string yes The CSV of runs, from the repository's root. The ratios are recomputed from it. sha256 string yes The SHA-256 of the file, 64 lower-case hex digits, so a ratio cites the bytes it was read from. producer string yes <owner>/<name> of the repository BLIS was built from for the runs. commit string yes The full 40-character commit of the producer. command string yes The command that reproduces the file. Key Type Required Meaning metric string yes The metric registry identifier of the figure, for example ttft_p50_ms. against list of strings yes The alternatives the policy was compared with, each by the name of its plugin composition in the evidence file's policy column. Sorted, each once, none the entry's own policy. regime mapping yes Where the ratio was measured, below. max_ratio number yes The largest, over every cell of the regime and every alternative, of the larger of the two means over the smaller, each mean taken over the seeds. At least 1, rounded up to two decimals so it never understates. Key Type Required Meaning workload string yes The kind of workload, below. concurrencies list of integers yes The closed-loop client counts the cells ran, ascending, each once, each at least 1. A point matches only a count in the list: nothing is interpolated between two, because time to first token has a sharp knee between them. model string yes The catalog model the runs used. hardware string yes The catalog hardware the runs used. engine_version string yes The engine release the runs simulated, as the scenario's engine_version states it. fabric string yes The catalog network between the pools, the scenario's cluster.fabric. prefill mapping yes The parallelism of one prefill instance: tp, pp, dp (each at least 1) and expert_parallel. decode mapping yes The same for one decode instance. shapes list of strings yes The pool shapes the cells cover, each <n>P<m>D: n prefill and m decode instances. Sorted, each once.

docs.title: Regime of a point
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning workload string yes The workload kind of the point. concurrency integer yes Its closed-loop client count. At least 1. model string yes The catalog model it simulates. hardware string yes The catalog hardware. engine_version string yes The engine release the scoring simulator runs. fabric string yes The catalog network between the pools. shape string yes Its pool shape, <n>P<m>D. prefill mapping yes The parallelism of one prefill instance, as for a regime. decode mapping yes The same for one decode instance.

A router_differs substitution carries this regime, and the part of the entry's bound that covers it (Bound.For): load.Data.CheckRouterSubstitutions recomputes that part from the entry and refuses a bound that omits a covering ratio, carries one for another regime, or is carried for a point the entry has no bound for.

Key Type Required Meaning tp integer yes Tensor-parallel width of one instance. At least 1. pp integer yes Pipeline-parallel width. At least 1. dp integer yes Data-parallel width. At least 1. expert_parallel boolean yes Whether the instance splits its experts across its ranks.

Workload kinds:

balanced · prefill-bound · decode-bound

balanced Closed loop, every request 1,024 prompt tokens and 1,024 output tokens, no prefix shared between requests. prefill-bound Closed loop, 8,192 prompt tokens and 16 output tokens. decode-bound Closed loop, 256 prompt tokens and 2,048 output tokens.

A regime is exact. Entry.BoundFor takes the point's workload, client count, model, hardware, engine release, fabric, instance layouts and pool shape and returns the ratios whose regime contains all of them; with none, the outcome is regime_not_covered and the point stays router_unsupported with the reason "no bound for this regime". A point record that carries a router bound whose regime does not list the point's client count is refused. The ratios are the sensitivity of BLIS's own figures to the choice of policy, not the error of standing a policy in for the router.

The list is closed because a bound is a statement about the workloads it names and no others: a kind joins it with the measurement that covers it. How the ratios are measured, how to reproduce them and what they leave out is in the router sensitivity guide.

docs.title: What the validator refuses
docs.text:
An entry with no evidence; one that lacks a citation for a field it states, or for either router's side of the policy; a policy llm-d's router does not offer; a none or a match with no reason; the router llm-d; an llm-d citation of another repository, a router citation of llm-d's, or an llm-d citation that names no file defining the policy; a file name that is not the entry's key; no revisions, a revision that is not a full commit, repeated or out of order, a router citation at a commit that is not one of the revisions, and a revision with no router citation of its own for the mode or the behaviour; a citation whose commit is not a full commit, whose path climbs out of the repository or whose lines run backward; a citation repeated.

For a policy other than none: no difference; an aspect that is empty, not a slug or stated twice; a statement with no text or no citation, or one that names a position outside the evidence list or names one twice; no bound; a bound with no ratios, no not_measured, a file path that climbs, a hash that is not 64 lower-case hex digits, a producer that is not <owner>/<name>, a commit that is not a full commit or no command; a ratio whose metric is not in the metric registry, that names no alternative or its own policy, whose alternatives are unsorted or repeated, whose value is not a finite number of at least 1 with two decimals, whose workload is not a kind above, whose client counts are empty, below 1 or not ascending, whose model, hardware, engine release, fabric or either instance layout is missing, whose shapes are missing, malformed or unsorted; a ratio stated twice for one regime. For none: a difference or a bound, because there is no stand-in policy to differ from or to bound. The catalog's tests also recompute every ratio from the evidence file and refuse one that is not the file's.

docs.title: Routing profiles
docs.text:
Expert-parallel routing imbalance: how unevenly a mixture-of-experts router loads the ranks of an expert-parallel group. It depends on the model's router and on the traffic, so, like acceptance, it is a profile keyed by model and workload category, hosted under routing/ in the registry, which a workload, a scenario or a command line may override.

The quantity is vLLM's own. In v0.31.0 a step's load on rank r in layer l is the routed (token, expert) assignments landing on r's experts (vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py:601-608), and vLLM logs balancedness as sum_l mean_r / sum_l max_r (:66-71). The token imbalance is its reciprocal, at least 1. Each layer's combine waits for its slowest rank, so the layer pays the busiest rank's routed compute. The expert imbalance is the busiest rank's distinct experts touched over the per-rank count under uniform routing, which scales a weight-bound decode read and may be below 1. Curves describe vLLM's default linear placement with EPLB off.

Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always RoutingProfileSet. name string yes The set's identity, by convention its file name. role string yes default, consulted for every run its keys match, or sensitivity, used only when a scenario names it. caveats list of strings no How far the values travel. profiles list yes At least one profile, below. Two with one key are an error. Key Type Required Meaning model string yes The catalog model name. category string yes The workload category, spelled as for acceptance. phase string yes decode (tokens mixed across requests) or prefill (a chunk of one request). placement string yes linear, the only placement described. expert_parallel integer yes The width the curve is for. At least 2. points list yes The curve, by strictly increasing batch_tokens. method string yes One of the methods except not_charged and calibrated. provenance mapping unless method is assumed Where the routes came from, below. rationale string unless method is measured The reasoning behind a value that was not measured. Key Type Required Meaning batch_tokens integer yes Tokens in the step. A lookup interpolates in log(batch) and holds the end values outside the curve. token_imbalance number yes Busiest-rank routed tokens over the mean. At least 1. expert_imbalance number yes Busiest-rank distinct experts over the uniform-routing count. Positive. token_p10 number no The step-to-step 10th percentile of the token imbalance. token_p90 number no The 90th percentile. Not below token_p10. Key Type Required Meaning source string yes The dataset the routes were read from, with its revision. derivation string no The script and output digest. hardware string no The chip the routes were captured on. A resolution on other hardware records it. engine string no The engine build. requests integer no How many requests the routes cover. tier integer no The source's reputation tier, 1 or 2.

docs.title: Inline values
docs.text:
A workload's routing, a scenario's routing.value and a command line's value. Flat in the step size.

Key Type Required Meaning token_imbalance number yes At least 1. 1 is evenly loaded. expert_imbalance number no Positive. Omitted, 1. source string no Where the value came from, recorded with the resolution.

docs.title: Scenario pin
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning profiles string one of two A routing-profile set under routing/ in the registry, default or sensitivity. A set without the run's key is refused. value mapping one of two An inline value, above. fallback_category string no With profiles, the category whose curves to use when the workload's has none. The substitution is recorded. Not with value.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: routing.Resolve picks the highest layer that states an imbalance: the command line, the scenario's pin, the workload's value, then the registry's default-role sets for (model, category, phase, linear, width). With none, or without expert parallelism, or with EPLB on and no pin, the run is priced as evenly loaded and the resolution records why. A registry miss is not an error; a scenario's named set that misses is.

docs.title: Engine rules
docs.text:
An engine release's rules hold what that release accepts and what it refuses. They live with the engine model that owns the release, and a validator passes them in for the release a scenario's engine_version names (Bundle.Rules). This schema registers none of its own.

Rules run after the field layer passes and read the scenario, the deployment and the model graph together. Each problem names the rule that reported it. A rule that reports an error describes a deployment the engine would refuse at startup, or one a cost model would price with the wrong constants. A rule that reports a warning describes one the engine would run differently from what the document suggests, or a name the engine may accept from an out-of-tree plugin.

A pool's engine block is opaque to this schema. The release's rules open it and check it (EngineRules.CheckEngineBlock), in the field layer, at the block's paths below deployment.pools[i].engine.

Three problems come from no release's rules:

engine-rules-given error. The bundle has a scenario but no engine rules were given. Nothing checked its engine blocks or its version-specific rules, so it does not pass. engine-version-known warning. The rules given know no release of the scenario's engine_version. Field validation passed, but no version-specific rule ran. engine-version-matches error. The rules given answered for a release other than the scenario's. No rule was applied.

For vLLM the rules packs, their constants and their reference are blis-vllm's (rules/v0_*).

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
The problem a run is given: a model, the cluster it may use, the traffic it serves, the coefficient sets that price it, and the engine release it runs. Everything in it is fixed for the run. It names catalog and registry entries rather than containing them.

kind: Scenario
name: deepseek-v3-on-h200
model: deepseek-v3
coefficients:
  - cost-model-primitives
  - cost-model-collectives
  - cost-model-host-overheads
  - cost-model-attention
  - cost-model-recurrent
engine:
  kind: vllm
  version: "0.29.0"
workload:
  shape: summarization
cluster:
  hardware: h200
  fabric: ib-400g
  nodes: 4
  gpus_per_node: 8
  storage:
    - cpu_dram

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always Scenario. name string yes The scenario's identity. model string yes A model directory under models/ in the catalog. coefficients list of strings yes Coefficient sets in the registry, named by file, at least one. How a cost model combines them is under Selecting an entry. engine mapping yes, or engine_version The engine that runs the scenario, below. The simulator chooses the engine by it and refuses a release it does not run. engine_version string no Deprecated; replaced by engine, and removed in M4. A scenario may state it alone, or beside engine with the same version. workload mapping no The traffic, as a shape, a trace or a replay. See Workload. Omitted for a question about capacity alone. routing mapping no Pins expert-parallel routing imbalance for the run, by a routing-profile set in the registry or an inline value. See Scenario pin. Omitted, the workload and the registry's default sets decide, else evenly loaded. acceptance mapping no Pins speculative acceptance for the run, by a profile set in the registry or an inline value. See Scenario pin. Omitted, the workload and the registry decide. cluster mapping yes The hardware available, below.

docs.title: engine
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes The engine, as its repository registers it: vllm or sglang. version string yes The upstream release the engine models, such as 0.32.0. Selects the rules pack.

docs.title: cluster
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning hardware string yes A chip under hardware/ in the catalog. Every node carries it. fabric string if nodes > 1 A fabric under networks/ in the catalog. Cross-node cost comes from it. nodes integer yes Node count, at least 1. gpus_per_node integer unless the chip states it GPUs per node, at least 1. Required when the chip's entry states no GPUsPerNode; otherwise omit it or state the entry's value. See Packaging. gpus_per_rack integer no GPUs per rack, an NVLink domain that spans nodes. Only a chip's entry states a rack: omit it or state the entry's GPUsPerRack. See Packaging. switch_groups list of lists of integers no A partition of the nodes 0 to nodes - 1 into the groups that sit under one leaf switch, each group a list of node numbers. Needs uplink_oversubscription. See Switch groups. uplink_oversubscription number with switch_groups The ratio r of a group's aggregate NIC rate to its uplink's rate, at least 1. Refused without switch_groups. storage list of strings no Storage classes from the catalog's devices/storage.yaml that the cluster provides. If any are listed, a deployment's offload tiers must use them.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
A cluster's packaging is the GPUs in one node and in one rack. A rack is an NVLink domain that spans nodes, priced at the chip's IntraRackBwGBps. Two documents own the two values:

Value Owner when the chip's product fixes it Owner otherwise GPUs per node the chip's catalog entry, GPUsPerNode (GB200 NVL72: 4) the scenario, gpus_per_node (an HGX H100 server: 8) GPUs per rack the chip's catalog entry, GPUsPerRack (GB200 NVL72: 72) nobody: the chip has no rack tier

Cluster.Packaging(chip) resolves the two against the chip's entry, and every reader calls it: the cost model, the engines' placement, the deployment-fit checks and the Result's input.packaging. A field the scenario omits takes the entry's value. A field it restates unchanged is accepted. Any other value is refused, with a message naming the field, both values and the entry. The resolved packaging records each value's source, stated or catalog.

A scenario's gpus_per_rack on a chip whose entry states no GPUsPerRack is refused. Such a chip has no rack tier at all: the entry may not state IntraRackBwGBps without GPUsPerRack, and the cost model prices a rack only from the entry. A different NVLink domain is a different product, and needs its own catalog entry.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A scenario is invalid if

  • kind is not Scenario, or name or model is empty;
  • it states neither engine nor engine_version; engine lacks kind or version; or both are stated and engine_version differs from engine.version;
  • coefficients is empty;
  • cluster.hardware is empty, nodes is less than 1, or gpus_per_node or gpus_per_rack is negative;
  • gpus_per_rack and gpus_per_node are both set and the first is not a multiple of the second;
  • the cluster has more than one node and names no fabric;
  • switch_groups has an empty group, names a node twice (switch_group_overlap), names a node the cluster does not have (switch_group_unknown_node), leaves a node out (switch_group_missing_node), or is stated for a one-node cluster; uplink_oversubscription is missing with groups, not a finite number, not positive, below 1, or stated without groups (each refused under its own rule name);
  • a storage entry is empty or appears twice;
  • workload is present and is not a valid binding.
  • acceptance is present and is not a valid pin.

Whether the names resolve is checked by ValidateAgainstCatalog, not by Validate; see Validation.

The packaging checks need the chip's entry, so Validate does not run them. They run in Cluster.Packaging, which ValidateAgainstCatalog, the bundle validator given a Chip, and the kernel call. A cluster is refused there if

  • gpus_per_node is stated and differs from the entry's GPUsPerNode;
  • gpus_per_rack is stated and differs from the entry's GPUsPerRack;
  • gpus_per_node is omitted and the entry states no GPUsPerNode;
  • gpus_per_rack is stated and the entry states no GPUsPerRack.

A bundle with a deployment and no Chip is refused when the scenario omits gpus_per_node, since the deployment's fit to the cluster could not be checked.

Source: spec/scenario.

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text:
Each substrate release publishes the JSON Schema of every document that crosses a repository boundary (SUB-19), generated from the Go types.

Document Schema Go type scenario contracts/schema/scenario.schema.json scenario.Scenario deployment contracts/schema/deployment.schema.json deployment.Deployment result contracts/schema/result.schema.json result.Result point-record contracts/schema/point-record.schema.json pointrecord.Record workload contracts/schema/workload.schema.json workload.Spec trace contracts/schema/trace.schema.json trace.Header, with the data row as $defs.trace.Record

go run ./tools/schemagen writes them; TestPublishedSchemasMatchTheTypes fails when a committed schema differs from the types. A key is required in a schema exactly when its reference table marks it required, every object refuses keys its type does not declare, and every closed vocabulary is an enum read from the Go constants. The package contracts/schema embeds the files, so blis schema <document> prints the schema of the substrate release the build pins.

A schema states structure: keys, types and vocabularies. The Go validators state the rest, such as that the fates sum to generated. blis schema validate <document> <file> runs them, and an application validates every document it reads or writes with it, not with the schema alone.

docs.title: Trace
docs.text:
A request stream on disk: a YAML header and a CSV of one row per request. blis run --trace-output and blis replay write one, blis convert writes one from another tool's capture, and blis replay reads one. A scenario binds a trace by path, with its header.

trace.ReadHeader and trace.ReadRecords read the two files strictly; trace.Read reads both and validates them together. trace.WriteHeader and trace.WriteRecords write them, and return the writer's error.

trace header
trace_version: 4
time_unit: microseconds
mode: generated
workload_seed: 42
goodput_slo_targets:
  critical:
    ttft_ms: 500
    itl_ms: 50
max_nodes_spanned: 2
router:
  epp_flags:
    - --pool-name=llama
  seed: 42
trace data
request_id,client_id,tenant_id,slo_class,session_id,round_index,prefix_group,prefix_length,streaming,input_tokens,output_tokens,text_tokens,image_tokens,audio_tokens,video_tokens,reason_ratio,model,deadline_us,arrival_time_us,first_chunk_time_us,last_chunk_time_us,status,think_time_us
0,chat,t1,critical,s0,0,sys,256,true,512,128,512,0,0,0,0,,0,0,182000,2904000,ok,
1,chat,t1,critical,s0,1,sys,256,true,64,96,64,0,0,0,0,,0,3100000,3290000,5410000,ok,200000
2,chat,t2,critical,s1,0,,0,true,1024,256,1024,0,0,0,0,,300000000,120000,0,0,incomplete,

Version 4 is the format inference-sim wrote as version 3, without what only the removed blis observe command wrote: the real mode; the header keys created_at, warm_up_requests, workload_spec, server, network and observed_kv_metrics; and the columns vllm_priority, x_request_id, server_input_tokens, send_time_us, num_chunks, error_message and finish_reason. It adds the mode converted.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning trace_version integer yes Always 4. time_unit string yes Unit of the data file's timestamp columns. One of the time units. mode string yes generated (blis run), replayed (blis replay) or converted (blis convert, from another tool's capture). workload_seed integer no The workload generator's seed. A seed of 0 is a real seed, distinct from absence. session_context_growth string no accumulate: each session round's input is the previous round's input and output, then its new tokens. Omitted, rounds are drawn independently. goodput_slo_targets mapping no Latency targets per SLO class, keyed by class name, below. Class names are free. kv_offload mapping no The resolved KV-cache offload configuration of the run that wrote the trace, below. max_nodes_spanned integer no The most nodes one instance occupied, when more than one. A replay refuses a trace it cannot reproduce. router mapping no The llm-d router inputs the run routed with, below.

A generated or replayed trace records a BLIS deployment, and a replay keeps its header authoritative: it does not add offload tiers or other deployment options the run did not have. A converted trace records none, so a replay takes them from the scenario and the command line (Header.RecordsDeployment, inference-sim #2067).

docs.title: goodput_slo_targets.<class>
docs.text:
Thresholds in milliseconds. Zero on a dimension leaves it unconstrained, but a class must constrain at least one.

Key Type Required Meaning ttft_ms number no Time to first token. Not negative. itl_ms number no Time per output token. Not negative. e2e_ms number no Request latency. Not negative.

docs.title: kv_offload
docs.text:
The resolved numbers, so a replay reproduces the run whatever its host's defaults are.

Key Type Required Meaning cpu_bytes_to_use integer yes Bytes of host memory for the CPU tier. per_block_bytes integer yes Bytes per KV block. block_size integer yes Tokens per block. blocks_per_chunk integer yes Blocks per transfer chunk. tokens_per_hash integer yes Tokens per prefix hash. eviction_policy string yes The CPU tier's eviction policy. offload_prompt_only boolean yes Whether only prompt blocks are offloaded. self_describing_kv_events boolean yes Whether KV events name their medium. secondary_tiers list no Tiers below the CPU tier, below. simple_cpu_offload boolean no vLLM's SimpleCPUOffloadConnector. lazy_offload boolean no Its lazy mode. Key Type Required Meaning type string yes The tier's type. root_dir string yes Its directory. n_read_threads integer yes Read threads. n_write_threads integer yes Write threads. locality string no Where the tier lives relative to the node. enable_kv_events boolean yes Whether it emits KV events. direct_io boolean yes Whether it uses direct I/O. device_class string no A label; the numbers below decide. read_bandwidth number yes Bytes per microsecond. write_bandwidth number yes Bytes per microsecond. base_latency number yes Microseconds. saturation_queue_depth integer yes Queue depth at saturation; 1 turns the ramp off. single_transfer_fraction number yes Fraction of bandwidth one transfer reaches; 1 turns the ramp off. capacity_bytes integer no Size; 0 is unbounded. latency_jitter_stddev number yes Standard deviation of latency jitter.

docs.title: router
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning epp_flags list of strings yes The router's flags, with its EndpointPickerConfig inlined as --config-text. manifests string no The Kubernetes manifests, as one YAML stream. pod_labels mapping no Extra labels on the engines' pods. gateway_latency_us integer no Gateway latency. scrape_jitter_us integer no Metrics-scrape jitter. kv_event_delay_us integer no KV-event delivery delay. seed integer no The router's seed.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
The first row names the columns; a reader finds them by name. The columns of Columns are required; those of OptionalColumns (slo_target_us, adapter, think_time_us, input_tokens_reset) are written only when some row carries one. Any other column is refused.

Key Type Required Meaning request_id integer yes Unique in the trace. client_id string yes The client that sent it; may be empty. tenant_id string yes The tenant; may be empty. slo_class string yes The SLO class; may be empty. session_id string yes The session; may be empty. round_index integer yes The round within the session, 0 first; each once per session. prefix_group string yes The shared prefix's group; may be empty. prefix_length integer yes Tokens of the group's prefix the prompt starts with. streaming boolean yes true or false. input_tokens integer yes Prompt tokens after the prefix; in an accumulating session, the round's new tokens. output_tokens integer yes Output tokens. text_tokens integer yes Text tokens of a multimodal prompt. image_tokens integer yes Image tokens. audio_tokens integer yes Audio tokens. video_tokens integer yes Video tokens. reason_ratio number yes The reasoning share of the output, in [0, 1]. model string yes The model tag; empty for the scenario's model. deadline_us integer yes Absolute deadline on the arrival origin; 0 is none; not before arrival_time_us. arrival_time_us integer yes Arrival. first_chunk_time_us integer yes First token delivered in the run that wrote the trace; 0 for none. last_chunk_time_us integer yes Last token delivered; not before the first. status string yes One of the trace statuses. slo_target_us integer no The request's TTFT target; 0 is none. adapter string no The LoRA adapter; empty for the base model. think_time_us integer no Recorded client think time before the round; an empty cell is not recorded, distinct from 0. input_tokens_reset integer no The recorded absolute input of a round whose context was compacted; empty on other rounds.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A header is invalid if trace_version is not 4; time_unit or mode is empty or not in its vocabulary (real is refused with a pointer to converted); session_context_growth is other than accumulate; an SLO class name is empty, a target negative or not finite, or a class sets no target; an offload number is negative or not finite; max_nodes_spanned is negative or 1; router has no flags; or a converted trace states kv_offload, max_nodes_spanned or router.

A record is invalid if a count or a time is negative, reason_ratio lies outside [0, 1], deadline_us precedes a non-zero arrival_time_us, the last chunk precedes the first, or status is unknown. A trace is invalid if a request_id repeats, or a session repeats a round.

Source: spec/trace.

docs.title: Vocabularies
docs.text:
Every enumerated key in a document accepts only the values listed here; an unrecognized value is an error. The kernel's own enumerations are listed at the end. The lists are generated from the Go constants, so they are the values the code accepts.

These vocabularies are fixed by the schema and do not change with an engine release. Values that do, such as backend names and cache dtypes, are listed with the rules pack for each release.

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
The unit of a coefficient's value.

dimensionless · us_per_layer · us_per_request · us_per_step · us_per_hop · bytes_per_us · bytes_per_rank · bytes_per_token · us_per_load · us_per_transfer · tokens · sm_count · us_per_token

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
How a coefficient's value was obtained. This is the field that keeps a measurement distinguishable from an estimate, so it is never inferred. The methods are ranked from most to least trusted (design 9.2), and a lookup that finds more than one entry uses the one with the smallest rank number.

measured · calibrated · transferred · literature · vendor_spec · roofline · assumed · not_charged

measured (rank 1) From a measurement of the thing it prices. The entry cites it. calibrated (rank 2) Back-solved through the cost model from end-to-end measured runs, and checked against held-out ones. The entry cites its runs as sources of kind measured_case and names the held-out metrics in validated. It is not derived, which is a catalog provenance: a figure computed from other catalog facts. transferred (rank 3) A value measured in another scope and carried to this one by a stated rule. The entry names the scope in transferred_from and the rule in transfer_rule. literature (rank 4) From a published result that was not independently reproduced. vendor_spec (rank 5) A datasheet figure: nominal, not achieved. roofline (rank 6) Derived from a datasheet peak by the roofline form, before any measurement exists. assumed (rank 7) A placeholder, or an estimate reached by reasoning. A careful estimate is still assumed; the reasoning goes in rationale. not_charged Deliberately zero, so that "no cost" can be told apart from "cost unknown". It has no rank.

measured, calibrated, literature and vendor_spec count as evidenced. That is a statement about the basis of a number, not its quality: a vendor figure is evidenced but nominal.

A price reports the least trusted effective rank among the coefficients it used. A lookup outside the range an entry's fit covered ranks no better than transferred, and an entry whose interval is unbounded or wider than half its value ranks as assumed.

docs.title: Rate bases
docs.text:
What a rate in bytes per microsecond measures. SUB-5 bounds a rate by the chip's datasheet memory bandwidth only where the rate is a memory rate.

memory · work

memory A rate at which a kernel reads or writes device memory. It cannot exceed the datasheet memory bandwidth. This is the default. work A rate over a quantity of work counted in bytes, such as a record counted once per query and key pair. It may exceed the memory bandwidth, and the entry's rationale says why.

docs.title: Measurement times
docs.text:
What a measured number includes (design VAL-9).

device · device_and_host

device Device time only. device_and_host Device time and the host issue time.

docs.title: Measurement executions
docs.text:
How the kernels ran when the number was measured.

captured · eager

captured From a captured graph. eager Launched one by one.

docs.title: Fit dimensions
docs.text:
The inputs of a priced step that a fit's data can have covered (design VAL-10). A lookup with an input outside the recorded range is extrapolated.

tokens · requests · context_tokens

docs.title: Scope keys
docs.text:
The dimensions along which a coefficient's validity is bounded. A coefficient's scope uses these as its keys.

hardware · tp · ep · nodes_spanned · model · fabric

docs.title: Source kinds
docs.text: discussion · publication · datasheet · model · vendor_doc · measured_case

docs.title: Source roles
docs.text: primary · supporting · upper_bound

docs.title: Provenances
docs.text:
Where a chip's or fabric's figures come from. vendor_spec is a datasheet figure; derived is one computed from datasheet figures by a step the datasheet does not state.

vendor_spec · derived

docs.title: Primitives
docs.text:
A node's op.

GEMM · GroupedGEMM · Attention · RecurrentUpdate · Elementwise · Gather · AllReduce · AllGather · ReduceScatter · All2All

docs.title: Dtypes
docs.text:
A graph's weight_dtype, and a node's weight_dtype and state_dtype. Only formats that change a byte count or a peak rate appear. nvfp4, mxfp4 and int4 are three different 4-bit formats, not spellings of one.

bf16 · fp16 · fp8 · nvfp4 · mxfp4 · int8 · int4 · fp32

docs.title: Attention kinds
docs.text:
An Attention node's kind. mla and sparse_mla store one latent vector per token, which is why their n_kv is 1. sparse_mla is attention by a sparse kernel over an explicit set of positions, bounded by a top-k (index_topk), a compressed stream (compress_ratio), a sliding window (window), or a combination: DeepSeek-V4.1's window-only layers run the same sparse FlashMLA kernel as its compressed ones.

gqa · mla · sparse_mla · swa

docs.title: Recurrent kinds
docs.text:
A RecurrentUpdate node's recurrent_kind.

mamba2 · kda · gdn

docs.title: Emit conditions
docs.text:
A node's emit. "", the empty value, means the node always exists, and is what an omitted emit reads as.

"" · tensor_parallel · expert_parallel · tensor_parallel_unless_sp_moe · sequence_parallel · tensor_parallel_unless_sequence_parallel · tensor_parallel_without_expert_parallel · expert_parallel_without_dispatch

tensor_parallel Present when the tensor-parallel width exceeds 1. expert_parallel Present when the expert-parallel width exceeds 1. tensor_parallel_unless_sp_moe Present when the tensor-parallel width exceeds 1 and the engine has not made the MoE input sequence-parallel. Under sequence-parallel MoE the reduction is replaced by a reduce-scatter and all-gather pair. sequence_parallel Present when the model's own sequence parallelism is on, as the rules pack decides it for global.architecture. DeepSeek-V4.1 then shards the residual stream by token and all-gathers each attention input, then reduce-scatters its output. tensor_parallel_unless_sequence_parallel Present when the tensor-parallel width exceeds 1 and the model's own sequence parallelism is off: the all-reduces sequence parallelism replaces.

The last two belong on collectives. Work runs in every layout, including tensor parallelism one, where neither condition holds, so a node stated twice, once under each, would vanish there. Work is stated once, with under_sequence_parallel for how the mode divides it. A non-collective node carrying either condition draws a warning.

A model that decides its own sequence parallelism never consults the engine-wide rule tensor_parallel_unless_sp_moe names, so its decoder-layer reductions, the MoE's included, use tensor_parallel_unless_sequence_parallel. DeepSeek-V4.1 passes its own flag to its MoE, and vLLM's FusedMoE then skips the final tensor-parallel all-reduce. The 0.31.0 rules pack reports the engine-wide condition on such a model as an error.

The condition holds on DeepSeek-V4's and V4.1's mega-MoE backend too. That backend requires expert parallelism, so it runs without the model's sequence parallelism only at tensor parallelism one or pipeline parallelism above one. There its routed experts combine over the expert-parallel group with no tensor-parallel all-reduce, and its shared expert, which fuses into the kernel only under sequence parallelism or tensor parallelism one, runs tensor-parallel and all-reduces its own output. So the layer still reduces one hidden-width tensor across tensor-parallel ranks, as on the default backend.

tensor_parallel_without_expert_parallel Present when the tensor-parallel width exceeds 1 and expert parallelism is off: a reduction an MoE layer needs only while its experts are sharded by tensor parallelism. expert_parallel_without_dispatch Present when expert parallelism is on, the tensor-parallel width exceeds 1, and the MoE layer dispatches no tokens: every rank holds every token, because the expert-parallel group is the tensor-parallel group, so the ranks' partial expert outputs combine by an all-reduce rather than an all-to-all.

A model whose MoE reduces a different tensor in each of those two modes states one collective under each. Muse Spark is the case: under tensor parallelism it all-reduces its top_k per-route rows before its post-expert norm, which is not linear in a partial sum; under expert parallelism only the combined output, at its latent width.

docs.text:

docs.title: Tensor-parallel layouts
docs.text:
A node's tp. An omitted tp leaves the layout to the cost model's inference. A GEMM accepts column, row and replicated; an Elementwise or Attention node accepts sharded and replicated. No other primitive accepts one.

"" · column · row · sharded · replicated

column The output width n splits across ranks. row The input width k splits across ranks. The partial sums are reduced by a collective the graph states separately. sharded The work splits across ranks with the heads or columns it operates on. replicated Every rank holds the whole weight and does the whole node for every token it holds.

docs.title: Sequence-parallel splits
docs.text:
A node's under_sequence_parallel: how it divides when the model's own sequence parallelism is on. An omitted value means the node runs as tp states, over every token the step schedules. It needs global.architecture, and a collective cannot carry it.

"" · token_sharded

token_sharded The node runs on its rank's shard of the step's tokens, ceil(tokens / tp) rows, because vLLM's sp_shard pads the count to a multiple of tp. A GEMM, Elementwise or Attention node then holds its whole weight, whatever tp states: a column or row split needs every rank to hold the same rows. A GroupedGEMM's experts stay divided as expert parallelism decides, and a Gather's table as its shard states.

tp alone can't say this. Under DeepSeek-V4.1's sequence parallelism the residual stream is sharded by token, and only attention runs on the gathered stream, between its all-gather and its reduce-scatter. mHC, before the gather, and the fused q/kv A-projection, after it, are both replicated, yet the first sees 1/tp of the tokens and the second all of them. Engram's wkv is column-split without the mode and replicated with it, and runs at tensor parallelism one too. It is one node, tp: column with under_sequence_parallel: token_sharded.

docs.title: Cache kinds
docs.text:
A cache's kind, which decides how it grows.

kv · index · window · state

kv Keys and values, or a latent: one entry per tokens_per_entry context tokens. index A sparse-attention indexer's key cache. It grows like kv. window A sliding-window ring, bounded by window tokens per request. state Fixed per-request state, entries entries for the request's lifetime.

docs.title: Gather residency
docs.text:
A Gather node's residency, and the engine setting that can change it, its residency_control. An omitted residency means device; an omitted residency_control means no setting moves the table.

device · host

"" · engram_cpu_offload

engram_cpu_offload vLLM's Engram cpu_offload. A deployment sets it with engine.engram_config.cpu_offload. The graph states the residency the engine gives the table when the deployment leaves it alone, which is a release fact: under 0.31.0 it is host, and that pack's engram-residency-default rule checks it.

docs.title: Gather shards
docs.text:
A Gather node's shard. An omitted shard means replicated.

replicated · rows · heads

rows The rows split evenly across ranks, and each token's row is read on the rank that holds it. vLLM's vocabulary embedding works this way. heads The table is rows_per_token sub-tables, one per hash head, split across S shards. Each shard holds ceil(rows_per_token / S) of them and reads one row from each for every token. S is the tensor-parallel width, or that times the node's data-parallel replicas when they split the table rather than share one host copy, which the deployment's engram_config decides. DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram works this way.

docs.title: Context work
docs.text:
An Elementwise node's context.per, context.phase and context.decode_extent.

query_token · request

query_token Once per scheduled token, each over the context. request Once per request per step, over its context, however many of its tokens are scheduled.

"" · prefill

An omitted phase means every step; prefill means only steps that schedule the request's prompt tokens.

"" · max_model_len

An omitted decode_extent means the request's context; max_model_len means the engine's max_model_len, for a kernel launched over a buffer padded to it.

docs.title: Drafting modes
docs.text:
A speculator's drafting. An omitted drafting means autoregressive.

"" · parallel_block

parallel_block The draft stack runs once per step over num_spec_tokens positions per request, and each position predicts one draft token. DeepSeek-V4.1's DSpark drafts this way.
