docs.text: Name Recorded when attention_prefill_<kind> A measured prefill family for an attention kind (sparse_mla) or a scorer's role (block_index_scores) is only partly in the scenario's sets, so it is not used, and prefill is priced as without it. Value fallback. async_scheduling_spec The deployment speculates and the engine rules carry no async-compatible draft list, so the draft method is taken as leaving async scheduling on. block_size The deployment states no block size. 64 for a DSA sparse-attention model, whose indexer accepts only 64; for a DeepSeek-V4-family model the one kernel block its sparse backends accept on the part (for DeepSeek-V4.1 64 on SM90 and 128 on SM100; for DeepSeek-V4 256 on every part); otherwise vLLM's default of 16. cache_record A graph states a cache with no record listed under the cache data type that runs, so the cache is sized at its base record. compute_rate_<kind> A GEMM's weights are in a format whose rate the catalog does not state: FP32 weights run at the TF32 rate, taken as half the dense BF16 peak. compute_capability The catalog states no compute capability for the chip, so its generation is inferred from its native-format peaks and name where it decides kernel selection. cudagraph_mode No CUDA graph mode is stated. vLLM's default, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE. deepep_v2_mode The MoE dispatch runs DeepEP v2, whose path vLLM picks from enforce_eager, which a deployment cannot state: a resolved cudagraph_mode of NONE is read as it. Value deepep_v2_eager or deepep_v2_graph. dcp_comm_backend Decode-context parallelism is on and no combine backend is stated: the stock ag_rs. Also when one is stated but the engine rules give no list to check it against. engine_version The scenario declares a vLLM release other than the one whose behavior the kernel prices (v0.31.0). fabric_bandwidth_efficiency The cluster names a fabric and the scenario's sets carry no fabric_bandwidth_efficiency scoped to it, so every byte that crosses it -- a cross-node collective, a P/D handoff, a pipeline-stage boundary -- is priced at the catalog's nominal line rate. Value 1. engram_cpu_offload A graph states an Engram table and the deployment does not say where it lives: the release's cpu_offload default. engram_dp_shared_memory An Engram table under data parallelism, with dp_shared_memory unstated: resolved as the engine resolves it. gemm_eps_max_<kind> A kernel with a ramp of its own has none in the registry for the part, so it is priced on the one it falls back to, at the peak it computes at: a weight-only kernel (Marlin W8A16 MXFP8, W4A16 grouped) on the BF16 ramp; Marlin W4A16 NVFP4 grouped on the W4A16 MXFP4 grouped ramp, and that on BF16's; a native-FP4 part's grouped NVFP4 MoE (nvfp4_grouped) on the dense NVFP4 ramp. host_gather_rate_uva A table lookup reads a host-resident table (an Engram table under cpu_offload) and the registry has no rate for that gather, so its rows are read at the host link's rate. hybrid_kv_cache_manager A graph states window caches and the deployment runs a KV connector, which can turn the hybrid KV cache manager off and the window rings into full-length caches. kv_cache_grouping A graph states its caches and the rules pack cannot group them into the engine's shared block pool, so each cache is sized at its own page rather than in whole pool blocks. The reason names what the pack does not model. mamba_cache_mode A model with recurrent layers states no recurrent cache mode: align with prefix caching on, none with it off. max_cudagraph_capture_size Any CUDA graph is captured and the deployment states neither max_cudagraph_capture_size nor cudagraph_capture_sizes: vLLM's default ceiling, above which a step runs with no graph. max_model_len The deployment states no context length, or states auto: the bound is the model's context window from the graph (for auto, the most the engine can fit it to). max_num_batched_tokens No token budget per step is stated. vLLM's default for the chip's memory size. max_num_seqs No limit on concurrent requests is stated. vLLM's default for the chip's memory size. modality The graph prices the text decoder of a multimodal model; its vision or audio tower is not priced. mhc Only one of the mHC pre and post forms resolves, so neither is used. Value fallback. moe_a2a_<kind> A DeepEP backend (deepep_high_throughput, deepep_low_latency, deepep_v2_eager, deepep_v2_graph) runs the MoE dispatch but has no measured price for the part and expert width, or the expert group spans nodes, so it is priced as the generic routed all-to-all. mhc_<kind> An mHC component's rate (pre or post) is in the scenario's sets without its floor, so the measured mHC form is not used. Value fallback. mla_context_chunk Decode-context parallelism is on for a latent-attention model and no context length is stated, so the chunk in which a prefill gathers its cached context is taken at its largest. num_spec_tokens The deployment drafts a different number of tokens a step from the graph's speculator, so what the graph sizes at its own count is taken as stated. pipeline_binding_stage The pool runs pipeline parallelism: FixedBytes and the sequence sizes are this stage's rank, the one whose pool -- its own budget less its own fixed bytes over its own KV a token -- holds the fewest tokens, compared at the deployment's gpu_memory_utilization. PipelineStageMemory reports every stage. Value the stage index. pipeline_stages The pool runs pipeline parallelism: each stage is priced as its own step over the layers vLLM gives it, the embedding on the first, the head and drafter on the last, plus its boundary send and the receiving stage's TP all-gather; each stage's memory is its own, and the stage whose pool holds the fewest tokens binds. Value the stage count. pp_layer_partition The pool runs pipeline parallelism, and VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION, which a deployment cannot state, is taken as unset: the stages split the layers as get_pp_indices does by default. Value unset. sharded_projection_gather The deployment splits a replicated projection over TP at decode, as Muse Spark's MoE pooler and unpooler on Blackwell (sharded_at_decode): the gather that reassembles its columns is priced as the registry's NCCL all-gather over TP, where the engine fuses it into the next norm with its own NVLink kernels, which no registry entry measures. Value nccl all_gather. recurrent_prefill_rate_<kind> A recurrent mixer has no measured prefill form, so its prefill tokens are priced as the chunked scan's FLOPs on the BF16 ramp rather than at the decode scan's rate. sparse_mla_backend A DSA sparse-attention model on Hopper selects FlashInfer's sparse MLA backend, which needs a FlashInfer release the kernel cannot see installed. sparse_read_per_query A speculating deployment of a sparse-attention model: each verify token is charged its own window-and-top-k read, as vLLM gathers them, though the registry's rate was fitted on single-token decode and the sharing between a request's tokens was never measured. adaptive_verification_survival A deployment enabling DSpark adaptive verification: every request's draft slots are ranked by one survival curve, the run's stated per-position rates or, from its mean acceptance length, vLLM's minimum-variance schedule (_acceptance_length_to_rates), where the engine ranks each request by its own online estimate. Natural acceptance spreads more, so the trimmed budget is a lower bound on the trim. adaptive_verification_cost_curves A deployment enabling DSpark adaptive verification: the draft and verify cost tables the engine profiles from timed dummy steps are built, as the engine builds them, from this kernel's own NoOverlap prices of the same dummy steps, so the budget follows the kernel's prices rather than measured timings. speculator The deployment speculates and the graph states no speculator, so draft passes are not priced; or the deployment names a different method from the graph's speculator, which is the one priced. trtllm_gen_prefill_lane The sets carry the trtllm-gen prefill pair and no pair lists the implementation the caller reports for the prefill primitive (the pairs list none, list another, or none was reported), so the part's pooled prefill pair prices it (VAL-8)

docs.title: Optional coefficients that were missing
docs.text:
When a coefficient the kernel can price without is absent from the scenario's sets, and the deployment needs it, the entry is named for the coefficient, its value is absent, and its reason says what was priced without it. These are the coefficients it can apply to; a per-kind name ends in the kind it covers, such as _mla or _kda, and is needed only where the model has a layer of that kind.

Coefficient Without it attention_decode_floor, attention_decode_rate No measured decode attention: the KV read is charged at memory bandwidth and the per-layer floor is not charged attention_decode_rate_<kind> The chip-wide attention pair is used for that kind; for a scorer named by its role, its attention kind's pair attention_decode_floor_<kind> A scorer with its own rate inherits the part-wide attention floor attention_prefill_floor, attention_prefill_work_scale Prefill attention is charged on the plain efficiency ramp, with no floor attention_prefill_rate_<kind> Prefill of that attention kind (sparse_mla) or scorer role (block_index_scores) is priced with the part-wide prefill pair on its FLOPs, not with its own measured floor, per-request, per-token and byte terms mhc_rate_<kind> The mHC nodes running that component (pre, post) are charged their stated bytes at memory bandwidth, and, without the pre form, the hc_*fn GEMMs on the dense ramp recurrent_decode_floor_<kind>, recurrent_decode_rate_<kind> The recurrent mixer's decode term is not charged recurrent_prefill_floor_<kind> A recurrent mixer with a measured prefill rate is charged no prefill floor moe_routing_imbalance_median Experts are priced as evenly loaded host_link_bandwidth An offload transfer is not capped at the host link's rate host_step_per_request The scheduler's per-request CPU cost is charged at zero; with it, a step without async scheduling carries it in series and one with async scheduling shows only its excess over the device work host_admission_per_token, host_admission_per_request, host_output_token, host_completion, host_launch_eager_per_layer, host_launch_per_kernel, host_replay_graph_per_step That host cost is charged at zero

The eager launch cost is read as host_launch_eager_per_kernel where a set carries it, and as host_launch_eager_per_layer otherwise; both are charged per kernel. A model-scoped entry under either name is taken over a part-wide one.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Evidence() returns three things: how many entries of Provenance rest on evidence (method measured, literature or vendor_spec), how many there are in all, and the names of those whose method is assumed. The last includes the kernel's own entries above and any registry coefficient recorded as assumed. Entries with the methods transferred, roofline and not_charged are in the total and in neither of the other two. Refuse, assume, override shows a worked example.

docs.title: Resolved
docs.text:
Resolved() returns a kernel.Resolution: the tensor-, data- and expert-parallel widths the layout resolved to, the all-reduce backend that will run, whether asynchronous scheduling, cascade attention and sequence-parallel MoE are on, and a list of overrides. Each override names the field, what was requested, what was resolved, and why. The kernel records these:

Field When all2all_backend An MoE dispatch backend is stated for an expert-parallel layout that runs no dispatch: dp 1, pcp 1 and no sequence-parallel MoE input, where vLLM's use_all2all_kernels is false. The experts run on the replicated tokens and the tensor-parallel all-reduce combines them, so the backend is resolved as none and every backend prices the same step. allreduce_backend The custom all-reduce was requested at a tensor-parallel width it does not support, or across nodes on a chip without multi-node NVLink. NCCL runs instead. cache_dtype A sparse-attention model's KV cache is stored in a packed format its backend chooses, such as fp8_ds_mla for a stated fp8 on Hopper, or DeepSeek-V4.1's nvfp4_ds_mla for a stated fp8 on SM100. cp_kv_cache_interleave_size Decode-context parallelism is on, the interleave is unstated, the block size is above one, and a NIXL connector is configured, so vLLM sets the interleave to the block size. cudagraph_capture_sizes Stated capture sizes above max_num_batched_tokens, which vLLM drops. cudagraph_mode DeepEP high-throughput with dp above one, or MoonEP where its all-to-all runs: the engine cannot capture the dispatch and runs with no CUDA graphs. mamba_cache_mode A hybrid model states none with prefix caching on, which vLLM runs as align. max_cudagraph_capture_size A stated maximum that vLLM lowers: capped at max_num_batched_tokens, or off the sizes it captures (1, 2, 4, every 8 below 256, every 16 from it). The largest size that runs is the ceiling.

The two context-parallel widths are not fields of kernel.Resolution. Until contracts/kernel adds them, read them from DecodeContextParallelWidth() and PrefillContextParallelWidth().

docs.title: What New refuses
docs.text: Every reason New returns an error instead of a kernel, grouped by why. Each error message names the setting at fault and, where there is one, the setting to change. The engine's reasons cite the vLLM v0.31.0 source in the code beside them.

docs.title: The documents are malformed
docs.text:
• A scenario file has a key its document type does not define. LoadBundle decodes strictly, so Open, OpenPool and OpenInputs fail here.
  • A document fails the contracts' field-level validation: a missing required field, a value out of range. Rule-level findings, which depend on the engine version, do not stop construction.
  • The deployment has no pool at the requested index, or a tensor- or data-parallel width below one.
  • No engine rules are given. Opening a scenario file (Open, OpenPool, OpenInputs) fails earlier, when Repos.Rules is unset or has no rules for the engine version it names.
  • The engine rules cannot answer: a rules method panics while the kernel is built, as a forwarding wrapper around nothing does. The refusal names the panic. A rules method that panics later, inside a pricing call, is a defect in the caller's rules and panics there.

docs.title: The kernel implementations that run are malformed
docs.text:
• Inputs.Operations names a layer the graph (the target's, or the draft model's) does not have, a block-index scorer the layer does not run, or kernel implementations that differ from Inputs.Implementations when both are given.
  • Inputs.Implementations lists a primitive with no implementation, or has an implementation with no library, a code hash that is not lower-case hexadecimal of at least 12 digits, a code hash with no variant, or two different code hashes for one library and variant. A pool runs one build of a kernel.
  • A coefficient the cost model needs lists kernel implementations, the implementations of the operations that read it (the primitive it prices, narrowed to its kind where its name states one) are not all among them (or none is stated for that primitive), and no less trusted entry of its name covers the deployment. The error names each refused entry, the implementation it is valid for, and the primitive and what runs it.

docs.title: The engine would not start it
docs.text:
These are layouts vLLM v0.31.0 refuses at startup.

Context parallelism

  • Prefill-context parallelism on a model with any layer whose attention is not latent, or with a recurrent layer.
  • Prefill- and decode-context parallelism together on anything but DSA sparse attention.
  • The a2a decode-context combine together with prefill-context parallelism.
  • A decode-context combine backend the engine release does not accept.
  • With decode-context parallelism on, a stated cp_kv_cache_interleave_size larger than the block size or not dividing it, unless a NIXL connector is configured. With a MultiConnector, whose child connectors a deployment cannot name, an interleave that does not fit, or one left unstated, is refused because the outcome cannot be known.

Sparse attention (DeepSeek sparse attention, DSA: DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5)

  • A stated block size that is not a multiple of 64.
  • A chip older than Hopper, where no sparse-attention backend runs.
  • A cache data type no backend on the chip serves under the requested parallelism.
  • Decode-context parallelism on FlashMLA's sparse backend with a 16-bit cache, with the a2a combine, with local and gathered head counts that pad to different kernel sizes, or, without prefill-context parallelism, with 32 or more attention heads per rank; or prefill- and decode-context parallelism there on a cache other than fp8_ds_mla.

Cache data types

  • A cache data type vLLM does not accept, or a recurrent-state data type it does not accept.
  • fp8_inc, which no CUDA attention backend serves.
  • The packed fp8_ds_mla and nvfp4_ds_mla layouts on a model whose target stack holds any attention that is not sparse.
  • Plain nvfp4 on a model with latent attention.

Block size and architecture

  • A block size a DeepSeek-V4-family model's sparse backends do not accept: DeepSeek-V4.1's run 64-token kernel blocks on SM90 and 128-token ones on SM100, and DeepSeek-V4's run 256-token blocks on every part.
  • A model graph that states facts by GPU generation, on a chip whose compute capability the catalog does not state or whose generation the graph does not describe.

Experts

  • An expert-parallel width larger than the model's number of experts, which would leave some ranks with none.

Attention heads

  • A tensor-parallel width that does not divide the KV heads of an attention whose graph says its projection cannot replicate a head across ranks (kv_heads_not_replicated), as Muse Spark's fused QKV and output-gate projection cannot: TP above 16 on its 16 KV heads.

docs.title: The prefill lane the engine reports
docs.text:
FlashInfer's trtllm-gen prefill is the one kernel with a pair measured on it: on b200, b300, gb200-nvl72 and gb300, attention_prefill_*_trtllm_gen_kv_bf16 and _kv_fp8 price the prefill of the non-latent layers. The kernel does not work out from any engine setting whether an engine runs that kernel, and it reads no engine setting for it: which kernel runs is the engine's to decide and to report (design X2, SUB-6). The caller reports the kernel of each lowered operation (Inputs.Operations, or Inputs.Implementations by primitive), and the lane prices the prefill only when one pair lists exactly the implementation reported for attention.prefill (library, variant and code hash, VAL-8). The pair that lists it prices; the cache dtype and the block size do not choose it. Latent (MLA) layers keep the part's pooled pair, and decode is not priced from the lane.

  • The pair is chosen by the element type of the cache the reported prefill operations read (PrimitiveShape.Dtype, in the catalog's words): the bf16 pair for bf16, the fp8 pair for fp8. The lane was fitted on those two caches only, so an fp16 or int8 cache, or one whose element type is not stated, is not priced from it (the storage size, Format, cannot tell bf16 from fp16): the lane is left unpriced, the part-wide pair prices the prefill, and the assumption trtllm_gen_prefill_lane names the element type. A kernel that serves both element types may be listed by both pairs and is not ambiguous. Prefill operations that read caches of two element types are refused, since the lane is priced from one pair for the layers of a kind. Reported only by primitive (Inputs.Implementations), the kernel cannot tell the format, and two pairs listing the reported implementation are refused.
  • The pairs are read by the prefill of the non-latent layers alone. A pool that runs trtllm-gen for them and another kernel for the latent layers accepts a pair that lists the trtllm-gen kernel alone.
  • With no pair listing it (the pairs list none, list another, or nothing was reported for the prefill primitive), the part's pooled pair prices the prefill and the assumption trtllm_gen_prefill_lane records why. A model with no non-latent layer has nothing for the lane to price.

The lookup binds each pair to the primitive its name prices. A pair valid for a decode kernel A does not price a prefill that runs B, a pool that reports A for decode and nothing for prefill does not admit it, and a prefill that runs two kernels is priced only by a pair that lists both.

The registry's pairs are transferred from vLLM 0.25.0 and list no implementation, because no engine release publishes kernel hashes yet (kernel_impls.json; inference-sim/blis-registry#73). So on the committed registry the lane is not priced and an engine's report changes no price. The lane is dormant until an entry lists the hash of the prefill kernel and the engine reports it.

A setting that selects a kernel the registry has not measured is the engine model's to refuse: it resolves the setting to the implementation that runs, reports it, and decides whether a primitive whose reported implementation no entry lists may be priced from the pooled entry. The kernel reads no setting and applies no engine default.

docs.title: The kernel cannot price it truthfully
docs.text:
• Pipeline parallelism beside data parallelism or context parallelism (pcp or dcp above one): the stage split prices one pipeline per pool. Pipeline parallelism on a model whose graph states its caches, whose sizes are per layer kind over the whole stack rather than per stage. A drafter that reads an auxiliary hidden state of a layer outside the target's stack.
  • dcp_q_replicate where it would take effect: decode-context parallelism without prefill-context parallelism, on a latent-attention model. It trades a collective for a replicated projection the kernel cannot identify in the graph, so pricing only the saving would make it look free.
  • A cache data type vLLM accepts whose page layout the kernel does not size: the turboquant and per-token-head formats.
  • A quantization, CUDA graph mode or decode-context combine backend the kernel does not price.
  • A deployment that speculates through an autoregressive drafter, a named EAGLE3 head or the graph's own MTP, when the pool's plan does not state which rows the drafter's first pass processes or for which requests its head and later passes run (draft_passes_unstated, naming the drafter and the missing fact), or states a word outside the fixed list (draft_passes_unknown). The facts are plan.DraftPolicy.FirstPassRows and PassRequests; the engine settings carry neither.

docs.title: The weight layout the engine says it serves
docs.text: Settings.ServedWeights states, class by class (linear, linear scale, routed experts, router, head, embedding), the dtype the engine serves the checkpoint in. The kernel proves the target graph stores exactly that and refuses a difference as served_weights_mismatch, naming each class with both values. A class the graph does not contain is empty, so a graph with its router, head or embedding removed cannot match, and a class at another dtype cannot either. The engine model resolves its own quantization setting and passes the result.

docs.title: A quantization spelling the kernel does not price
docs.text: The kernel prices the quantization spellings servedDType lists (fp8, ptpc_fp8, fbgemm_fp8, modelopt, modelopt_fp4, nvfp4, mxfp4 and the weight-only integer names) and refuses any other as "not one this kernel prices". It recognises no engine's own resolution of a quantization setting: vLLM's mxfp8, modelopt_mxfp8, gpt_oss_mxfp4 and modelopt_mixed name a method the checkpoint declares, which the engine model reads, so it leaves Quantization empty for a checkpoint served as stored and states the layout in ServedWeights above.

docs.title: A coefficient is missing
docs.text:
• A required coefficient has no entry in the sets the scenario names, or none whose scope covers this chip, model and layout: the matrix-multiply efficiency for the served data type, the memory derate, the memory magnitudes, or a collective's floor, rate or transition rate at the width the layout needs.
  • A collective's group width is not one the registry measured on the chip. The kernel does not borrow a narrower width's figures, because they would understate the wider group. Two cases are priced rather than refused: a group narrower than every measured width, at the narrowest, and a group wider than 16, the widest the registry's sweeps cover, at the chip's widest measured width.

Optional coefficients are not refused when missing; see Provenance, Evidence, Resolved.

docs.title: In the source
docs.text: The checks run in New and the functions it calls in new.go, sparse_mla.go and internal/resolve, and the tests in refusals_test.go, sparse_mla_test.go and dcp_knobs_test.go check most of them.

docs.title: Sources of truth
docs.text:
Every claim the kernel makes about the engine is stated against one release of vLLM. The contracts, the catalog and the registry it reads are in the same repository, at the same commit. This table is generated from the pins themselves.

What Version Commit Pinned in Engine behavior: vLLM v0.31.0 db9527a46873 EngineBehaviourVersion, EngineBehaviourCommit in new.go Interfaces and document types: blis-schemas v0.10.0 — go.mod Engine rules for the commands, docs and tests: blis-vllm/rules v0.0.0-20261027143841-9b5ec9da1999 — go.mod Declared facts: blis-catalog 0.5.0 b5550f750cb5 testdata/upstream.lock Coefficients: blis-registry v0.3.0 96bead697172 testdata/upstream.lock

docs.title: Two sources of engine behavior
docs.text: Most of what the kernel knows about vLLM is encoded here, at v0.31.0: which kernels run, how work is split, what an unstated setting defaults to, which layouts start. Some version-scoped facts are read instead from the engine rules the caller supplies for the release the scenario declares (for vLLM, the packs of github.com/inference-sim/blis-vllm/rules), among them which tensor-parallel widths the custom all-reduce supports, when the MoE input is made sequence-parallel, which decode-context combine backends the release accepts, how many pages a window cache holds, how stated caches group into the shared KV block pool, and the CUDA graph capture sizes a deployment's stated knobs resolve to (resolve.EngineRules lists them).

docs.title: Reading a citation
docs.text:
A comment in the source that cites vllm/<path>:<lines> means those lines at the commit above. To read them in a vLLM checkout:

git show v0.31.0:vllm/config/parallel.py | sed -n '571,577p'

A comment that cites a vLLM line without a path, as :571-577, continues the path of the citation before it.

docs.title: Changing a pin
docs.text:
• vLLM. Moving to a newer release is a review of every behavior the kernel encodes, not a version bump: each citation must be checked against the new release, and the constants EngineBehaviourVersion and EngineBehaviourCommit in new.go changed with them.
  • The contracts, the catalog and the registry. These are contracts/, catalog/ and registry/ of this repository, so there is no pin to move: a change to any of them is tested against the kernel in the same pull request. Run go test ./kernel/.... A renamed chip or coefficient is meant to break the tests that name it.

After a change to a pin or to pricing, regenerate the generated files with blis-vllm's go run ./kerneltests/internal/docgen, so this table and the figures follow.

docs.title: Research
docs.text:
How well the kernel's step price matches measured forward passes, where it falls short and why, and how its laws are tested. For readers deciding how far to trust a prediction, or working on the model itself.

Accuracy The comparison with measured forward passes, which also chooses between the kernel's two estimates, and where the known error comes from. How the laws are tested The kinds of test the repository relies on, and why most of them compare against the engine's own source or against an exact relation rather than against fixed numbers.

The places where the kernel knowingly prices something differently from the engine are listed on Known divergences.

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text: The cost model prices one engine step. The evidence for that price is a comparison with measured forward passes, which time one step at a known batch and context with no scheduler in between. It also decides which of the cost model's two estimates to use. How accurate a whole simulation is, against measured end-to-end benchmarks, is computed in one place: accuracy-dashboard's scoring harness, which the dashboard publishes.

docs.title: Whole-step time
docs.text:
NVIDIA's FPM dataset, published alongside AISimulate, times single forward passes at a known batch and context, with no scheduler in between. That is the quantity the kernel prices, so it is the right evidence for choosing between Overlap and NoOverlap. Over 219 points, on two models, two chips and five parallel layouts:

Estimate Mean signed error Mean absolute error Overlap −13.5% 14.7% NoOverlap −3.4% 10.2%

NoOverlap is the closer of the two at 158 of the 219 points, and at four of the five layouts. The exception, MiniMax-M2.7 at pure tensor-parallel width 2, is the one layout where a single resource holds most of the step. Both signed errors are negative: on this data the measured step is slower than either estimate. The registry records the comparison in Choosing the overlap band, with a script that reproduces it from the output of bandprobe (Commands).

docs.title: Where the error is known to come from
docs.text: Some of it is recorded in the source. The routed experts' arithmetic is charged at more than its share under tensor parallelism, a known over-charge that is kept because removing it makes the measured accuracy worse: it offsets a term not yet identified. That and the other notes are listed on Known divergences.

docs.title: How the laws are tested
docs.text: A cost model can be wrong in ways that still produce plausible numbers, so its tests are written to catch exactly that. Few of them compare against a fixed number. Most compare against the engine's own source, against an exact relation the answer must satisfy, or against a deployment that differs in one setting.

docs.title: Against the engine's source
docs.text:
Where the kernel reproduces an exact rule of vLLM, a test transcribes that rule from vLLM v0.31.0 and checks the kernel against the transcription, over a grid of inputs rather than at one point. The rules checked this way include how ranks are grouped for each kind of parallelism, the size of a KV cache page, how many tokens of a context each decode-context rank holds, and how a prefill is split across prefill-context ranks.

The transcription is the oracle, so it is kept as close to vLLM's code as Go allows, and cites the lines it follows.

docs.title: Against exact relations
docs.text:
Where no closed form exists to compare against, a test changes one input and checks how the output must respond. Three kinds recur:

Inflate one coefficient. Multiply the fixed cost of one collective, on one group size, by ten, and a step's time rises exactly when the step launches that collective, by exactly nine times its fixed cost for each launch. This asks which collectives a layout runs without reading anything inside the kernel, and it is how the decode-context combine and the prefill-context gathers are tested.

Laws that hold exactly. Growing a decode's context must add exactly the bytes the KV cache grew by, divided by the attention rate, to the memory time. Three expert-parallel widths of the same model must satisfy an exact linear relation in the number of experts the fullest rank holds. Tripling every memory coefficient must move the fixed memory and no step time.

Properties over random inputs. The KV page arithmetic is checked against vLLM's over 20,000 random model geometries, and the efficiency ramp is checked over a sweep of sizes to be monotone, bounded and exact at its half point.

docs.title: Against a deployment that starts
docs.text: Most refusals are tested beside a deployment that differs only in the setting at fault, and does start. A test that checked only for an error would pass when the kernel refused for some other reason.

docs.title: Breaking a law on purpose
docs.text: A test that has never failed has not been shown to test anything. The practice here is to check a new law by breaking it on purpose (deleting a term, changing a comparison, swapping a divisor) and confirming that a test fails, and to name in the commit the changes it was checked against.

docs.title: The documentation
docs.text: The Go on these pages is taken from example_test.go, whose examples Go runs and checks, and a test checks the output shown beside each example against that example's. The figure on Pricing a step, the list of known divergences and the pins are generated from the code, and a test fails when a committed copy differs from what the generator would write. The table of assumptions on Provenance, Evidence, Resolved is checked against the assumptions the code can record.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
The registry holds the learned numbers behind a BLIS latency estimate: the coefficients a cost model fits from measurements or, where no measurement exists, assumes. Each coefficient records how it was obtained and which hardware it applies to, so an estimate can be traced back to the evidence it rests on.

At revision 965b05834c47, the registry holds 1,241 coefficient entries in 9 sets, covering 13 GPU parts. By method: 901 measured, 51 vendor_spec (transcribed from NVIDIA's AISimulate), 263 assumed, and 2 not_charged (a declared zero).

docs.title: Where it sits
docs.text:
BLIS keeps different kinds of number in different places. The registry, registry/ in blis-substrate, holds one kind: numbers that a measurement could revise.

flowchart LR
    subgraph substrate["blis-substrate"]
        contracts["<b>contracts/</b><br/>shapes and validators"]
        catalog["<b>catalog/</b><br/>declared facts"]
        registry["<b>registry/</b><br/>learned numbers"]
        kernel["<b>kernel/</b><br/>prices one step"]
    end
    sim["<b>inference-sim</b><br/>simulates serving"]

    contracts -. validates .-> catalog
    contracts -. validates .-> registry
    catalog -- read by --> kernel
    registry -- read by --> kernel
    contracts -- imported by --> kernel
    kernel -- called by --> sim

How the work is divided explains the split and why it is drawn where it is.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
To run BLIS with the registry, or read it from your own code, read Using. A released simulator carries the registry it was tested with; you need a directory only to run another one.

To add a part, refit a family or correct an entry, read Contributing. Most sets are written by scripts, and the page explains which checks run where.

To understand what a coefficient is and why the registry is shaped the way it is, read Concepts. Three short pages.

To look up a value, go to Reference. Every table there is generated from the committed files, and every value links to its entry.

To challenge a value, read Methodology: the rules, the evidence behind each decision, and the claims later withdrawn.

To learn how a coefficient earns its place, read Fitting principles: the landing gate and the repeatable procedure.

docs.title: One coefficient
docs.text:
Every entry looks like this one, quoted from the committed file when this page was built:

registry/coefficients/cost-model-primitives.yaml, line 49
- gemm_m_half_bf16:
    value: 94
    units: tokens
    method: measured
    fitted: true
    scope: {hardware: [a100-80, a100-sxm]}
    sources:
      - {kind: model, cite: "NVIDIA AISimulate systems/data/a100_sxm/gemm/vllm/0.14.0/gemm_perf.parquet (NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB), 9,240 bfloat16 rows over 21 token counts, kernel torch.nn.functional.linear", role: primary}
    rationale: >
      The token count at which the ramp reaches half its asymptote, so it sets how fast a widening batch approaches peak. Fitted jointly with gemm_eps_max_bf16 on the same envelope; residual 0.0673.

Quoted from the committed file at build time.

It is a measured, fitted constant of the GEMM efficiency ramp, scoped to two names for the same A100 silicon, citing the exact sweep it was fitted on. The Coefficients page explains each field.

docs.title: Choosing between the kernel's two step-time band edges
docs.text: The cost model (kernel/) reports a band rather than a point estimate. Overlap sums the max over resources within each layer and then sums layers; NoOverlap sums every resource. Which edge a consumer should use is a model-selection question, and this document records how it was answered.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
NVIDIA's FPM dataset (huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/aisimulate-fpm-dataset, Apache-2.0) measures one synchronized whole-forward iteration at a known batch and KV-token count. It prices the same quantity the band brackets, with no scheduler in between, which makes it the right evidence for this choice — and the wrong evidence for fitting a coefficient, because it constrains a composition rather than a constant.

Reproduce with registry/scripts/select_overlap_band.py. The band CSV comes from bandprobe (Commands), which prices the band with the cost model, because the cost model owns composition; the registry only selects between its columns.

cell n Overlap NoOverlap winner MiniMax-M2.7 h200 pure-tp4 45 9.32% 8.33% NoOverlap MiniMax-M2.7 h200 pure-tp2 41 6.17% 9.89% Overlap MiniMax-M2.7 h200 tep4 45 18.35% 7.88% NoOverlap MiniMax-M2.7 h200 tep2 43 15.19% 9.60% NoOverlap GLM-5.2-NVFP4 b200 tep8 45 23.71% 15.05% NoOverlap pooled 219 14.70% 10.16% NoOverlap

Signed means matter more than absolute ones here, because a one-sided error is a missing term rather than scatter:

edge signed mean Overlap −13.45% NoOverlap −3.44%

NoOverlap is closer on 158 of 219 points and is nearly unbiased. Overlap's −13.45% is almost exactly the −13.10% one-sided TPOT deficit BLIS shows end-to-end on the InferenceX corpus, which is independent corroboration: two different datasets, measured through different paths, agree on the magnitude of the same defect.

docs.title: Physical reason
docs.text: vLLM serves decode in PIECEWISE cudagraph mode, where attention executes eagerly between captured segments. Per-layer overlap is therefore structurally limited, so the pessimistic edge being closer is the expected outcome rather than a coincidence.

docs.title: The dissent, and why it is a regime boundary
docs.text:
pure-tp2 holds the whole model on two GPUs with no expert-parallel sharding, so the expert weight read is four times the tp4 case and dominates a single resource. Where one resource holds most of a step, per-stage max IS the right composition, and Overlap wins. Even there NoOverlap is closer at batch ≥ 128.

The principled fix is not a global switch but a concentration-aware choice inside the kernel, which is the only place that holds StepEstimate.PerResource. Five cells is not enough evidence to propose that form; it is enough to reject the optimistic edge as a universal default.

docs.title: Separation of evidence
docs.text:
• Fitting — AISimulate operator tables (Apache-2.0), per-kernel.
  • Model selection — NVIDIA FPM (Apache-2.0), whole-forward. Used for fitting nothing.
  • Evaluation — SemiAnalysis InferenceX. Never used for fitting or selection.

select_overlap_band.py refuses any path under an inferencex or semianalysis directory, so the separation is enforced by the tool rather than by convention.

docs.title: Fitting BLIS to the real world: principles and a repeatable procedure
docs.text: This document states how a coefficient, or a pricing mechanism, earns its place in BLIS. It complements methodology.md, which defines what a coefficient is and how each family was fitted, and reproducing-coefficients.md, which says how to regenerate any value. Where this document and methodology.md §3 differ on the role of end-to-end data, this document records the newer rule and §3.1 below says what changed.

docs.title: 1. The principle
docs.text:
A fit that does well across latency, KV, queueing and throughput together is the evidence that BLIS's mechanisms mimic the real ones. A fit that does well on latency alone is not.

A simulator can match a median latency for the wrong reason: an over-large KV pool hiding an under-priced step, or an optimistic queue hiding a pessimistic kernel. Two errors of opposite sign cancel in one metric and show up in every other. So a mechanism is accepted only when the quantities it governs agree with the measurement simultaneously, at the levels where the mechanism acts:

level what to compare what a disagreement means GPU step step time against batch composition; operator timings a kernel or composition term is wrong memory KV pool size, KV usage over time, host-tier usage a memory term, the cache layout, or admission is wrong scheduling running and waiting requests, prefix-hit rate, prompt tokens by source admission, eviction, chunking or routing is wrong queueing per-request queue wait, its distribution arrival handling, client pacing, or a capacity term is wrong end to end TTFT, TPOT/ITL, E2E, output throughput, interactivity the composition of all of the above

A KV deviation is often the clearest diagnosis: a simulated KV usage of 10% against a measured 90% names a wrong pool, eviction or admission long before the latency error says why.

docs.title: 2. Compare apples to apples, or not at all
docs.text:
Every comparison is between the same quantity on both sides. Before any number is trusted:

  1. Same definition. Map each measured field to the simulator's field by its source code, not its name. Examples found the hard way:
  2. InferenceX's ITL and TPOT are the same per-request quantity; interactivity is 1 / ITL percentile.
  3. vLLM's logged "GPU KV cache size" for DeepSeek-V4 is not pool tokens. It is num_blocks / blocks_reserved_per_request x max_model_len, summed over every KV group (vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py). Compare blocks with blocks.
  4. A log whose stated KV size contradicts its own "maximum concurrency" line is excluded, not compared.
  5. Same window and request set. Profile phase on both sides; warmup excluded on both; cancelled requests handled identically. The code asserts it, and a mismatch is recorded by name instead of compared.
  6. Same offered load. The replay must reproduce the client's pacing. The anchor runs used aiperf's --trace-idle-gap-cap-seconds 300; a replay without the cap carried 2.6-4x fewer requests in flight at the same nominal concurrency, and its latency error was a load artefact, not a model error.
  7. Same engine behaviour. Resolve every version-dependent behaviour from the run's own engine build, never the newest default: SWA bounded replay, model runner, async scheduling, frontend, capture sizes. A behaviour the schema cannot state becomes a named mismatch on that point.
  8. Same model and hardware. Use the checkpoint the run actually served (from its recipe or log), and the device memory the driver reports, not the marketing figure.
  9. Check parity with KV first. A gross KV deviation (the pool, or the usage distribution) is checked first as a parity defect: in the setup (memory budget, max_model_len, block size, KV dtype, layout, prefix caching, the checkpoint served, KV groups), the workload (ISL/OSL, prefix sharing, offered load, window) or the definitions. Only after those are ruled out is it treated as a model error. Points with an unresolved parity defect are excluded from fits with a named reason. Because KV capacity drives admission, queueing and preemption, closing KV parity usually improves the other metrics too, where capacity binds.

docs.title: 3. Data roles
docs.text: source class role operator and microbenchmark data (AISimulate sweeps, InferenceX OperatorX / CollectiveX / ubenchX, vendor kernel READMEs verified against their repos) fit the primitive it measures forward-pass data (FPM) fit composed terms; validate composition end-to-end runs, FIT share fit terms no operator data can supply: host and scheduler cost, admission, queueing, collectives at scale, KV transfer, offload end-to-end runs, HELD share evaluation only named anchor sets evaluation only, reported separately

docs.title: 3.1 The end-to-end split
docs.text:
End-to-end runs are partitioned once, before any scoring, by a seeded, documented, diversity-stratified random draw: about 40% FIT and 60% HELD. Every level of every factor (model, GPU, engine build, parallel layout, P/D mode, speculation, offload tier, frontend, scenario, concurrency band) appears in both sets wherever its stratum has at least two points. A point keeps its request pairs and its seed repeats in one set. Named anchors are HELD in full. The partition is hashed, and new runs are added by the same seeded rule without re-drawing existing assignments.

This replaces methodology.md §3's "evaluation only" rule for end-to-end rows. The protection that rule gave is kept by the HELD share and the anchors: no HELD result is read by a fit until that fit is frozen.

docs.title: 3.2 Reputation of a source
docs.text: Authoritative sources are vendors and benchmark organisations publishing their own measurements (NVIDIA, the engine projects, InferenceX, MLCommons, model labs), verified as the real organisation. Research data with a published method is usable with stated caveats and never as a coefficient's only source. Anonymous, re-uploaded, synthetic or unlicensed data is not used. A figure forwarded from a secondary summary is verified against its primary file at a pinned commit before use.

docs.title: 4. The loss: distributions, on informative metrics
docs.text:
1. Fit distributions, not points. Per run and metric, use the median-normalised Wasserstein-1 distance between the measured and simulated empirical distributions, plus a tail term (quantile errors at p50/p90/p99 or KS). Where server time series exist, include the distributions of running requests, waiting requests and KV usage, so a fit must reproduce queueing as well as latency. A one-to-one request join (same trace turn, input and output length) gives per-request comparisons where the data allows.
  2. Choose the metrics that carry the term's signal. For each term, a metric enters its loss only if it passes all of:
  3. signal: variance across configurations well above variance across seed repeats;
  4. sensitivity: it moves when the parameter moves (check by perturbation on FIT runs);
  5. independence: it is not a restatement of a metric already in the loss;
  6. reliability: no definitional mismatch, window effect or aggregation quirk on either side;
  7. level: it observes the level where the term's mechanism acts. Weight the remaining metrics by inverse noise variance, and record the choice before fitting.
  8. Few, bounded, physical parameters. A distribution loss can be gamed by a flexible term, so no free-form corrections. Each parameter has a physical meaning and bounds.

docs.title: 4a. Why distributions, not aggregates
docs.text:
An aggregate (a mean, a median, one percentile) answers "is the typical value right". A distribution answers "is the process that produced the values right", and that is the question a simulator has to answer.

  1. Aggregates hide compensating errors; distributions expose them. A median latency can match while the simulated distribution is too narrow (no queueing tail) and the measured one is bimodal (some requests stalled). The medians agree for the wrong reason. Example from the DeepSeek-V4.1 H100 anchor at its saturation point: the measured decode spent most of its time in chunk gaps over 250 ms, a second mode the simulator never produced. No single percentile names that; the distribution shape does.
  2. The shape carries the mechanism.
  3. A long right tail in TTFT is queueing; its weight says how often the system is saturated.
  4. A second mode in ITL is stalls: preemption, a blocking transfer, a sync point.
  5. A distribution of KV usage pinned near 100% is a capacity regime; one spread across the range is a lightly loaded system.
  6. A width that grows with load is contention; a width that does not is a fixed overhead. Matching the shape constrains the mechanism. Matching the median constrains only one point of it.
  7. Tails are what deployments are judged on. Interactivity is quoted at P90 and SLOs at P90/P99. A model fitted to medians is unconstrained exactly where it is used.
  8. More information per run. A run with thousands of requests is one point to an aggregate loss and thousands of observations to a distribution loss. That identifies more parameters per run without needing more runs. Uncertainty is still clustered by run, since requests in one run are not independent.
  9. Robustness. A median-normalised Wasserstein-1 distance is in units of the metric, comparable across models and loads, and less sensitive to a few outliers than a mean error.

What distributions cost, and the guard rails. - They need the same population on both sides. A distribution comparison over different request sets (warmup on one side, a different window, different cancellation handling) is meaningless, so the request set is asserted (§2.2). - They are noisier per run than a median, so a distance enters a loss only after its seed-to-seed spread has been measured (§4.2, signal), and is weighted by inverse noise variance. - A flexible term can fit any shape, so distributional losses make the "few, bounded, physical parameters" rule (§4.3) stricter, not looser.

How both are used.

question measure is a deployment's typical cost right (what a user plans capacity on) aggregate error: MAPE per metric, signed median are the mechanisms right (what makes a prediction trustworthy off the training set) distribution distance: W1, KS, p10/p50/p90/p99 quantile errors; server-state distributions is something grossly broken gross-deviation flags (e.g. KV usage off by more than 30 points or 2x, hit rate off by more than 0.2)

Fits minimise distribution distance on the informative metrics. Both aggregate error and distribution distance are reported for every held-out set, and the landing gate (§7) requires both to improve. An improvement in one with a loss in the other means a mechanism is still wrong, and the change does not land.

docs.title: 5. Where direct data is missing: model, don't assume
docs.text: When no measurement covers an operator at the needed hardware, dtype or shape, build a mechanistic model from the kernel's implementation: tiling, FLOPs and bytes per tile, wave quantisation over SMs, launch and sync overhead, the roofline. Fit its few physical parameters on all indirect data (the same kernel on other hardware through a declared transfer, sibling kernels, forward-pass data, end-to-end FIT decomposition). Report identifiability, and run a parameter-recovery check. A parameter the data cannot identify is fixed at a stated physical value with a range; it is never called fitted. Such coefficients carry the evidence class modelled, distinct from measured, fitted and assumed.

docs.title: 6. Version discipline
docs.text: A coefficient fitted on data from engine version V may be used for version W only if every function on the term's code path is unchanged between V and W, shown by a per-function diff that ignores comments, typing and logging. A branch that changed counts as unchanged for a particular point only when that point's recorded configuration provably disables it. Terms that do not pass through engine code (collectives, NVMe, host link, GPU kernel floors) may use any version's data, with the reason recorded.

docs.title: 7. The landing gate
docs.text:
Every change is pre-registered (data, split, metric choice, pass condition) before any held-out number is computed. It lands only if:

  1. held-out error improves, per factor where a stratum has at least 10 points;
  2. held-out distribution distance improves;
  3. nothing else gets worse: the other metrics, the named anchors, the transfer check, and seed-averaged comparisons within the pooled standard error;
  4. the code change carries tests that fail when the fix is reverted.

A change that fails is parked with its evidence, or lands as a recorded deviation only when the failure is shown to be measurement noise or a definitional artefact, and the record says so.

docs.title: 8. The repeatable procedure
docs.text:
1. Enumerate every source; classify it (§3); check its reputation and whether it has updates.
  2. Build or extend the run inventory; record each run's blocker and what would unlock it.
  3. Draw or extend the FIT/HELD partition (§3.1). Hash it.
  4. Resolve every run's engine behaviour from its own build (§2.4).
  5. Replay FIT points apples to apples (§2); assert definitions, windows and load.
  6. Triage gross KV deviations for parity (§2.6) before anything else; exclude points with an unresolved parity defect, with a named reason.
  7. Keep a per-coefficient data ledger: every source, used or not, and why. An unused relevant source is a defect to close.
  8. Diagnose on FIT points across every level of §1 before fitting anything. A term fitted to absorb a different mechanism's error is wrong.
  9. Choose the metrics per term (§4.2); pre-register the gate (§7).
  10. Fit; check identifiability; freeze.
  11. Evaluate on HELD; report per factor, with stratified sampling fractions and run-clustered bootstrap intervals; report the count of single-run strata, which make intervals optimistic.
  12. Land or park (§7). Record every landing and deviation where the next fitter will find it.

docs.title: How a coefficient in this registry is defined, fitted and checked
docs.text: This document states the rules. band-selection.md records one model-selection decision made under them; vllm/docs/perf-model/hypothesis-log.md records the measurements, the negative results and the retractions.

docs.title: 1. What a coefficient is
docs.text:
A coefficient is a measured constant of a law the kernel evaluates — never a fudge factor and never a per-model correction. Each entry carries:

field meaning value the number units stated explicitly, because the single commonest error in this project is a unit slip method measured, vendor_spec, assumed, or not_charged (a deliberate zero) fitted whether a script produced it scope the deployment dimensions it applies to: hardware, model, TP, EP, nodes sources the exact file the value came from, with row counts rationale why this value, what it replaced, and what rejecting it would cost

Three rules follow from method:

  • An assumed coefficient is a declared gap, not a measurement. §6.0 counts them by kind; the ones nothing in this project's data could replace are the seven host overheads and the four CUDA-graph capture sizes (§11). Any claim resting on one has to say so.
  • A vendor_spec coefficient is NVIDIA's observation, not this project's. hbm_derate at 0.8 is the example.
  • A not_charged coefficient is a deliberate zero, so a consumer can tell "no cost" from "cost unknown". cudagraph_capture_bytes_none is the one instance.

A value and its citation move together. Editing one without the other is how a registry comes to describe a fit nobody ran, and the validator re-derives values from the sweep its citation names, so a stale citation fails rather than lies.

A coefficient with no reader is not live. dtypeFit in the kernel can return only three dtype suffixes — bf16, fp8, nvfp4 — so the 14 gemm_*_fp8_block entries are unreachable. That was discovered by grepping the kernel for the key, not the registry. Check both.

Each unread family is either given a reader or removed, and the decision is recorded (inference-sim/blis-registry#36):

  • Removed: hbm_constant_latency and p2p_latency, the two NVIDIA-simulator constants whose fixed cost the kernel's measured attention and collective floors already carry, so a reader would double-count; and moe_routing_imbalance_p90, a tail a mean-step model does not price (its value is stated in each median's rationale). A property test keeps them out.
  • Kept, with a named reader: the gemm_*_fp8_block ramps. They are what vLLM runs for a 128×128 block-scaled FP8 checkpoint (DeepGEMM and FlashInfer block-scaled kernels), and their fit differs from per-tensor FP8 (h100: 0.749 / 160 against 0.648 / 131). A ramp selected by block scaling, blis-latency-kernel#34, is what would read them; the cost model does not select one.
  • Given readers: cost-model-memory (blis-latency-kernel#22); the weight-only Marlin ramps on parts with no native four-bit peak, the indexer pair and the host-gather rate (§10.5), through blis-latency-kernel#44, which also added the role-keyed attention lookup. The reference overview lists every family that has no reader, so "committed" is never read as "live".

docs.title: 2. The lane rule: fit the engine you predict
docs.text:
AISimulate ships five framework lanes (vllm 332 files, sglang 313, trtllm 217, nccl 23, oneccl 2). The lane is part of the path, so choosing it is explicit — and the lanes are not interchangeable:

operator finding decode attention vLLM/TRT-LLM differ 1.30-1.35x on Hopper and 0.83-0.85x on Blackwell. The SIGN flips, because vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py:99-107 dispatches on compute capability — FA3 at major 9, FA4 at major 10. prefill attention vLLM runs at 0.79-0.81x of TRT-LLM's on all five parts, concentrated at short prompts: 0.505x at isl=1 against a ~0.87x plateau above 128. MoE 1.38-1.41x Hopper, 0.86-0.90x Blackwell, with entirely disjoint kernel_source values. GEMM the lanes AGREE to 0.4-3.6% over 100,668-130,156 shared shapes — same cuBLAS/CUTLASS kernels — so GEMM stays on the larger TRT-LLM sweep. all_gather, reduce_scatter, broadcast NCCL is the vLLM path. CustomAllreduce implements all-reduce only; should_custom_all_gather and should_custom_reduce_scatter gate and fall through. AISimulate has no vLLM data for them because there is nothing to measure.

So "use the vLLM lane" is a conclusion to be tested per operator, not a blanket rule. Of 654 lane-citing coefficients, 572 are not on the vLLM lane and most of those are RIGHT:

citation n verdict nccl, all_gather / reduce_scatter / all_to_all 414 correct — not implemented by CustomAllreduce nccl, all_reduce 84 the vLLM lane exists; applied where it helps (see §5) trtllm, gemm 42 correct — lanes agree to 0.4-3.6% trtllm, attention 12 sliding-window and L40S/A100 gaps; see the absences in §5 trtllm, moe 12 the vLLM lane differs by architecture; untried sglang / trtllm, recurrent 4 vLLM kda and linear_attention data exists; untried sglang, gemm / moe 4 A100's only lane for those families vllm 82 decode and prefill attention, all five served parts, plus A100

One collection per part, per family. Globbing collections mixes engine versions and silently changes the row set — it once produced 66,148 rows where the committed fit used 40,367. A difference between two parts should be the silicon, not a software release.

docs.title: 3. The three-level data separation
docs.text:
Fitting principles §3.1 supersedes this section's "evaluation only" rule for end-to-end rows: InferenceX end-to-end points are split 40/60 into fit and held-out sets.

source role why that role AISimulate per-operator sweeps fitting per-kernel, lane-labelled, and the only data that isolates one primitive HF FPM whole-forward (Apache-2.0) validation, model selection, and fitting a COMPOSED term one synchronized forward pass at a known batch and KV composition — the quantity the kernel composes, with no scheduler InferenceX measured rows evaluation only end-to-end with a scheduler and a client; never enters a fit or a selection InferenceX remaining rows reporting only their engine settings are not stated per run vLLM start-up logs in the vLLM issue tracker anchoring an assumed magnitude only vLLM's own measurement of CUDA-graph capture memory, on uncontrolled deployments; the only public record of that quantity (§11)

What FPM may and may not fit, and why the rule changed. An earlier revision of this table read "validation and model selection" and forbade FPM from entering any fit. The reason given was a confound: model and system were perfectly collinear, so a model holdout was also a chip holdout and a change across it could be attributed to neither. That is no longer true of the dataset. Derived from the catalog index rather than recalled:

model systems it appears on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash b200-sxm, b300-sxm, gb200, gb300, h200-sxm DeepSeek-V4-Pro b200-sxm, b300-sxm, gb300 MiniMax-M2.7 b200-sxm, h200-sxm GLM-5.2-NVFP4 b200-sxm, gb200

Four of seven models now span multiple systems, and b200-sxm carries six models against gb300's three, so both axes vary independently. A chip holdout is no longer a model holdout. The confound that justified the prohibition has dissolved, and keeping the prohibition would now cost accuracy for no methodological gain.

The distinction that remains, and it is a real one, is what kind of quantity each dataset constrains:

  • AISimulate isolates ONE primitive. A GEMM sweep varies M with everything else held, so it identifies that primitive's two parameters and nothing else. This is the only data that can fit a per-primitive coefficient, and every measured entry in this registry still comes from it.
  • FPM constrains a COMPOSITION. One latency_ms per (batch, prefill_tokens, kv_tokens) is the sum over every layer and every resource. Fitting a per-primitive coefficient against it is under-determined: many assignments across the primitives produce the same total, so the fit would attribute to one term whatever every other term gets wrong. That is not a provenance rule, it is an identifiability fact, and it does not change with the dataset.

So FPM may fit a term that is itself about composition — the overlap-band choice (docs/registry/band-selection.md), the attention-DP funnel factor, a per-step host constant — because those are properties of the whole forward pass and FPM measures the whole forward pass. It may not fit an attention rate or a GEMM asymptote, because nothing in a whole-pass total identifies those separately.

Three obligations on any FPM-fitted term, so the looser rule does not become a looser standard:

  1. Hold out along a dimension the term must generalise across — a chip, a model, or a parallelism — and report train and holdout error separately. §4 lists the splits the dataset now supports.
  2. Cite FPM explicitly, by dataset revision SHA, since the dataset is rewritten and has no tags.
  3. Keep the end-to-end check. FPM is not the evaluation corpus, so a term fitted on it still has to face InferenceX, and the standing rule below still governs.

No committed coefficient cites FPM today. This records what is permitted, so the next composed term does not have to argue the rule from scratch.

scripts/select_overlap_band.py enforces the last two by refusing any path under an inferencex or semianalysis directory, and a new fitter should import that guard rather than restate it.

FPM is entirely vLLM — all 85,484 rows carry backend: vllm — and splits as 12,522 pure decode, 5,226 pure prefill, 67,736 mixed prefill+decode.

The constraint that governs everything else: a better fit to a component benchmark can be a worse model. Six independently verified corrections each improved a per-primitive or per-step measurement and made the end-to-end score worse, because the kernel's accuracy rests on partially cancelling errors. So no per-primitive fit ships without an end-to-end check, and a correction whose offsetting term is unidentified waits.

The sixth is the clearest case and is worth stating in full, because it shows the rule catching something that every other gate passed. attention_decode_floor_mla was fitted from AISimulate's mla_generation_module_perf tables, committed as method: measured, fitted: true, and the fit was clean — it reproduced from its own writer, satisfied the schema, and sat inside every physical bound then checked. It was also wrong about which quantity it measured: those tables are MODULE measurements covering the whole MLA block including its down-projections, and the catalog's graph prices qkv_proj and o_proj as separate GEMM nodes in the same layer, so the kernel charged the projection weight read twice. scripts/fit_attention_mla.py had already recorded the arithmetic (DeepSeek-V3's projections are 293.6 MB at fp8, 61.2 µs at H200's 4.80 TB/s, against a 44.0–63.8 µs measured module floor) as its reason for being rejected; the pair was nonetheless committed later from the same tables.

Only the end-to-end check found it. Scored as a 2×2 over the two terms on the InferenceX corpus (573 points, vLLM lane):

floor rate overall TPOT mean|e| kimi-k2.5 TPOT part-wide fitted 14.98% 6.38% part-wide part-wide 14.90% 6.91% fitted (module) part-wide 17.32% 15.38% fitted (module) fitted 17.43% 14.57%

The rate is sound — 0.80–1.13× of each part's part-wide rate, the right order for a latent-cache read, and the only arm that improves kimi-k2.5 on its own. The floor was the entire regression: either arm carrying it lands near 15% on kimi-k2.5 and 17.3% overall, flipping the kernel from beating AISimulate's 15.39% to losing to it. scripts/correct_mla_floor.py commits the floor as assumed from the same part's measured attention-kernel floor, and three gates now hold it: that script's --check, relane_attention_mla.py --check-rate for the half still fitted, and a property test bounding any kind-specific floor at 3× its part-wide sibling.

The generalizable lesson is not "distrust module tables" but a fit can be clean and still answer a different question than the coefficient asks. Provenance of the number is not provenance of the quantity, and only a check at the level the model is used at can tell them apart.

docs.title: 4. Train, validate, evaluate
docs.text:
Fitting splits are taken along a dimension generalization actually has to cross, not at random — a random row split puts near-duplicate shapes on both sides and reports a generalization that was never tested.

  • GEMM shape ramp: whole k VALUES held out, so a test shape has a reduction depth the fit never saw. Train and test agree to within 0.04x on every part and dtype.
  • FPM topology: MiniMax-M2.7 on h200_sxm spans six topologies (dep/tp1/ep2, dep/tp1/ep4, pure_tp/tp2/ep1, pure_tp/tp4/ep1, tep/tp2/ep2, tep/tp4/ep4), so a parallelism-dependent term can be validated with model and chip fixed.
  • FPM regime: fit on pure-prefill and pure-decode rows, validate on the 67,736 mixed rows, whose batch composition varies independently of concurrency.

A confound that WAS true and no longer is: an earlier revision recorded model and system as perfectly collinear in FPM — DeepSeek-V4-Pro only on gb300, GLM-5.2 only on b200_sxm, MiniMax-M2.7 only on h200_sxm — so a model holdout was also a chip holdout. The dataset has since grown and that is false: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash spans five systems, DeepSeek-V4-Pro three, MiniMax-M2.7 and GLM-5.2-NVFP4 two each, and b200-sxm carries six models. Both axes now vary independently, which is what makes the holdouts above attributable and what §3 relies on in permitting FPM to fit a composed term.

The confound is recorded rather than deleted because the figures it produced are still in this document's history, and a reader comparing revisions needs to know which claim held when. Re-derive the current state from the catalog index rather than trusting either version: the dataset is rewritten in place.

Errors are reported for train, validation AND evaluation. A fit quoted only on its training data is not a result.

docs.title: 5. Per-part provenance
docs.text:
Counts in this section were taken when it was written. The current counts, generated from coefficients/ on every documentation build, are on the reference pages.

Coefficient counts by citation lane:

chip total nccl vllm trtllm sglang other h200 100 63 @ 2.29.2 13 @ 0.24.0/0.25.0 10 @ 1.3.0rc20 — 14 h100 104 63 @ 2.29.2 13 @ 0.24.0/0.25.0 12 @ 1.3.0rc20 2 @ 0.5.16 14 b200 102 63 @ 2.29.2 13 @ 0.24.0/0.25.0 12 @ 1.3.0rc20 — 14 b300 102 63 @ 2.29.2 13 @ 0.24.0/0.25.0 12 @ 1.3.0rc20 — 14 gb200-nvl72 78 48 @ 2.29.2 4 @ 0.25.0 12 @ 1.3.0rc20 — 14 l40s 100 72 @ 2.27.3 4 @ 0.24.0 10 @ 1.3.0rc20 — 14 a100-sxm 94 63 @ 2.27.3 13 @ 0.14.0 — 4 @ 0.5.10 14 a100-80 174 126 @ 2.27.3 22 @ 0.14.0 — 4 @ 0.5.10 22

other is the non-AISimulate set: host overheads, HBM derate, communicator sizes.

docs.title: Version pins, stated rather than averaged away
docs.text: A100's vLLM collection is 0.14.0 and L40S's is 0.24.0, against 0.25.0 on the Hopper and Blackwell parts. Those are the newest vLLM collections AISimulate ships for those SKUs. Pinning one collection per part keeps a difference between parts attributable to silicon; it also means A100's coefficients describe an older engine, and that is a property of the data rather than a choice.

docs.title: A100-80 is an alias
docs.text:
a100-80 and a100-sxm are the same silicon — identical TFlopsPeak 312, BwPeakTBs 2.039, MemoryGiB 80, SMCount 108 — and the catalog's own chip file says "Alias for A100-SXM". Both names appear in hardware_config.json, so a BLIS run can request either.

Aliasing is done two ways, deliberately:

  • Where the coefficient NAME has no chip suffix, a100-80 is added to a100-sxm's scope, so one measurement serves both names and a refit cannot update one and miss the other. The kernel matches scope by membership (resolve.Scope.Admits).
  • The collective names DO carry a chip suffix, because the kernel builds the key as collective_<kind>_<op>_<dtype>_<rank>rank_<chip> with - replaced by _. A membership scope cannot satisfy that, so 72 measured *_a100_80 entries carry A100-SXM's values with the alias stated in each rationale (24 more are the derived 16-rank widths). Re-fit both together. Every *_a100_sxm entry is scoped to a100-sxm alone: an a100-80 deployment builds the _a100_80 name and never looks them up, so the 72 that listed it in their scope said nothing.
  • The descriptor entries (hbm_derate, host_link_bandwidth, the NCCL buffer sizes, engine_workspace_bytes) come from systems/a100_sxm.yaml alone, scoped to both names. An earlier revision also emitted systems/a100_pcie.yaml for a100-80, which put two entries of every descriptor name in scope for it; the values were equal, so nothing was mispriced, but the kernel kept whichever came later and a refit of one copy would have moved the answer silently.

docs.title: Deliberate absences
docs.text:
Absent is not the same as missing:

  • gemm_*_fp8 and gemm_*_fp8_block on A100 — the part has TFlopsFP8: 0, so dtypeFit returns the bf16 suffix. A fraction of a rate the silicon does not have would be worse than nothing.
  • attention_decode_*_swa on A100 — vLLM 0.14.0's schema has no window_size column; the sliding-window sweep postdates it. The kernel falls back to the unsuffixed pair.
  • int8 all-reduce on A100 stays on NCCL — allreduce_dtype in the custom_allreduce sweep is bfloat16 across all 138 rows, so there is no vLLM int8 measurement. Unmeasured is not unchanged.
  • L40S sliding-window decode is on the vLLM lane (vllm/0.24.0, its newest vLLM attention collection) by decision, at a measured cost. Commit 5be809b moved it for lane correctness — the alternative sums two engines in one step for every windowed model on the part — knowing its held-out folds favour TRT-LLM (§7.1: 2.073x against 1.681x, 0 of 2 folds won). The trade is recorded here rather than reverted. An earlier revision of this bullet said it stayed on TRT-LLM; the committed entries never did after 5be809b.
  • L40S all-reduce stays on NCCL — the vLLM-graph floors agree with NCCL to within 13%, because L40S has no NVLink (PCIe Gen4, 32 GB/s) and custom_allreduce needs peer-to-peer NVLink to help. A100-SXM has NVLink 3 at 300 GB/s and its floors drop 2.1-3.8x, which is the same mechanism that moved the Hopper and Blackwell parts.

docs.title: 6. Reproducing any value
docs.text:
Every fitted coefficient names its script in the rationale. The fitters are pure: given the same collection they print the same numbers, and the validator re-runs them.

scripts/fit_attention.py <data>/<sku>/attention/<lane>          --chip <chip>
scripts/fit_attention_prefill.py --collection <lane> <sku>:<chip>
scripts/fit_attention_by_kind.py --collection <lane> --sku <sku> --chip <chip>
scripts/fit_collectives_vllm.py <data>/<sku>/comm/vllm/<version>
scripts/fit_collectives.py <data>/<sku>/comm/nccl/<version>
scripts/fit_gemm_envelope.py <data>/<sku>/gemm/<lane>
scripts/fit_gemm_shape_ramp.py [--emit] <sku>:<chip>
scripts/probe_cudagraph_dispatch.py --settings S --corpus C
scripts/emit_memory.py [--check]
scripts/mine_vllm_cudagraph_memory.py {fetch,extract} CACHE_DIR

Two traps these scripts exist to avoid, both of which produced wrong answers by hand:

  • latency is MILLISECONDS in every AISimulate parquet. Reading it as seconds gives 2,070 TB/s on a 4.8 TB/s part, or a 143,314 GB/s collective peak. The error announces itself if you check the number against the datasheet, and not otherwise.
  • FPM's total_kv_read_tokens is summed OVER THE BATCH, while the kernel takes a per-sequence context. Joining them directly is a 256x KV error at batch 256; the join is on (batch, batch*ctx == kv_total).

docs.title: 6.0 What is reproducible, and what is not
docs.text:
Five kinds of value live in this registry. Counted from the coefficient files themselves (1,143 entries in six sets):

method entries reproducible by measured 844 a named fitter in scripts/, re-run by the validator vendor_spec 57 NVIDIA's own descriptor or simulator source, transcribed by a writer with --check assumed 239 a derivation script where one exists; otherwise nothing — each states its reasoning and what would replace it transferred 1 nothing to reproduce: another scope's value carried by a stated rule, transferred_from naming it -- an assumed transfer, not a derivation (DeepSeek-V4.1's host_launch_eager_per_kernel off h200, §10.6) not_charged 2 nothing to reproduce: a declared zero (cudagraph_capture_bytes_none; DeepSeek-V4.1's host_admission_per_request, §10.6, an inferred zero the schema requires to carry this method)

The 239 assumed entries are of four different kinds, and the difference matters to a reader weighing one:

  • Derived from this project's own measurements — 212 entries, each regenerated by a script. 204 collective triples close rank-width and part gaps (extrapolate_collective_width.py, extrapolate_by_generation.py, each holdout-validated, §8.5); A100's two sliding-window attention entries scale its own measured full-attention floor and rate by its kernel sibling's windowed/full ratio (extrapolate_by_generation.py); six attention_decode_floor_mla entries are set from the part's own measured attention floor (correct_mla_floor.py, §3).
  • Derived from committed siblings — 8 entries, all fit_deepseek_v41_h200.py (§10.5), four per part on h200 and h100, each from that part's own siblings and descriptor: the indexer-scan rate at NVIDIA's empirical HBM rate (BwPeak × hbm_derate, not a bound; at most 1.25x pessimistic, its optimism unbounded), the weight-only MXFP8 ramp at the measured BF16 envelope (an upper bound on the asymptote; the knee is not a bound), and the engram host-gather rate at the PCIe 5.0 line rate (an upper bound). Each states its direction where one is known, and each is re-derived from its siblings by a property test that needs no sweep.
  • Fitted on a neighbouring kernel's measurements — 6 entries, all fit_deepseek_v41_prefill.py (§10.6): V4.1's prefill indexer, fitted on the paged logits kernel's prefill-shaped rows because vLLM runs the ragged kernel there, which is measured only on the SGLang lane, with the lane decision open (§10.6 states the gap).
  • Not derivable from any dataset this project reads — 13 entries. The seven host overheads in cost-model-host-overheads.yaml: no dataset measures client-observed host time (AISimulate times kernels, FPM times one synchronized forward pass — all 42 of its columns were enumerated, and there is no ttft, e2e, client, queue or host column — and InferenceX is evaluation-only). And the four capturing cudagraph_capture_bytes_<mode> entries in cost-model-memory.yaml, whose magnitude is anchored on vLLM's own start-up logs (§11); their anchor is reproducible from a committed CSV, but the samples are uncontrolled deployments, which is why the method stays assumed. And DeepSeek-V4.1's host_launch_eager_per_kernel, backed out of a vendored end-to-end enforce-eager anchor (fit_deepseek_v41_host.py, §10.6), and its host_admission_per_token, a front-end timing taken on an Apple M1 Max and transferred to every part, because no serving node's CPU was measured (§10.6).

Each of those thirteen carries the measurement that would replace it. host_admission_per_request names the exact experiment, a client-observed TTFT measurement at 1-token and 1,024-token prompts against a running vLLM server at concurrency 1 with a warm cache, whose intercept is the coefficient with no evaluation data involved. The capture entries name one log line from one start-up of the target deployment.

This boundary is stated rather than smoothed over because the largest single accuracy movement in this work — TTFT mape 52.94% to 31.47% on the measured tier — comes from one of the seven.

docs.title: 6.1 Reproducing the end-to-end evaluation tables
docs.text:
End-to-end accuracy figures, which compare a simulation with a measured InferenceX run, come from one place: the accuracy dashboard's scoring harness, a signed and versioned tool (design §2.2, §11.7). This registry holds no scorer of its own, because two scorers would sooner or later disagree about what a figure means. To see what a registry change does end to end, run the harness with a simulator build and this registry's directory as its registry path. Its figures on published fit units inform review; they are never landing evidence for an accuracy change (design §11.7).

A figure is a claim about every input that produced it: the simulator build, the catalog, the registry and the harness digest. The harness records all four with every figure, so a reader can reproduce it.

docs.title: 6.2 Which tier to weigh
docs.text:
inferencex_engine_settings.json records 68 sweeps with a captured engine-args log and 136 without, each of the latter listed in its incomplete array with reason: "no engine-args log". For those 136 the engine configuration is resolved from vLLM's defaults rather than observed, so an error there is as likely to be a wrong assumed configuration as a wrong model.

The measured tier is the only one where the simulated deployment is ground truth. It is therefore the tier on which a coefficient change can be attributed to the model, and the tier to weigh when judging one. The resolved tier answers a weaker and still useful question — how well a predictor does when it must guess the configuration too — and mixing the two in one average mixes two kinds of evidence, which is why the scorer takes -config-tier and the baseline records them separately.

docs.title: 6.3 Validation gates
docs.text:
pytest validator/ runs the registry's derivation / value-preservation gates. Schema and provenance validation are validate-registry's, the Go validator in validate/ that loads through the same types every consumer uses (Validation). The derivation gates that matter:
