The GEMM envelope re-derives, and is checked against the committed value, with its owner:

python scripts/relane_gemm_envelope.py --check

docs.title: cost-model-collectives.yaml — generated
docs.text:
This set is generated in two passes, because its entries come from two different lanes.

python scripts/emit_collectives.py "$AISIMULATE_DATA" > /tmp/collectives-nccl.yaml

That regenerates the NCCL-sourced entries. Checked against the committed file, all 435 entries that cite an NCCL collection reproduce with no value difference. The generator is pinned to the collections those entries cite (PINNED_NCCL: 2.27.3 for A100 and L40S, 2.29.2 elsewhere) rather than taking the newest directory. That pin matters: AISimulate has since added NCCL 2.30.7, which carries 60 rows under a narrower schema with no device or version column where 2.29.2 carries 504 under the full one, so "newest wins" would both crash and silently re-cite the entries. Set NCCL_COLLECTION to move a fit deliberately.

The remaining 45 entries are all all_reduce, and they do not come from NCCL. vLLM uses its own one-shot/two-shot kernel for any tensor-parallel all-reduce that fits the custom kernel's size limit, which AISimulate measures separately; on matched (num_gpus, message_size) pairs the custom kernel under CUDA graph is the faster by a median factor of 0.635, so an NCCL-derived coefficient over-charges a graph-mode all-reduce by about 1.6×. Those 45 ship from the vLLM lane:

python scripts/fit_collectives_vllm.py --all "$AISIMULATE_DATA"

Re-running the NCCL pass alone will therefore differ from the committed file on exactly those 45 entries, and on nothing else. A reproducer should expect that.

Every entry is method: measured. The 208 with fitted: true are curve fits; the remainder are order statistics — a floor is the minimum over the size-independent region, not a regression — which is why they are fitted: false while still being measurements with their own Parquet citation.

The 72 _a100_80 entries are the one group the NCCL pass cannot emit from this checkout: a100_pcie ships no comm/ tree. They are scoped to a100-80 and carry the A100-SXM measurement — 63 citing a100_sxm/comm/nccl/2.27.3, the other 9 the vLLM custom-all-reduce sweep — so each names the sweep it actually comes from rather than claiming an A100-PCIe measurement that does not exist. Treating the two A100 80GB parts as one for collectives is a modelling choice, recorded in each entry's rationale.

docs.title: cost-model-attention.yaml — fitted per part
docs.text:
Decode (attention_decode_floor, attention_decode_rate), fitted on the vLLM lane:

python scripts/fit_attention.py "$AISIMULATE_DATA"/h200_sxm/attention/vllm/0.25.0 --chip h200

which prints attention_decode_floor 13.5 us and 0.54 of 4.800 TB/s — that is the committed attention_decode_rate of 2,592,000 bytes/µs — over 34,818 full-attention points, the count its citation records.

Prefill (attention_prefill_floor, attention_prefill_work_scale):

# Five parts have a vLLM 0.25.0 context-attention sweep.
python scripts/fit_attention_prefill.py --collection vllm/0.25.0 \
    h200_sxm:h200 h100_sxm:h100 b200_sxm:b200 b300_sxm:b300 gb200:gb200-nvl72

# L40S and A100 do not. Each ships from the newest vLLM lane that has one,
# which is what their `sources` entries cite.
python scripts/fit_attention_prefill.py --collection vllm/0.24.0 l40s:l40s
python scripts/fit_attention_prefill.py --collection vllm/0.14.0 a100_sxm:a100-sxm

Expected output, matching the committed entries and the point counts in their citations:

part lane floor µs work_scale points h200 vllm/0.25.0 18.5 0.44 27,693 h100 vllm/0.25.0 19.5 0.44 27,693 b200 vllm/0.25.0 16.5 0.38 27,574 b300 vllm/0.25.0 15.0 0.44 27,574 gb200-nvl72 vllm/0.25.0 17.0 0.38 27,574 l40s vllm/0.24.0 13.0 0.50 26,267 a100-sxm vllm/0.14.0 19.5 0.50 5,457

--collection defaults to trtllm/1.3.0rc20, the lane an earlier revision of these coefficients was fitted on, so that fit also stays reproducible; pass the lane explicitly for the values currently committed. Only full attention is fitted — rows with a non-zero window_size read a bounded number of bytes, and fitting them together would fit one curve to two byte counts.

docs.title: cost-model-recurrent.yaml — fitted per family
docs.text:
# KDA (Kimi-K3), h100 / h200 / gb300. Re-derives all six entries and diffs them
# against the committed file; --insert CHIP adds a part the set does not carry yet.
python scripts/relane_recurrent_kda.py --check

# MAMBA2 (Nemotron-3-Ultra). The model filter is required to reproduce the committed
# values: this sweep carries six geometries and pooling them fits none of them.
python scripts/fit_recurrent.py \
    "$AISIMULATE_DATA"/h100_sxm/linear_attention/trtllm/1.3.0rc20/mamba2_perf.parquet \
    --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4

The second prints n=11 floor=3.5us rate=8.50 tok/us geo-err 1.120x, which is both committed *_mamba2 value and the error its rationale states. Without --model the same command pools 66 rows across six models and prints 4.2/23.25 — a number that is in the file's history nowhere and should not be mistaken for a refit.

The KDA command prints h100 3.8us/0.235, h200 4.3us/0.237 and gb300 7.4us/0.457, which are the committed values. Do not fit KDA from kda/sglang/0.5.16 or take the kda_fused_decode row: an earlier revision of this guide did, and both are wrong. fused_kda_decode is AMD-only — vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py gates on gfx942/gfx950 — so it runs on no CUDA deployment, and vLLM's NVIDIA path (nvidia/kda.py:980-993) runs causal_conv1d_update then fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode, so a layer costs the sum. The superseded recipe gives floor 5.1 µs and rate 1.50 tok/µs, a rate 6.4× too fast.

What this data does and does not cover matters more here than anywhere else in the registry, and the script's header says it: KDA (Kimi-K3) is complete, carrying the convolution and the recurrent scan separately plus a fused decode variant. MAMBA2 is not — the sweep has only causal_conv1d_fn and causal_conv1d_update, so the committed *_mamba2 pair is the convolution alone and is a documented LOWER BOUND on a Mamba2 layer, not its cost. The selective-scan kernel is in no collection in the tree.

docs.title: Sliding-window attention — *_swa
docs.text:
The windowed entries are fitted by a separate script, because a windowed kernel reads a number of bytes bounded by the window rather than by the context. scripts/relane_attention_swa.py owns them and reads its values from scripts/fit_attention_by_kind.py:

python scripts/relane_attention_swa.py --collection vllm/0.25.0 --check

The windowed entries were relaned from TRT-LLM to vLLM (methodology §7.1), and each entry's citation names the collection it was fitted on: vllm/0.25.0 on the Hopper and Blackwell parts, vllm/0.24.0 on L40S, whose newest vLLM collection that is. Pass the collection the entry cites; the A100 pair is assumed and is written by extrapolate_by_generation.py instead.

Using the context length for both kinds is what made an early windowed fit land at 2.00 of datasheet peak — a physically impossible rate, and the reason the two kinds are fitted apart rather than together.

docs.title: InferenceX CollectiveX run bodies ($COLLECTIVEX_DATA)
docs.text:
Three writers read CollectiveX run bodies: fit_deepep_ll_graph.py, fit_host_link.py and fit_deepep_collectivex.py. Fetch the run list and each body from

https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/api/v1/collectivex/runs?version=1
https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/api/v1/collectivex/runs/<run_id>?version=1

and save each body as cx_run_<run_id>.body. The query must be the bare integer version=1: without it, or with v1, the API answers {"error":"Unknown version"}. scripts/fetch_cited_inferencex.py <dir> does this for the bodies the committed entries cite that the API still serves, and fails unless the points of each match the pinned digest; the rederive workflow runs it. The bodies are third-party data and are not committed.

The API keeps a bounded window of recent runs, so a cited run can stop being fetchable. The DeepEP writer checks that the bodies its committed entries cite are present and that their points hash to the cited digest (scripts/collectivex_points.py: the series, point and p50 the fit reads, not the body's bytes, which the API changed on 2026-11-07 without changing a point). If they are not, it exits 3 rather than re-fit and re-cite the entries on other runs, and validator/test_deepep_ll_graph.py skips with "the cited CollectiveX bodies are not present". The entries fit_deepep_ll_graph.py and fit_host_link.py wrote cite runs the API no longer serves (33356406487, 36334392363, 36367074689, 36402856875, and the swap_blocks bodies sha256 26cad6ccbdaa; each answered 404 on 2026-11-05). They stay as committed, and cannot be re-derived from public data. Their two tests are on .github/quarantine.yaml under inference-sim/blis-registry#57, so the gate reports them and fails when the entries expire, until the bodies are restored or the entries are re-cited through a reviewed refit.

The OperatorX response fit_marlin_nvfp4_grouped_ramp.py cites is cited by the digest of the rows that fit reads (scripts/operatorx_points.py), not by its bytes: the URL served a different response by 2026-11-05, with the same rows and so the same values (h100 0.237 and 24, h200 0.230 and 61). fetch_cited_inferencex.py fetches it with the run bodies, and validator/test_operatorx.py runs in the gate and is no longer quarantined.

docs.title: Offload tiers
docs.text:
A storage tier (catalog/devices/storage.yaml) is a name and a description. What a transfer to or from it costs is three coefficients per tier, offload_tier_<tier>_read_rate, _write_rate (bytes per microsecond, which is MB/s) and _base_latency (microseconds per transfer), in cost-model-offload-tiers.yaml. The set is separate from cost-model-primitives because that set is single-sourced to NVIDIA AISimulate (a test refuses any non-measured entry there that cites another measurement), and these figures are not AISimulate's. A scenario whose deployment offloads to a tier lists the set; the kernel refuses to build when it does not. The kernel's TierTime prices a transfer as max(base_latency, bytes / rate) for the direction, with the rate held to the chip's host_link_bandwidth and divided by the queue depth. They are in the registry because none is a declared fact of a device (design SUB-18, SUB-3): the catalog held them as the tiers' own figures, and every one was either a fit to a single host or a value the simulator's authors chose.

What each is. Before this change the catalog stated, for six tiers, a read rate, a write rate and a base latency. The registry now holds the same figures to the digit, for every catalog chip, so no offload price moved (kernel/tiers_test.go holds the old figures as a table and prices every tier on every chip against them).

Tier Method Why nvme_gen4, nvme_gen3, sata_ssd, s3 assumed, every chip Representative classes seeded in inference-sim's defaults with no source cited; a class is not a product. nvme_gen4_raid0_8x assumed, DGX H100 node; the same figures assumed on the other chips The drive model is not public. Read is NVIDIA's > 50 GB/s design target and 8 x the measured PM1733 rate; write is 8 x the PM1733 datasheet; latency is a sum of cited per-file costs. cpu_dram rates transferred, from the H100 host (hardware=h100), on every chip Fitted to InferenceX CollectiveX swap_blocks rows on one H100 host at vLLM v0.27.1; the engine priced issues the same copies from swap_blocks_batch, so the engine is not the one measured (design D5, VAL-8) and the large-payload rate carries over by a stated rule. On other chips it is the same figure, now labeled; TierTime holds a slower host link to its own host_link_bandwidth. cpu_dram base latency assumed, every chip The small-copy floor of swap_blocks does not carry over to a batched call; it is held as a judgement that the floors are alike.

Regenerate. emit_offload_tiers.py writes every entry and holds every figure; it needs no data:

cd registry
python scripts/emit_offload_tiers.py          # write
python scripts/emit_offload_tiers.py --check  # exit 1 if the committed file would change
python -m pytest validator/test_offload_tiers.py -q

It reads the catalog's chip list, so a chip added there fails --check until the writer has run for it. The expected output of --check is cost-model-offload-tiers.yaml already matches and exit 0. It costs about a second. To add a tier, add its name to catalog/devices/storage.yaml and its three figures, method and rationale to emit_offload_tiers.py.

The one fitted source. The cpu_dram rates are the medians fit_host_link.py derives for host_link_bandwidth (contiguous, payload >= 64 MiB, all block sizes, 26 points per direction: host to device 27,058, device to host 46,089); that script refuses when its median for either direction is not the committed tier rate, so the cap and the tier are one fit. Its data are the InferenceX CollectiveX run bodies cited by sha256 26cad6ccbdaa (runs 35158674963 and 36334394602, public InferenceX Data API), which the API no longer serves; the fit cannot be re-derived from public data today, and its gate sits on the quarantine list with the rest of that family (see above). The cpu_dram floor (19.3 µs, the mean of the two directions' 19.7 and 18.9) rests on the same rows and is held as an assumption. A held-out check (random layout, payload >= 1 MiB: median absolute error of p50 latency 0.51 host to device and 0.14 device to host, against 0.55 and 0.98 for the 2.0e4 MB/s and 1 µs placeholder it replaced) is on the two rate entries as validated.

What it does not show. None of the six tiers is timed on the engine and version the kernel prices, on any chip but one H100 host, and that host's rates are not measurements of swap_blocks_batch. The assumed figures are not bounds: a deep queue on a drive, or a store under load, can sit well below them. The queue-depth rule divides the rate and does not model saturation. The NVMe aggregate is optimistic at low concurrency, because one O_DIRECT stream does not reach the aggregate on md RAID 0. No cpu_dram figure exists for a host other than the one H100 DGX host; a Grace host's link is held to its own host_link_bandwidth, which says what the link can do and not what the copy engines do over it.

docs.title: Dense Marlin MXFP8 ramp on Hopper (transferred)
docs.text:
On SM90, vLLM v0.31.0 runs every dense MXFP8 linear with MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel (W8A16). No sweep times it on any part. The registry carries its ramp as the assumed bound on h100 and h200, and as a transferred pair on h200 only:

  • gemm_eps_max_w8a16_mxfp8 and gemm_m_half_w8a16_mxfp8, assumed: the part's cuBLAS BF16 envelope (1.0 / 170 on h100, 0.992 / 110 on h200). The registry calls it an optimistic upper bound for a compute-bound GEMM. Owned by fit_deepseek_v41_h200.py; it stays.
  • The same two names on h200, transferred: the same part's measured Marlin grouped pair (gemm_*_w4a16_mxfp4_grouped: 0.245 / 26), moved to the dense kernel by one rule (same library, same Marlin kernel family and MMA core, same die; the pair is kept whole and never taken from the other part). Owned by emit_marlin_dense_transfer.py.
  • The h100 pair (0.282 / 15, by the same rule from h100's own grouped pair) is a candidate and is not selected. It is written to registry/candidates/dense-marlin-mxfp8-transferred.yaml, which is outside the registry's data directories (acceptance, coefficients, routing), so the embedded registry, the lookup and the validators do not read it. h100 has no withheld series, so the landing criteria (the page added at the top of this stack) give it no verdict, and the assumed bound keeps pricing it in released output. To select it, a held-out verdict for h100 must exist; then the writer's ACTIVE_PARTS takes h100 and the entries move into cost-model-primitives.yaml.

The lookup uses the entry of the smallest method rank (design 9.2, VAL-4), so on h200 the transferred pair prices the GEMM and the assumed bound is the entry it displaces. Remove the transferred pair and the price returns to the bound. The h200 pair is still subject to the held-out verdict the landing criteria describe; it is not select-gated here.

cd registry
python scripts/emit_marlin_dense_transfer.py          # write
python scripts/emit_marlin_dense_transfer.py --check  # exit 1 if the committed file would change
python -m pytest validator/test_coefficient_properties.py -q -k "dense_marlin or h100"

It reads only the committed grouped entries: no sweep, no catalog, no end-to-end result. Expected output of --check: cost-model-primitives.yaml and dense-marlin-mxfp8-transferred.yaml already match the transfer, exit 0; it costs well under a second. Writers that share the file identify an entry by name, scope and method (coefficient_blocks.py), so the assumed and transferred pairs are maintained independently. That test run covers the h200 pair, the h100 candidate record and this --check.

What it does not show. Dense Marlin was never timed. The entries are unkeyed: the engine reports no kernel implementation for a GEMM, so they state no kernel_impls and a price records their kernel match as unkeyed, never exact. They carry transferred, which for the closeness grade (design 11.3) is a G2 condition, the same grade the assumed bound already gave; they do not make a point G1. The grouped fit sums its compute and memory halves over 27 token counts of one MoE shape, and whether the dense kernel shares that composition, or holds at other GEMM shapes, is not shown. The effect on the development points is in-sample (the pair was chosen from the registry before the points were re-scored, but the points are the only end-to-end check available). A MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel sweep on one H100 and one H200, fitted like fit_marlin_grouped_ramp.py and written as measured with kernel_impls, replaces it.

docs.title: cost-model-host-overheads.yaml — not derived from either dataset
docs.text: All seven entries are method: assumed and none is fitted. These are host-side costs that neither dataset isolates — the script header notes that several could move to measured without cluster time, and should. Three of them cite the removed trained-physics set as an order-of-magnitude anchor only — the values there were fitted against a different functional form, and a coefficient is valid only for the form it was fitted against. The citations name the git SHA where that file can still be read.

docs.title: cost-model-memory.yaml — AISimulate's memory model, and vLLM's own logs
docs.text:
scripts/emit_memory.py writes the whole file, and --check gates it.

  • The activation multiples and floor are vendor_spec, read with ast from AISimulate's aisimulate_core/sdk/backends/ (located from $AISIMULATE_DATA, two directories up). Verified against AISimulate 70305030.
  • The CUDA-graph capture bytes are assumed, the median per mode of the committed registry/docs/vllm-cudagraph-capture-samples.csv. That CSV is regenerated from the vLLM issue tracker, which needs an authenticated gh and changes as issues are filed — so a re-mine is a deliberate data update, committed with its diff, not part of --check:
python scripts/mine_vllm_cudagraph_memory.py fetch   /tmp/vllm-cg-cache
python scripts/mine_vllm_cudagraph_memory.py extract /tmp/vllm-cg-cache \
    > registry/docs/vllm-cudagraph-capture-samples.csv
python scripts/emit_memory.py            # then review the value diff

The capture half needs no AISimulate tree, so test_capture_bytes_re_derive_from_the_committed_samples runs it in CI. Methodology §11 gives the composition these terms enter and why each is scoped as it is.

docs.title: Every committed value, and the one command that regenerates it
docs.text:
The table below is the reproducibility contract: each family names the script that owns it, and each of those scripts takes --check, which re-runs its own fitter and exits non-zero if the committed file would change. validator/test_writers_are_idempotent.py runs them all, and test_every_fitted_family_has_a_writer fails if a fitted family appears with no owner — so a value that cannot be regenerated cannot be added.

family writer source gemm_eps_max_*, gemm_m_half_* relane_gemm_envelope.py AISimulate gemm, vLLM lane moe_routing_imbalance_median relane_moe_imbalance.py AISimulate moe, vLLM lane gemm_*_w4a16_mxfp4_grouped fit_marlin_grouped_ramp.py AISimulate moe, vLLM MarlinExperts MXFP4 rows, h200, h100, gb300, b200 and b300; GB200 EP8/EP16 inside one NVL72, H200 EP16 over two nodes (scoped fabric: [ib-400g]) gemm_*_nvfp4_grouped (PARKED, none committed) fit_nvfp4_grouped_ramp.py ($AISIMULATE_NVFP4_DATA at aisimulate 8ae6b658) AISimulate moe/vllm/0.30.0 TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsMonolithic; its held-out error is no better than the dense nvfp4 ramp's on any part, so the kernel's fallback stands (see the script's docstring) fabric_bandwidth_efficiency (cost-model-fabric) emit_fabric.py --check (--verify DIR re-hashes the cited pages) NVIDIA/nccl-tests#309 for ib-400g (literature); roce-200g, ib-800g (equal to ib-400g, line rate from NVIDIA's Blackwell Ultra Datasheet) and ethernet-100gbe assumed with stated ranges host overheads (assumed) none — see that file's header not measured by either dataset activation_buffer_count_*, activation_scratch_floor_bytes emit_memory.py AISimulate sdk/backends source (vendor_spec) cudagraph_capture_bytes_* emit_memory.py registry/docs/vllm-cudagraph-capture-samples.csv, from mine_vllm_cudagraph_memory.py (assumed)

Derived entries carry their own reproduction too. Two scripts write method: assumed values, and both state the predictor, its holdout error and the parts it was derived from, inside the entry:

script what it derives predictor, and how it was chosen extrapolate_by_generation.py a family absent for one part same-generation median, or a kernel-matched within-part ratio; both chosen by leave-one-part-out holdout against every part that is fitted extrapolate_collective_width.py a 16-rank collective triple floor(n) = a + b(n−1) on that part's own {2,4,8}, holdout-validated against gb200-nvl72, the one part with a measured 16-rank floor

Neither script will write a value it cannot defend: they refuse a part whose generation has no fitted sibling, a prediction below the measured 8-rank floor, a set of fit widths spanning two lanes, and a lane with no same-lane holdout. A refusal is the correct output when the data does not support an estimate.

docs.title: Adding a part — the GB300 worked example
docs.text:
Every fitted family has a writer with --check (it re-runs its own fitter and exits non-zero if the committed file would change) and --insert CHIP (it appends a part the set does not carry yet, through the same renderer, so an inserted entry is byte-identical to what a later re-run produces). The order matters in one place: prefill attention reads the bf16 GEMM ramp from the registry, so the envelope must be committed first.

export AISIMULATE_DATA=<aisimulate>/python/aisimulate/src/aisimulate_core/systems/data
export BLIS_CATALOG=$PWD/../catalog

# 1. descriptors (vendor_spec, from NVIDIA's own systems/gb300.yaml)
#    emit_primitives.py owns this family; its GEMM/MoE path is superseded — see below.
# 2. GEMM ramp, then MoE imbalance
python scripts/relane_gemm_envelope.py  --insert gb300
python scripts/relane_moe_imbalance.py  --insert gb300
# 3. attention: decode, then prefill (needs the ramp from step 2), then windowed
python scripts/relane_attention_decode.py  --insert gb300 gb300:gb300
python scripts/relane_attention_prefill.py --insert gb300 gb300:gb300
python scripts/relane_attention_swa.py     --insert gb300 gb300:gb300
# 4. recurrent
python scripts/relane_recurrent_kda.py     --insert gb300 gb300:gb300
# 5. collectives, per operator from the lane each belongs on
python scripts/insert_collectives_part.py --chip gb300 --sku gb300

Then assert idempotence, which is what makes the result auditable:

for s in relane_gemm_envelope relane_moe_imbalance relane_attention_decode \
         relane_attention_prefill relane_attention_swa relane_recurrent_kda; do
    python scripts/$s.py --check || echo "$s DRIFTED"
done
python -m pytest validator/ -q

Do not run emit_primitives.py or emit_collectives.py to regenerate a whole set. Both predate lane decisions that moved families off them. emit_primitives.py's COLLECTIONS table still pins trtllm/1.3.0rc20 while every committed gemm_* entry cites a vLLM lane (5be809b), and regenerating cost-model-collectives.yaml from NCCL gives 144 removals and 36 changes — all 36 being the all_reduce entries 2f71dd6 moved to vLLM's custom kernel, so it would silently re-introduce a 3.4× mispricing. Use the per-family writers; they are what --check guards.

docs.title: 4. Why the registry holds only what the kernel reads
docs.text:
When the removals below were made, the cost model requested five sets (cost-model-primitives, cost-model-collectives, cost-model-host-overheads, cost-model-attention, cost-model-recurrent) and coefficients/ held exactly those, 724 entries.

cost-model-memory supplies the memory magnitudes the kernel had hard-coded (inference-sim/blis-registry#33); the cost model reads it (inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel#22). Every set under coefficients/ has a reader, and the reference overview lists the families within them that have none.

Four sets were removed because nothing in BLIS read them; they are recoverable from git history, where they last appear at 8d78ff8:

set what it held why it went communication-coefficients.yaml 10 named TP/MoE collectives the kernel prices collectives from cost-model-collectives; 9 of its 10 entries were assumed/copied placeholders, 7 of them the value 1.0 pd-transfer-estimates.yaml PD KV-transfer base latency, fabric overhead PDTransferTime prices from catalog facts instead legacy-kv-transfer.yaml pre-#1590 CPU↔GPU transfer defaults TierTime prices from catalog facts instead lora-adapter-costs.yaml Digital-Twin adapter terms no consumer

The kernel's TierTime and PDTransferTime take their numbers from the catalog's hardware facts — StorageDevice read/write bandwidths and base latency, IntraNodeBwGBps, InterNodeBwGBps — using only host_link_bandwidth from cost-model-primitives as a host-link ceiling. inference-sim does not read any of the four either; its own defaults.yaml carries the values its backends use.

The removal was verified to change nothing measurable. Scored against the InferenceX measured tier (-config-tier measured -framework vllm -length-range-ratio 1.0), the before and after reports are identical after stripping timestamps — every summary table, every GPU family, every model, the same n:

registry TPOT shape TPOT mape TTFT shape TTFT mape 747 entries, 9 sets 11.60% 13.52% 15.32% 50.68% 724 entries, 5 sets 11.60% 13.52% 15.32% 50.68%

Both runs used one binary, one catalog revision and one kernel revision, varying only the registry — the figures move with the catalog, so a comparison across catalog revisions proves nothing. n is 292/360/288/356.

Anyone extending the kernel to price offload tiers, PD transfer or LoRA should expect to calibrate those terms rather than recover them from history: the removed values were placeholders and transcriptions, not measurements.

docs.title: 5. Checking a re-derivation
docs.text:
python -m pytest validator/ -q        # derivation / value-preservation gates; schema validation is validate-registry's
python scripts/validate_against_aisimulate_tables.py   # oracle check against AISimulate's own tables

A re-fit that lands on a different number is not automatically a correction. This registry has recorded six independently verified per-primitive improvements that each made end-to-end accuracy worse, because the composed model's accuracy rests on partially cancelling errors. No per-primitive refit ships on the strength of its own fit quality alone; see the standing rule in methodology.md.

docs.title: 6. Reproducing the evaluation figures
docs.text: End-to-end accuracy figures come from the accuracy dashboard's scoring harness, the one scorer BLIS has (design §2.2, §11.7). Methodology §6.1 says how to run it on a registry change.

docs.title: The registry in BLIS
docs.text:
A latency estimate depends on three kinds of number, and BLIS keeps them apart:

Declared facts What a vendor states about a model or a chip: layer counts, head dimensions, peak FLOP rates, memory bandwidth. Someone wrote them down; nothing about them is learned. They live in the catalog. Learned numbers What a cost model needs but no datasheet states: the latency floor of a decode attention kernel on an H200, the bandwidth an 8-rank all-reduce actually reaches, the token count at which a GEMM gets halfway to peak efficiency. They are obtained by fitting measurements, or assumed where no measurement exists. They live here. Deployment choices What a particular run selects: the GPU, the parallelism, the engine settings. They are stated per run, in a scenario, and committed nowhere.

The test for which side of the first line a number falls on is simple: could a measurement revise it? A chip's SM count cannot be revised by a benchmark; its achievable bandwidth can. The first belongs in the catalog, the second in the registry.

docs.title: Where the registry sits
docs.text:
The registry is one directory of blis-substrate, beside the parts it works with:

Directory Holds Relationship to the registry contracts/ Go types and validators; no data Defines what a coefficient set may contain. validate-registry rejects any file that breaks the rules, on every pull request. catalog/ Models, chips, fabrics, workloads: declared facts The registry's scope.hardware values are the catalog's chip names (h200, gb200-nvl72, …). registry/ Coefficient sets: learned numbers with provenance — kernel/ The cost model: prices one forward pass Reads coefficient sets by name and evaluates its cost laws with them. Holds no numbers of its own.

The catalog and the registry are data, validated against the contracts. The cost model reads both through one loader, from the copy embedded in each release or from a directory given by path (design §3.3). The simulator, inference-sim, is the only repository that imports the cost model and the data.

docs.title: What happens at run time
docs.text:
A scenario names everything a run needs, including which coefficient sets to use:

kind: Scenario
name: kimi-k3-h100-nospec
engine_version: "0.29.0"
model: kimi-k3
coefficients: [cost-model-primitives, cost-model-collectives, cost-model-host-overheads, cost-model-attention, cost-model-recurrent]
cluster:
  hardware: h100
  ...

(Abridged from testdata/kernel/kimi-k3-h100-nospec.yaml in inference-sim.)

The kernel then does three things with the registry, once, before the first step:

  1. Loads each named set from <registry>/coefficients/<name>.yaml with the strict loader in contracts/, then validates it with the same rules the repository's CI runs. A file that fails either is refused before anything is priced.
  2. Filters by scope. An entry applies only if its scope admits the deployment: an entry scoped to hardware: [h200] is skipped on an H100. A dimension the scope does not mention is unconstrained.
  3. Resolves names. Sets apply in the order the scenario lists them; if two admitted entries share a name, the later one wins.

The result is a fixed table of numbers the kernel's cost laws read for the rest of the run.

What happens when a name is absent is the kernel's decision, made term by term in its new.go. Some lookups are required and fail with an error naming the missing coefficient. Many others fall back, usually to zero, so a part with no entry for a family has that term priced at nothing, and the run still completes. This is why coverage matters: the recurrent set fits every part its sweeps measure for exactly this reason.

docs.title: Why the learned numbers are kept apart from the code
docs.text:
Because a learned number is only as good as the evidence behind it, and the evidence has to travel with the number. Each coefficient carries its method, its sources and its scope; can be re-derived and checked in CI on its own; and changes by a pull request whose diff shows exactly which numbers moved. Because the simulator can read the registry from a directory instead of its embedded copy, a candidate registry is scored with the released simulator and no rebuild.

Next: what a coefficient records.

docs.title: A constant in a law
docs.text:
The kernel prices each primitive with a closed-form law. The registry supplies the constants in those laws, and nothing else. Three examples:

Primitive Law the kernel evaluates Constants the registry supplies Dense GEMM efficiency(M) = εmax · M / (M + M½) gemm_eps_max_<dtype>, gemm_m_half_<dtype> Decode attention latency = floor + KV bytes / rate attention_decode_floor, attention_decode_rate Collective latency = max(floor + size / rt, size / rpeak) collective_floor_…, collective_transition_rate_…, collective_peak_rate_…

The division matters. A law is code, reviewed as code, and the same for every part. A constant is data, specific to a part, and carries the evidence for its value. A constant is never a correction for one model: if a model is mispriced, the remedy is in the law or in the evidence, not in a per-model fudge factor.

It also means a coefficient is only meaningful for the law it was fitted against. Two constants with similar names in models of different form are different quantities. This is why sets do not inherit from one another.

docs.title: What an entry records
docs.text:
Each coefficient is one entry, keyed by its name:

Field Required Records value yes The number. Finite. units yes Its dimension, from a closed list (us_per_transfer, bytes_per_us, tokens, …). method yes How the value was obtained. See below. fitted yes Whether a curve fit produced it. scope yes Where it applies. See below. sources by method Citations: the exact file a value came from, and its role. rationale by method Why this value: what it replaced, what would replace it, where it is weak. ci95 no An interval [low, high] that must contain the value.

The file format lists every field and rule exactly.

docs.title: Method: how the value was obtained
docs.text:
The method is the field that keeps a measurement distinguishable from a guess. It is never inferred; the author states it.

measured Obtained from a measurement this project can re-run. Cites the data it came from. vendor_spec Taken from a vendor's own figure: here, the values NVIDIA ships in AISimulate's system descriptors and its memory model. NVIDIA observed or tuned them; this project did not. Requires a source. assumed An estimate arrived at by reasoning, where no dataset this project reads measures the quantity. Requires a rationale; by this registry's convention it also names the measurement that would replace the value. A careful estimate is still assumed. not_charged A deliberate zero, so that "this costs nothing" is distinguishable from "this cost is unknown". A value of zero under any other method is rejected.

The schema also defines literature (a published result not reproduced here), transferred (measured elsewhere and moved here by a stated rule: transferred_from names the scope it was measured in and transfer_rule states the rule), roofline (computed from catalog facts alone, which it cites as sources) and calibrated (back-solved through the cost model from end-to-end measured cases, which it cites as measured_case sources, with the held-out metrics in validated). Ranked from most to least trusted the methods are measured, calibrated, transferred, literature, vendor_spec, roofline, assumed (design §9.2); not_charged is outside the ranking. One committed entry is transferred (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's host_launch_eager_per_kernel on the parts other than h200); no committed entry is calibrated or roofline.

fitted is separate from method because the two answer different questions. A vendor_spec value is never fitted. A measured value may be fitted (the GEMM ramp) or not (an order statistic of measured ratios, like the MoE routing imbalance). The schema allows fitted: true only with method: measured or calibrated.

docs.title: Scope: where the value holds
docs.text:
A scope lists the deployments an entry applies to, along five dimensions: hardware, model, tp, ep and nodes_spanned. Every committed entry is scoped by hardware alone, using the catalog's chip names.

Three rules govern it:

  • A stated dimension restricts; an unstated one does not. An entry scoped to hardware: [h200] applies to every model and parallelism on an H200, and to nothing else.
  • An empty scope is an error, not a wildcard. A coefficient whose applicability is not stated cannot be applied safely, so the schema refuses it.
  • An entry's identity is its name and its scope. One set may hold gemm_eps_max_bf16 for h100 and again for h200; the kernel picks by scope. Two entries with the same name and the same scope are rejected, because only one could be used.

Some quantities vary along dimensions that are not scope keys, such as data type, collective operation and rank count. Those ride in the name: collective_floor_all_reduce_fp16_8rank_h200. The collective names also carry the part, because the kernel constructs those keys from the chip name.

docs.title: Sets
docs.text:
A coefficient set is one YAML file under coefficients/, naming itself (name: cost-model-attention) and listing its entries. Sets are standalone: no file extends another, and a scenario that wants several lists them all. If two listed sets hold the same name for the same part, the one listed later is used.

How entries are grouped into sets follows the evidence as much as the primitive. The seven host overheads are all assumed and are kept in their own set so that no reader takes the provenance of a mostly measured set to be uniform. The memory-occupancy magnitudes are kept apart from the primitives because they rest on a different source.

Most sets are written by a script, not by hand. Their headers say so, and the committed file is whatever the script prints; Contributing a change explains why that matters.

Next: where the numbers come from.

docs.title: Where the numbers come from
docs.text:
The registry draws on public data only, and gives each dataset one job. Keeping the jobs separate is what lets an accuracy figure mean something: a dataset used to fit a number cannot also be the evidence that the number is right.

Dataset What it measures Its job here NVIDIA AISimulate operator sweeps One kernel at a time (a GEMM, an attention call, a collective) across many shapes, per GPU and per serving engine Fitting. Every measured entry comes from these sweeps. AISimulate system descriptors and memory model NVIDIA's own per-part corrections and capacity figures Transcription. The source of every vendor_spec entry. AISimulate FPM One whole forward pass at a known batch and KV composition Validation and model selection. It may fit only a term that is itself about the whole pass. SemiAnalysis InferenceX End-to-end serving runs, with a scheduler and a client Evaluation only. Never used to fit or select anything. vLLM start-up logs in vLLM's issue tracker CUDA-graph capture memory on real deployments Anchoring the magnitude of four assumed memory entries.

docs.title: Why a sweep can fit a constant and a forward pass cannot
docs.text: An operator sweep varies one primitive with everything else held fixed, so it identifies that primitive's two or three constants and nothing else. A whole-forward measurement is one number per batch: the sum over every layer and every resource. Many assignments of constants produce the same sum, so fitting a per-primitive constant to it would attribute to that constant whatever every other term gets wrong. This is a fact about identifiability, not a policy, and it does not change as the dataset grows.

docs.title: Fit the engine you predict
docs.text:
AISimulate measures the same operator under several serving engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) and collective libraries (NCCL). BLIS predicts vLLM. Where the engines run different kernels, the measurements differ, sometimes in sign between GPU generations, so an entry is fitted on the lane that matches what vLLM executes. Where vLLM delegates to NCCL, as it does for every collective except all-reduce, the NCCL lane is vLLM's path. Where the engines share kernels, the lanes agree and the choice is made on data volume.

The rule is applied per operator, and the decisions are recorded with their evidence in the methodology. The current state, computed from each entry's primary citation when this page was built:

primary sourceentriesmeasuredtransferredliteraturevendor_specassumednot_charged AISimulate sweep, nccl lane582 (46.9%)582————— AISimulate sweep, vllm lane305 (24.6%)27718——10— derived from other registry entries210 (16.9%)————210— AISimulate system descriptor46 (3.7%)———424— other (model)32 (2.6%)264——2— other (discussion)28 (2.3%)31——222 AISimulate sweep, trtllm lane12 (1.0%)12————— AISimulate source code9 (0.7%)———9—— other (vendor_doc)8 (0.6%)————8— vLLM start-up logs4 (0.3%)————4— no source cited2 (0.2%)————2— other (publication)2 (0.2%)——1—1— AISimulate sweep, sglang lane1 (0.1%)1—————

docs.title: A better fit can be a worse model
docs.text: The kernel's accuracy rests partly on errors that cancel. A correction that improves one primitive's fit can make the end-to-end estimate worse, because it removes an error that was offsetting another. This has happened six times in this project. So no per-primitive fit is committed without an end-to-end check, and a correction whose offsetting term has not been identified waits.

docs.title: Gaps are declared, not filled
docs.text: Where no dataset measures a quantity, the entry says so: it is assumed, its rationale states the reasoning, and it names the measurement that would replace it. The host overheads are the clearest case. No public dataset times an engine's Python path on the parts these entries price, so all seven are assumed, and each entry describes the experiment that would measure it. (FPM's GLM-5.3-Flash vLLM leaves on GB300 time the scheduler's per-request cost indirectly; they are held-out evidence, not a fit, see the methodology §10.7.)

docs.title: Every measured number can be re-derived
docs.text:
Each generated set is written by a script that its header names, and the scripts are pure functions of their input data: given the same AISimulate collection, they print the same file. The registry's derivation tests re-run them and compare the output with what is committed, so a value edited by hand, or a citation that no longer reproduces its value, fails.

Those tests need a local clone of AISimulate. CI does not fetch one, so on a pull request they skip and say why; the schema gate and the property tests run on every pull request regardless. Validation lists what runs where, and Reproducing the coefficients is the step-by-step guide.

For the full argument behind each rule, with the measurements and the retractions, read the methodology.

docs.title: Contributing a change
docs.text: Most changes to the registry change numbers that every estimate using the affected sets will read. The process below exists so that each such change is visible, reproducible and checked at the level the numbers are used at.

docs.title: Rules that apply to every change
docs.text:
Never edit a generated value by hand. Most sets are written by a script, and the header of each file says which. Change the script or its input, re-run it, and commit what it prints. A hand edit is indistinguishable from a typo, and the derivation tests will reject it when they run against the data.

A value and its citation move together. An entry's sources must name the exact collection the value was fitted on. Changing one without the other is how a registry comes to describe a fit nobody ran.

One collection per part, per family. Fit on a single engine release. Mixing collections changes the row set silently and makes a difference between two parts reflect software rather than silicon.

Fitting data never includes evaluation data. A fitter must not read InferenceX or SemiAnalysis results; scripts/select_overlap_band.py holds the guard to import.

No per-primitive fit ships without an end-to-end check. A better fit to one primitive has, six times in this project, made the overall estimate worse. Run the accuracy dashboard's scoring harness on the change (see methodology §6.1) and report the before and after figures in the pull request.

A coefficient with no reader is not live. Before adding a family, confirm that the cost model looks the key up. Search kernel/ for the name, not registry/.

docs.title: The usual workflow
docs.text:
1. Set up the data. Clone AISimulate and export its path. The fitters read the repository's own catalog/ unless BLIS_CATALOG names another directory; scripts/rederive.sh requires BLIS_CATALOG to be set. From registry/:

    git clone https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aisimulate
export AISIMULATE_DATA=$PWD/aisimulate/python/aisimulate/src/aisimulate_core/systems/data
export BLIS_CATALOG=$PWD/../catalog
pip install --require-hashes -r scripts/requirements-fit.txt

    scripts/requirements.txt covers the property tests. scripts/requirements-fit.txt adds what the fitters need to read the Parquet sweeps: pyarrow, pandas and numpy.

  2. Run the family's writer. The writer table names the script that owns each family. Each takes --check, which exits non-zero if the committed file would change, and most take --insert CHIP to add a part.

  3. Run the derivation tests with the data present. The rederive workflow runs them on every pull request that touches a coefficient, a writer or a test (~20 minutes); run them locally first. With COLLECTIVEX_DATA also set to the CollectiveX run bodies (python -I scripts/fetch_cited_inferencex.py <dir> fetches and checks them):

    scripts/rederive.sh

    It runs python -m pytest validator/ -q -rs and fails on any skip other than the by-design ramp-form ones and the tests on .github/quarantine.yaml, because a skip with the data present is a test that did not run.

  4. Run the schema validator. CI runs it on every pull request; running it first saves a round trip. From the repository root:

    go run ./validate/cmd/validate-registry registry

  5. Score the change end to end, as above, if it changes a value a step time depends on.

  6. Preview the documentation. The reference pages are generated from registry/coefficients/, so they show your change. From the repository root:

    pip install --require-hashes -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

  7. Open a pull request. CI's registry job runs the schema validator and the validator tests, and its docs build job builds the site. The required check passes only if every job that ran passed.

docs.title: Adding a part
docs.text:
A part must exist in the catalog before the registry can scope an entry to it, because scope.hardware uses catalog chip names. The order of the writers matters in one place (prefill attention reads the GEMM ramp from the registry), so follow the GB300 worked example.

The host-overhead and memory sets list every catalog part in their scope, and a property test checks that they do. Adding a part is therefore also a visible edit to those sets, which is intended: it is the reminder that their values were never measured on the new part.

docs.title: Adding a set
docs.text: Add the file under registry/coefficients/, then add a reference page for it at docs/registry/reference/sets/<name>.md and list that page in the nav of mkdocs.yml. The documentation build fails until both exist, so a set cannot be committed without a page. Copy an existing page; the table on it is generated, so the page needs only a short description of what the set prices and where its values come from.

docs.title: Writing documentation
docs.text: The pages under docs/registry/ are Markdown, built with Material for MkDocs. A number that describes the registry's contents (a count, a value, a census) must not be typed into a page. Use a registry: directive instead, which the build computes from the committed files; docs/hooks/registry.py lists them. A retyped count is correct on the day it is written and wrong after the next refit.

docs.title: Changes beyond the registry
docs.text: A change that also touches contracts/, catalog/ or kernel/ is one pull request in blis-substrate. A change that also needs another BLIS repository, such as inference-sim, follows Changes across repositories.

docs.title: Coefficient sets
docs.text: Everything on the pages in this section is generated from the committed files when the site is built, at revision 965b05834c47. Nothing is typed in by hand, so a count here cannot disagree with the data.

docs.title: The sets
docs.text:
setentriescoefficientsmeasuredtransferredliteraturevendor_specassumednot_chargedparts cost-model-attention106277416——16—9 cost-model-collectives-inferencex161216—————3 cost-model-collectives888108684———204—9 cost-model-fabric44——1—3—4 cost-model-host-overheads1211—1——1019 cost-model-memory17173——9419 cost-model-offload-tiers2418—4——20—9 cost-model-primitives13826882—426—9 cost-model-recurrent36636—————6 all sets1,24122990123151263213

Entries counts every (name, scope) pair. Coefficients counts distinct quantities, after folding the part out of names that carry it, such as collective_floor_all_reduce_fp16_8rank_h200. Parts is the number of GPU parts with at least one entry.

The speculative acceptance-profile sets under acceptance/ are not coefficient sets and are not counted here; they have their own page.

docs.title: What each set rests on

docs.title: Which sets the kernel reads
docs.text:
A scenario names the sets it loads. Step time reads the five cost-model-* sets the cost model's scenario fixtures list, and memory occupancy reads cost-model-memory. Within them, a few families are committed but not looked up by the cost model in kernel/ at this revision:

Set Not read Why cost-model-primitives every gemm_*_fp8_block entry the kernel's dtype selection resolves an FP8 GEMM to fp8, never to a block-scaled ramp (blis-latency-kernel#34) cost-model-primitives gemm_*_w4a16_mxfp4_grouped on b200, b300 and gb300 the weight-only Marlin ramps are read only on a part with no native four-bit peak (h100, h200); a part with one is priced on its FP4 class, as stock vLLM v0.31.0 runs it cost-model-attention attention_decode_{launch_floor,split_floor,serial_rate,per_token,throughput_rate}_sparse_mla the two-branch FlashMLA decode form of methodology §10.7 has no reader; the kernel prices sparse-MLA decode with attention_decode_rate_sparse_mla

attention_decode_rate_sparse_mla IS read, for the one model it is scoped to; that model is not yet priceable end to end (methodology §10.5).

Three families that had no reader were removed rather than listed here: hbm_constant_latency, p2p_latency and moe_routing_imbalance_p90 (methodology §1).

An unread entry still passes every check, so this table is the place to look before assuming a change to one will move an estimate.

docs.title: Reading a set page
docs.text:
Each set page shows the set as a matrix: one row per coefficient, one column per part. A glyph before each value gives its method, and its shape alone identifies it:

Glyph Method ■ measured ◆ vendor_spec ○ assumed – not_charged

Every value is a link to its entry in the file, where the sources, rationale and scope are recorded. A dot (·) marks a part the set has no entry for. Whether that is an omission or a deliberate absence is stated in the set's header and on its page.

docs.title: Acceptance profiles
docs.text:
How far speculative decoding advances a request per verification step, by model, speculative method, K and thinking mode. Generated at build time from acceptance/, at revision [`965b05834c47`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-substrate/tree/965b05834c47882bc0f9f1a960c90327a756ef3d); nothing below is typed in by hand.

An acceptance-profile set is the acceptance counterpart of a coefficient set. Its format, and how a run resolves one value from it, are on the contracts' acceptance reference (blis-schemas#65). Each profile holds the mean acceptance length (AL): the tokens a request gains per verification step, counting the target's bonus token, so it lies in [1, K + 1]. No per-position rates are stored. A consumer that needs them derives vLLM v0.31.0's minimum-variance schedule, which is how the InferenceX runs that force a published AL realise it.

docs.text:
SemiAnalysis InferenceX's golden SPEED-Bench curves, the values its AgentX runs force through vLLM's synthetic_acceptance_length. A cell links to its profile in the file. A dot (·) is a K with no profile, and a lookup for it is refused rather than interpolated.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
The set's own caveats, as committed:

  • Coding only. Every profile is SPEED-Bench's coding category, the only one InferenceX publishes; no other category has a value. A consumer must refuse other traffic, or fall back to coding with the substitution recorded; it must not substitute silently.
  • Measured on b300: deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-pro-0813, glm-5.2-fp8, glm-5.3, minimax-m3. Acceptance depends mostly on the model, drafter and workload rather than the chip; a resolution on another part records the reuse.
  • Measured on b200: deepseek-v4.1-flash. Acceptance depends mostly on the model, drafter and workload rather than the chip; a resolution on another part records the reuse.
  • deepseek-v4.1-flash dspark: the source file names no hardware. b200 is the part run 34493175056 ran on: its collect-al job 102924945774 ran on runner b200-nscale-slurm_00 (label cluster:b200-nscale) and launched runners/launch_b200-nscale-compat.sh with BENCH_BASE benchmarks/single_node/dsv41flash_fp4_b200.
  • deepseek-v4.1-flash with dspark at K 6-8 was rejected by the image vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909 (https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34494319147), so those K have no value.
  • glm-5.3 mtp (K 3) is provisional: copied from glm5.2_mtp.yaml, not measured on glm-5.3.
  • Deployment precision. The fp4 in the collectors' names is the label speedbench-al.yml gives every collection (PRECISION fp4, and the _fp4_b300_vllm.sh name it requires), not the precision served. Each collector serves its model's checkpoint at that checkpoint's own weight precision, which is the catalog model's. At InferenceX 9fa76586ed1e: dsv4_fp4_b300_vllm.sh (deepseek-v4-pro) serves the staged checkpoint with no quantization flag, and --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (line 123); dsv4dspark_fp4_b300_vllm.sh (deepseek-v4-pro-0813) serves the staged checkpoint with no quantization flag, and --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (line 169); glm52_fp4_b300_vllm.sh (glm-5.2-fp8) serves the staged checkpoint with no quantization flag, and --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (line 131); minimaxm3_fp4_b300_vllm.sh (minimax-m3) serves the staged checkpoint, which its comment (lines 16-19) states is unquantized BF16, with no --kv-cache-dtype. kv_cache_dtype is recorded where a collector sets it; a collector may have changed since its run.
  • The source files for deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-pro-0813, glm-5.2-fp8, minimax-m3 name no engine image, so their engine_image reads "unrecorded: the source file names no engine image".
  • minimax-m3 eagle3: the curve is for the base EAGLE3 drafter. InferenceX's MiniMax-M3 runs serve EAGLE3 through a separate draft_model, which the catalog graph does not describe (the catalog lists no such drafter), and its minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa curve is for a second one. The catalog lists no such drafter yet, so a profile cannot name one (its drafter must be a catalog model) and these profiles name none. Until it does, a run that uses the model's own speculator would borrow them as another drafter's.
  • Not carried: kimik3_dspark.yaml (kimi-k3), because the two Kimi-K3 DSpark curves differ only in the draft sampler (greedy, and probabilistic with block rejection), which a profile's key cannot state, and InferenceX's own resolver (curves.py curve_name) refuses to pick one without it.
  • Not carried: kimik3_dspark_probabilistic_sample_method_block_rejection_sample_method.yaml (kimi-k3), because the two Kimi-K3 DSpark curves differ only in the draft sampler (greedy, and probabilistic with block rejection), which a profile's key cannot state, and InferenceX's own resolver (curves.py curve_name) refuses to pick one without it.
  • Not carried: minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml (minimax-m3), because it is the curve for the Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA drafter and shares minimaxm3_eagle3's key, since a profile's key cannot state the drafter; InferenceX's resolver uses it only for a GQA drafter, and the base curve otherwise.
  • Not carried: qwen3.5_mtp.yaml (qwen3.5-397b-a17b-nvfp4), because its model qwen3.5-397b-a17b-nvfp4 is no catalog model's repository, and no alias maps it.
  • Not carried: qwen3.8next_mtp.yaml (qwen3.8-flash-next-fp8), because its model qwen3.8-flash-next-fp8 is no catalog model's repository, and no alias maps it.

docs.title: How the set is made
docs.text: scripts/emit_acceptance_profiles.py writes the file, and its --check is the drift gate, as for the coefficient writers. The rules it follows are in methodology §12.

docs.title: File format
docs.text: A coefficient set is a YAML file under coefficients/. The rules on this page are enforced by the contracts, in contracts/spec/coefficient and contracts/vocab, at the same commit as the data; validate-registry also validates acceptance/ and routing/. Where this page and the schema disagree, the schema is right.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text:
kind: CoefficientSet          # exactly this
name: cost-model-primitives   # the set's identity; scenarios refer to it by this name
coefficients:                 # a list; each item is a map with one key, the coefficient's name
  - <name>:
      <fields>

One entry from the committed sets, quoted from its file:

registry/coefficients/cost-model-primitives.yaml, line 627
- gemm_eps_max_bf16:
    value: 1.0
    units: dimensionless
    method: measured
    fitted: true
    scope: {hardware: [h100]}
    sources:
      - {kind: model, cite: "NVIDIA AISimulate systems/data/h100_sxm/gemm/vllm/0.25.0/gemm_perf.parquet (NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3), 37,518 bfloat16 rows over 74 token counts, kernel torch.nn.functional.linear", role: primary}
    rationale: >
      The fraction of this part's bfloat16 peak a large, well-shaped matmul asymptotically reaches, on vLLM's own linear kernel rather than the generic `torch_flow` path the TRT-LLM sweep measures. Envelope rather than mean: a cost model predicts what a well-shaped GEMM achieves. Least-squares residual 0.0629 over 74 token counts.

Quoted from the committed file at build time.

Unknown keys are errors at every level: top level, entry, scope and source. A misspelled field is rejected, not ignored.

docs.title: Entry fields
docs.text:
Field Type Required Rule value number yes Finite. Zero only with method: not_charged. units term yes One of the units below. method term yes One of the methods below. fitted bool yes Must be present, even when false. true requires method: measured or calibrated. scope map yes At least one dimension. sources list by method If present, non-empty. Required for literature and vendor_spec; calibrated requires at least one of kind measured_case. rationale string by method Required for every method except measured. ci95 [low, high] no Finite, low ≤ high, and the value must lie inside. transferred_from string for transferred The scope the value was measured in. transfer_rule string for transferred The stated rule that moved the value. supersedes string no The entry this one replaces. validated metric or list for calibrated Metrics the value has been checked against. unsupported metric or list no Metrics it has explicitly not been checked against.

Within one set, no two entries may share both a name and a scope. Scope comparison ignores the order of values, so [h100, h200] and [h200, h100] are the same scope.

The registry's own tests add two requirements the schema leaves out: every measured entry cites a source, and every assumed entry carries a substantial rationale.

  • role: primary, supporting, upper_bound

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
Names are snake_case. A name states the quantity, then the axes that vary it and are not scope keys, in a fixed order per family:

  • gemm_eps_max_<dtype>
  • attention_decode_floor_<kind>, with no suffix for full attention
  • collective_<param>_<op>_<dtype>_<N>rank_<chip>, where <chip> is the catalog name with - replaced by _
  • nccl_communicator_bytes_<N>rank, cudagraph_capture_bytes_<mode>

The kernel constructs these names when it looks a value up, so a name is an interface. Renaming one is a change to the kernel too.

docs.title: Typical error of each method
docs.text:
Design 9.3 and VAL-5: each method's typical error is measured by leaving one chip out. For every chip that has a measured value, the method estimates it as if the measurement did not exist, and the estimate is compared with the measurement. The two parts of the A100 family carry the same measured values, so they are left out together; otherwise each would predict itself from its twin.

The figures below cover 911 measured points of the committed coefficient registry. A ratio is max(estimate/truth, truth/estimate): 1.00 is exact and 2.00 is a factor of two either way.

  • Same generation is the median of the same quantity on the other chips of the held-out chip's architecture generation, and gives no estimate for a chip with no sibling. It is the predictor extrapolate_by_generation.py writes.
  • Global median is the median over every other chip. It is the baseline a method must beat.

A family with fewer than 10 held-out points is merged into other, and other is left out if it too has fewer. What this does not yet measure: the roofline (rank 6) and vendor-specification (rank 5) methods. Each estimates a value from a datasheet figure, so measuring its error needs an estimator that reads the chip's datasheet; the two above read only other chips' measurements. Until such an estimator is written, the page states no error for those methods and says so rather than reusing the figures above for them. The whole-run error is the dashboard's.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Three kinds of check guard the registry. They answer different questions, and passing one says nothing about the others.

Check Question it answers Where it runs Schema Could a consumer load this file? CI, every pull request and every push to main Properties Is every value physically sensible, and is its provenance complete? CI, every pull request and every push to main Re-derivation Does every value still come out of its fitter, from its cited data? The rederive workflow: every pull request that changes registry/coefficients, registry/scripts, registry/validator or .github/quarantine.yaml, nightly, and by hand; locally, with an AISimulate clone; skipped in CI's registry job

If a merge queue is enabled (none is today), the rederive workflow also runs on every queue entry, because GitHub applies no path filter to a merge group. Its cheap rederive changes job runs every time and compares the entry with the workflow's own paths; the roughly 20-minute rederive job runs only when one of those paths changed. The required job of ci.yml then requires a successful run of the workflow at the merge-queue commit, which is the tree being merged. The same holds for the ledger candidate workflow.

The documentation build is a fourth, narrower check: it fails if a set has no reference page, or if a set holds data the reference tables cannot represent faithfully.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
CI's registry job runs the repository's validator over every file under coefficients/, acceptance/ and routing/. From the repository root:

go run ./validate/cmd/validate-registry registry

It applies exactly the rules a consumer applies when it loads a set: strict decoding, then field validation, through the Go types in contracts/spec/coefficient. The rules are listed on File format. The registry keeps no schema validator of its own, so there is one definition of a valid file, and it is the one the cost model uses. The validator and the data are in the same commit, so a change to either is checked against the other.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
validator/test_coefficient_properties.py reads only the committed files and the repository's own catalog/ chip descriptors, so it always runs. Each test encodes a defect that this project has shipped at least once:

  • no bandwidth rate exceeds its part's datasheet peak, and every rate is a plausible fraction of it;
  • GEMM asymptotes are fractions; MoE imbalance is near one, and its 90th percentile is not below its median;
  • collective floors do not fall as the group widens, rates do not rise steeply, and no transition rate exceeds its peak rate;
  • recurrent floors are positive and bounded, and rates are slower than the convolution alone;
  • a kind-specific attention floor is not a module measurement in disguise;
  • the hardware-independent sets cover every catalog part;
  • every measured entry cites a source, and every assumed entry explains itself;
  • the memory set has a capture entry for every vLLM CUDA-graph mode, respects the capture-pool overlay, and its activation multiples fall with width; and the capture sizes re-derive from the committed log samples.

docs.title: Re-derivation
docs.text:
validator/test_generated_from_aisimulate.py and validator/test_writers_are_idempotent.py re-run the fitters and compare with the committed files. They need the AISimulate sweeps, which are not vendored here, and they skip when the data is absent, saying so. CI has no copy, so in CI they always skip.

Run them before any pull request that changes a fitted value, and before a release:

Run from registry/:

export AISIMULATE_DATA=/path/to/aisimulate/python/aisimulate/src/aisimulate_core/systems/data
export BLIS_CATALOG=$PWD/../catalog   # run from registry/; the repository's catalog
python -I scripts/fetch_cited_inferencex.py /tmp/collectivex   # sha256-pinned
export COLLECTIVEX_DATA=/tmp/collectivex
scripts/rederive.sh

scripts/rederive.sh is also what the rederive workflow runs. A skip fails it unless the test is a by-design ramp-form skip or is on .github/quarantine.yaml, with an owning issue and an expiry (X16, X25).

They check that:

  • each writer reproduces its committed file byte for byte (--check), and every fitted family has a writer;
  • the generated GEMM and collective values survive an independent re-derivation by a second code path;
  • the all-reduce entries come from the vLLM CUDA-graph lane specifically, since the eager lane is slower than NCCL and accepting it would misprice all-reduce by 3.4×;
  • in the primitive and collective sets, every source is NVIDIA's, and no assumed entry carries a foreign measurement in through its rationale.

A test that cannot run says why. Treat an unexpected skip as a test that did not run.

docs.title: The end-to-end check
docs.text: None of the above can tell whether a change makes BLIS more accurate. That needs the accuracy dashboard's scoring harness, the one end-to-end scorer, described in methodology §6.1.

docs.title: cost-model-attention
docs.text:
The constants for attention, by phase and by kind.

Decode is priced as a fixed setup cost plus a read of the KV cache:

latency = attention_decode_floor + KV bytes / attention_decode_rate

The floor is why a pure-bandwidth model is wrong at short context: an attention kernel costs on the order of 10 µs whatever the context. The rate is the bandwidth the kernel actually reaches, which on these parts is well short of the datasheet figure and varies too much between parts for one derate to serve.

Three kinds of attention carry their own pair, because each reads a different number of bytes:

Suffix Kind Read per step, per request none full attention (GQA) K and V for every cached token _swa sliding window K and V for at most the window's tokens _mla multi-head latent attention one compressed latent vector per cached token

The _mla floors are assumed: they are set from the part's own measured full-attention floor, because the tables they were first fitted on measured the whole MLA block, projections included, and the kernel prices those projections separately. Methodology §3 records how that was found. Sparse MLA has no pair of its own; §10 explains why none is fittable from this data.

Prefill is priced from the GEMM efficiency ramp, scaled by attention_prefill_work_scale, above a floor attention_prefill_floor. The scale is a fraction of the bf16 ramp in cost-model-primitives, so refitting that ramp means refitting this.

Prefill on the trtllm-gen kernel. The prefill pair of b200, b300, gb200-nvl72 and gb300 is fitted on every full-attention row of the vLLM 0.25.0 context sweep, and that sweep holds three kernels: 24,720 rows of FlashInfer's trtllm-gen prefill, 2,038 one-token batches vLLM classed as decodes, and 816 Triton rows. FlashInfer's prefill runs the first one when attention_config.use_trtllm_attention is true, when a stated block size is 128 or more, and, unset, when the cache dtype is auto. The pair refitted on those rows alone, once for each of the sweep's two cache dtypes (they differ: on b200 the floor is 18.5 us at bf16 and 21.0 at fp8, against 20.0 pooled over both), is attention_prefill_floor_trtllm_gen_kv_{bf16,fp8} and attention_prefill_work_scale_trtllm_gen_kv_{bf16,fp8}. The kernel reads them for the non-latent layers when the engine reports that kernel as the implementation of the prefill primitive and an entry lists it (VAL-8), and not otherwise. They are transferred, not measured: no kernel hash shows the 0.25.0 build runs the kernel of the v0.32.0 pin, and a measured entry needs one (D5, VAL-8; the hashes are tracked in inference-sim/blis-registry#73). So a lane price grades one rank lower than the pooled measured pair fitted on the same sweep; that is the label's cost, not the data's. Each entry records the range its rows covered, and every row has no cached prefix, so a prefill with cached context is outside the data. The lane replaces the pooled pair for every non-latent kind, sliding-window and sparse layers included, as the pooled pair did. Decode has no lane, because v0.32.0 decodes with trtllm-gen or XQA wherever the chip supports it.

docs.title: cost-model-collectives-inferencex
docs.text:
DeepEP dispatch plus combine, priced as one MoE layer's all-to-all:

latency = floor + tokens · hidden · 2 · top_k / rate

with per-rank tokens. Two variants are here, both as InferenceX CollectiveX times them:

  • deepep_low_latency_graph: DeepEP's legacy low-latency kernels under CUDA-graph replay, which vLLM v0.31.0 uses for a captured decode step. The eager pair (moe_a2a_*_deepep_low_latency_<N>rank_<part> in cost-model-collectives) prices a step with no graph.
  • deepep_v2_graph: DeepEP v2's ElasticBuffer with vLLM deepep_v2's CUDA-graphs-on flags (no CPU sync, no expand). CollectiveX replays decode as a graph and runs prefill eager on the same path.

Where the values come from. InferenceX CollectiveX, backend deepep-v2, bf16, shape hidden 7168, top-6 of 384, uniform routing, the roundtrip p50 per tokens-per-rank point. The h100 and h200 8-rank pair (one node, NVLink) fits tokens 1/4/16/64/256 and holds out 2/8/32/128. GB200-NVL72 at 8 and 16 ranks (2 and 4 trays of one MNNVL rack) and H200 at 16 ranks (two nodes over 400G InfiniBand, scoped fabric: [ib-400g]) use the same split for the low-latency mode. The v2 mode adds the prefill ladder: it fits 1/4/16/64/256/1024/4096 and holds out 2/8/32/128/512/2048/8192. Each entry states its run, its body's sha256 and its held-out error. The H200 16-rank entries measure a virtualised pool's path, not the InfiniBand fabric, and say so.

Why a separate set. cost-model-collectives comes from a single source, NVIDIA AISimulate. A set that mixed the two methodologies would confound comparisons across parts. A scenario lists this set next to cost-model-collectives to take these prices. Without it, the kernel prices as before.

docs.title: cost-model-collectives
docs.text:
The constants for the four collectives the kernel prices: all-gather, all-reduce, all-to-all and reduce-scatter. Each configuration (operation, dtype, rank count, part) has three:

latency = max(floor + size / transition_rate, size / peak_rate)

The floor is the latency of a small message, where size no longer matters. The peak rate is the bandwidth a large message reaches. The transition rate governs the region in between, roughly 64 KiB to 8 MiB, where a two-parameter model is optimistic and where a prefill batch's collectives fall.

Operation, dtype and rank count are not scope keys, so they are part of the name, and so is the part, because the kernel builds the key from the chip name: collective_floor_all_reduce_fp16_8rank_h200. The tables below fold the part into the columns.

Where the values come from. All-reduce at fp16 is measured on vLLM's own custom all-reduce kernel on most parts; the other operations, and the int8 all-reduce, are measured on NCCL, which is what vLLM runs for them. The source table on Where the numbers come from gives the current split. Rank widths a part was never swept at are assumed, extrapolated from that part's own measured widths with a holdout-validated linear model, and each such entry states its predictor and holdout error. Methodology §8.5 gives the argument, including the model that was tried first and refuted.

The set also holds the MoE all-to-all that DeepEP dispatch plus combine costs, as floor + bytes / rate per backend, rank count and part (moe_a2a_floor_deepep_low_latency_8rank_h100). All of them come from AISimulate. The low-latency pair measured by CollectiveX under CUDA-graph replay is in cost-model-collectives-inferencex.

docs.title: cost-model-fabric
docs.text:
The effective / nominal bandwidth of each inter-node fabric class the catalog defines under networks/. A fabric's catalog figure, InterNodeBwGBps, is its line rate divided by eight, per GPU, per direction. A transfer over it achieves less. The cost model multiplies the nominal rate by fabric_bandwidth_efficiency wherever bytes leave a node: a P/D handoff, a pipeline-stage boundary, and the cross-node share of a collective. It refuses a value outside (0, 1].

Each entry is scoped by the fabric's catalog identity (scope: {fabric: [ib-400g]}), not by hardware. A rack-wide NVLink domain (gb200-nvl72) belongs to the chip, so it is not corrected here.

Where the values come from. None is a measurement this project made.

  • ib-400g is literature: published nccl-tests all_reduce results on H100 hosts with eight ConnectX-7 400G InfiniBand NICs each (NVIDIA/nccl-tests#309), as a fraction of the 400 GB/s ceiling an NVIDIA maintainer states there.
  • ib-800g is assumed, equal to ib-400g: no public multi-node measurement of ConnectX-8 (InfiniBand XDR, 800 Gb/s per GPU) was found. Only its line rate is cited, from NVIDIA's Blackwell Ultra Datasheet. A handoff over ib-800g therefore takes half the time of the same handoff over ib-400g; a measured 800G efficiency would change that.
  • roce-200g and ethernet-100gbe are assumed. No public multi-node measurement of either was found. Each rationale states the range the value could lie in and the one public datum that bounds it.

docs.title: cost-model-host-overheads
docs.text:
CPU time spent by the engine around the GPU work: tokenizing a prompt, launching kernels or replaying a captured CUDA graph, detokenizing each output token, and tearing down a finished request.

Every entry is assumed. No public dataset measures an engine's host path: AISimulate times kernels, FPM times one synchronized forward pass, and InferenceX is used for evaluation only. The values rest on reasoning and, for three of them, on the order of magnitude of an earlier BLIS fit against a different functional form. Each entry's rationale states its reasoning and the measurement that would replace it.

The set is kept separate from the measured sets so that its provenance is not mistaken for theirs. Its scope lists every catalog part because the work is CPU-side and has no per-part value; listing them makes adding a part a visible edit here.

Assumed is not the same as unimportant. The largest single accuracy movement recorded in this project, measured-tier TTFT error from 52.94% to 31.47%, came from one of these seven (methodology §6.0).

docs.title: cost-model-memory
docs.text:
The per-rank memory a deployment holds besides weights and KV cache. These numbers set how many sequences fit, not how long a step takes.

The terms add, per rank:

weights + activation + nccl_communicator_bytes_<N>rank + engine_workspace_bytes + cudagraph_capture_bytes_<mode>

with

activation = max(activation_buffer_count_<family>_<N>rank · max_num_batched_tokens · h · 2, activation_scratch_floor_bytes)

where family is dense or moe, N is min(tp, 8), and h is the attention width. The communicator and workspace terms are in cost-model-primitives, because NVIDIA's descriptors state them per part.

Two provenances. The activation multiples and floor are vendor_spec: NVIDIA's own memory model, as AISimulate's vLLM backend uses it. The CUDA-graph capture sizes are assumed: their magnitude is the median of vLLM's own start-up logs, collected from vLLM's issue tracker into a committed CSV (vllm-cudagraph-capture-samples.csv). FULL and FULL_DECODE_ONLY have too few samples and are charged the FULL_AND_PIECEWISE figure as an upper bound. NONE is a declared zero.

The cost model reads every term of this set and refuses a scenario that does not list it (blis-latency-kernel#22). Methodology §11 gives the composition and each scoping decision.
